"כִּי אֲשֶׁר רְאִיתֶם אֶת מִצְרַיִם הַיּוֹם לֹא [תוֹסִיפוּ לִרְאֹתָם עוֹד עַד עוֹלָם]",
"'For as you have seen the Egyptians today, you shall see them no more forever, etc.,'"
דְּיוֹם הַהוּא עֲדַיִן רְאוּם,
for on that very day they still saw them,
וְהָרְאִיָּה אֵינוֹ מִקְרֶה וְסִפּוּר מַעֲשֶׂה,
and this seeing was neither incidental nor a casual chronicle of event,
רַק עֲדַיִן הָיָה לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִרְאוֹתָם
rather they still harbored a residual connection enabling them to see them,
שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִזְדַּכְּכוּ לְגַמְרֵי
because they were not yet completely purified
לְהַשִּׂיג רְאִיָּה דְּיָם
to apprehend the spiritual vision of the Sea,
עַד רֶגַע קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף
until the very instant of the parting of the Red Sea,
דְּהִבְטִיחָם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "לֹא תוֹסִיפוּ וְגוֹמֵר".
when the Holy One, blessed be He, promised them: 'You shall not see them again, etc.'
זוֹ הַבְטָחָה דְּכָל מִי שֶׁהוּא מִשָּׁרְשָׁא וְגִזְעָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
This is an enduring guarantee that whoever stems from the holy root and lineage of Israel
לֹא יָבוֹא לוֹ הִרְהוּר וּמַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ כְּלָל בְּלִבּוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
shall never have such a doubt or thought arise in his heart, Heaven forbid,
לוֹמַר: "לֹא יִרְאֶה [יָהּ וְלֹא יָבִין] אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב".
to claim: 'God will not see, neither will the God of Jacob understand.'
דְּכָל מִי שֶׁמִּזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב מַאֲמִין שֶׁהוּא רוֹאֶה וּמֵבִין וּמַשְׁגִּיחַ בִּפְרָטוּת,
For everyone from the seed of Jacob believes that He perceives, understands, and supervises in precise individual detail,
וְהוּא אֱמוּנָה הַכְּלָלִית,
and this constitutes the universal faith,
וְזֶהוּ "לֹא תוֹסִיפוּ" לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים.
and this explains 'you shall not continue' (lo tosifu) stated in the plural.
וְאָז רָאוּ אַחַר כָּךְ כָּל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט בַּיָּם,
And then they saw subsequently, each one individually at the Sea;
וּמִזֶּה נִצְמַח אַחַר כָּךְ הַשָּׂגָה דְּכָל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and from this sprouted forth the individualized comprehension of each person at the Giving of the Torah
דְּ"אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
in the phrase 'Who brought you out, etc.,'
כְּפִי הַהוֹצָאָה שֶׁהִשַּׂגְתָּ בִּפְרָט נַפְשְׁךָ,
so that according to the measure of liberation you perceived within your specific soul,
כֵּן תַּשִּׂיג "אָנֹכִי" בִּפְרָט כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
so do you apprehend 'I am' (Anokhi) in particular, as mentioned above.
– וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעֵת קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף "ה' אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה",
[[Therefore Hashem, blessed be He, is titled at the parting of the Red Sea 'Hashem is a man of war,']
דִּכְשָׁפִים מַכְחִישִׁין – הַיְינוּ כְּנִלְחָם שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַכְחִישׁוֹ וּלְבַטְּלוֹ.
[for sorcery which 'denies' operates like a combatant seeking to resist and nullify Him.]
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר: "כְּאִישׁ מִלְחָמוֹת יָעִיר [קִנְאָה] וְגוֹמֵר",
[And so regarding the future it is said: 'Like a man of wars He will stir up jealousy, etc.',]
וְנִקְרָא "כְּאִישׁ" וְלֹא "אִישׁ",
[and He is termed 'like a man' (ke-ish) rather than 'a man',]
כִּי בִּרְכַּת עֵשָׂו "וְעַל חַרְבְּךָ תִחְיֶה" גַּם כֵּן מִלְחָמָה וְנִיצּוּחַ לַנִּבְרָאִים וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל
[since the blessing of Esau 'and by your sword you shall live' likewise involves war and conflict against creatures and Israel,]
וְלֹא לִפְלִיא שֶׁל מַעְלָה.
[and not against the Wonder of the supernal Realm.]
וּלְפִי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רַשִּׁ"י מַטּוֹת ל"א, ג מִסִּפְרֵי שָׁם, וּפָרָשַׁת בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ פִּסְקָא פד):
[And because they taught (Rashi, Matot 31:3 from the Sifrei there; and Parashat Beha'alotekha, section 84):]
"כָּל [הָעוֹמֵד] כְּנֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּאִלּוּ [עוֹמֵד כְּנֶגֶד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא]",
['Whoever stands against Israel is as though he stands against the Holy One, blessed be He,']
לָכֵן נִקְרָא "כְּאִישׁ וְכוּלֵי",
[therefore He is termed 'like a man, etc.',]
הַכָּ״ף הַדִּמְיוֹן הַיְינוּ כִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים: "כְּאִלּוּ"].
[the prefix Kaf denoting comparison, corresponding to the rabbinic idiom 'as though'].

sections.en: Opposing Views within Living Torah

items.h: Torah truth can contain opposite positions because both emerge from the Divine source; mature wisdom grasps the unity underlying apparent contradiction.

Seif 1 — Both Are the Words of the Living God
Opposing Torah positions can both be true because they reflect distinct facets of one divine source.

p: בְּכָל חִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת דָּבָר מְבוֹרָר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נְטִיָּה לְכָאן וּלְכָאן,
In all novel insights of the Torah, it is impossible for a matter to be elucidated without a leaning this way and that,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (חֲגִיגָה ג:):
as it is written (Chagigah 3b):
"הַלָּלוּ מְטַמְּאִין וְכוּלֵי",
"These declare impure, etc.,"
"וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים" (עֵירוּבִין יג:).
"and 'both these and those are the words of the living God' (Eruvin 13b)."
פֵּירוּשׁ, "אֱלֹהִים" – בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם הַנִּפְרָדִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם,
The meaning is: 'Elohim' denotes the Master of all differentiated forces in the world,
וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים,
and this is why it is phrased in the plural;
וְכֵן "חַיִּים" לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים,
and likewise 'Chayyim' (life) is in the plural,
דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא חַיּוּת הַבְּרִיאָה כֻּלָּהּ.
for words of Torah are the vitality of the entire Creation.
וְיֵשׁ חֲלוּקוֹת שֶׁל חַיִּים,
And there are varied allocations of life,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "פַּלְגֵי מַיִם לֶב מֶלֶךְ בְּיַד וְגוֹמֵר",
and concerning this it is stated: 'Like streams of water, the heart of a king is in the hand of [Hashem], etc.'
מַאן מַלְכֵי – רַבָּנָן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גִּיטִּין סב.),
'Who are kings? The Rabbis' (as written in Gittin 62a),
וְאֵין מַיִם אֶלָּא תוֹרָה (בָּבָא קַמָּא יז.),
and 'water' refers specifically to Torah (Bava Kamma 17a),
וְהֵם נִפְלָגִים לְמַעְיָינוֹת שׁוֹנִים לֶאֱסוֹר וּלְהַתִּיר,
and they divide into distinct springs—to prohibit and to permit;
וְכִסְבוּרִים אָנוּ דְּהוּא בְּדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל חָכָם,
and we might assume that this depends merely upon the sage's own reasoning,
וְאֵינוֹ כֵן,
yet it is not so,
אֶלָּא גַּם זֶה בְּיַד ה'
rather this too is in the hand of Hashem,
שֶׁמֵּאִיר עֵינָיו וּמַטֶּה לְבָבוֹ כְּפִי הַחֵפֶץ וְרָצוֹן אֱלֹהִי לְבַד.
Who illuminates his eyes and bends his heart solely according to the divine will and desire.
וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים",
Therefore they are termed 'the words of the living God,'
דְּבֶאֱמֶת הֵן דִּבְרֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for in truth they are the words of Hashem, blessed be He.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב.):
And as they said (Bava Batra 12a):
דּמִן הַחֲכָמִים לֹא נִיטְּלָה נְבוּאָה,
that prophecy was not taken away from the sages,
דְּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּנְבוּאָה;
for it truly derives from Hashem, blessed be He, just like prophecy;
רַק הַחִלּוּק דִּנְבוּאָה הוּא "כֹּה אָמַר ה'",
the only distinction being that prophecy declares 'Thus said Hashem,'
הַיְינוּ כָּזֶה מַמָּשׁ
meaning precisely thus,
וְאֵין בּוֹ הַטָּיָה וְחִלּוּק,
admitting no variance or division,
וּשְׁנֵי נְבִיאִים הַמַּכְחִישִׁים זֶה אֶת זֶה הָאֶחָד נְבִיא שֶׁקֶר.
and if two prophets contradict one another, one is a false prophet.
כִּי "נָבִיא" מִלְּשׁוֹן נִיב כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י בַּחוּמָשׁ,
For navi (prophet) derives from niv (utterance), as Rashi explains in the Chumash,
וְהַיְינוּ דִּבּוּרוֹ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and that denotes the explicit speech of Hashem, blessed be He,
דְּהַדִּבּוּר דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַמָּשׁ בִּגְרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל נָבִיא.
for the actual speech of Hashem resonates in the throat of the prophet.
וְהַדִּבּוּר הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת לַפּוֹעַל,
And speech represents externalized manifestation into actuality,
וּבְהִתְגַּלּוּת אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד כַּיָּדוּעַ,
and in manifest reality two opposites cannot coexist in a single subject, as is known,
דְּשֵׂכֶל בְּנֵי אָדָם מַכְחִישׁ זֶה כַּנּוֹדָע מִדִּבְרֵי רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן.
for human intellect denies this, as known from the teachings of the Rambam.
אֲבָל חָכָם הוּא דָּבוּק בְּחָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
However, a sage clings to the supernal wisdom of Hashem, blessed be He,
שֶׁהוּא בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
which abides within thought in the brain;
שָׁם אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד.
there it is possible for two opposites to coexist within a single subject.
וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא כִּמְעַט מוּכְרָח
Moreover, it is almost necessary,
כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה דָּבָר וְהֶפְכּוֹ
according to how Hashem, blessed be He, established all Creation—each thing alongside its opposite,
כַּיָּדוּעַ מִסֵּפֶר יְצִירָה:
as is known from Sefer Yetzirah:
אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה הִיפּוּכוֹ מַמָּשׁ גַּם כֵּן;
there is nothing in existence that does not also possess its exact opposite;
וּבְוַדַּאי יֵשׁ לָזֶה רְשִׁימוּ בְּחָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
and there certainly exists an imprint of this in His wisdom, blessed be He,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן הַמּוֹצִיא לַפּוֹעַל.
which constitutes the root of the will bringing things into actualization.
רַק שֶׁבַּפּוֹעַל שְׁנֵי הַהֲפָכִים אֵינָם בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד:
Only in practical manifestation do two opposites not coexist in a single subject:
כְּשֶׁהוּא יוֹם אֵינוֹ לַיְלָה וּכְשֶׁהוּא לַיְלָה אֵינוֹ יוֹם,
when it is day it is not night, and when it is night it is not day;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּמָּקוֹר, שָׁם כּוּלָּא חַד.
whereas in the primordial Source, everything is utterly one.
וּלְכָךְ כָּל חִידּוּשׁ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁיּוֹצֵא לָעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה חָכָם,
And for this reason, with any novel insight of Torah that emerges into the world through a sage,
בְּהֶכְרֵחַ יוֹצֵא אָז גַּם כֵּן הַהֵיפֶךְ.
its opposite perforce emerges alongside it as well.
וְזֶה טַעַם: "פּוֹטֵר מַיִם רֵאשִׁית מָדוֹן" –
And this is the meaning of: 'One who releases water begins strife' (Proverbs 17:14) –
מַיִם הַיְינוּ תוֹרָה,
water signifies Torah;
מִי שֶׁפּוֹתֵחַ אֵיזֶה שַׁעַר וְדָבָר הוּא רֵאשִׁית מָדוֹן וּמַחֲלוֹקֶת.
whoever unlocks a gate or new concept inaugurates controversy and dispute.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ז.): "רֵישׁ מֵאָה דִּינֵי",
And our Sages of blessed memory taught in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (7a): 'the beginning of a hundred judgments,'
פֵּירוּשׁ כִּי יֵשׁ חֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה,
meaning that there exist fifty gates of understanding (Binah),
וְזֶה טַעַם מֵ"ט פָּנִים טָמֵא וּמֵ"ט פָּנִים טָהוֹר,
and this explains why there are forty-nine aspects to declare impure and forty-nine to declare pure,
כִּי שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים אֵין מוּשָּׂג.
because the fiftieth gate is beyond human comprehension.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּ"פָּנִים" פֵּירוּשׁ גִּלּוּיִים
And this signifies that 'panim' (aspects/faces) denotes outer disclosures,
מַה שֶּׁהֶחָכָם מַרְאֶה פָּנִים מִפְּנֵי מָה אוֹמֵר כֵּן;
wherein the sage demonstrates reasoned grounds explaining why he rules thus;
וְיָדוּעַ מֵ"ט הֵם שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע
and it is known that forty-nine is seven times seven,
נֶגֶד שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת הַבִּנְיָן שֶׁל כֹּחַ הַהִתְגַּלּוּת,
corresponding to the seven structural attributes of the power of manifestation;
וְשַׁעַר חֲמִשִּׁים נֶגֶד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
while the fiftieth gate corresponds to the intuitive understanding within the heart,
שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת כְּלָל לַחֲבֵירוֹ הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב מַה שֶּׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ בְּלִבּוֹ הַטַּעַם לַדָּבָר,
which is completely impossible to convey to another—the subjective feeling in his heart regarding the true reasoning for the matter,
דְּטַעַם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַסְבִּיר וּלְגַלּוֹת כְּלָל.
for the inner taste and essence can never be fully articulated or revealed.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (לה.):
And along the lines of what they stated in Sanhedrin (35a):
"לִיבָּא דְּאִינָשֵׁי אִינָשֵׁי",
'The heart of people makes them men,'
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹתוֹ בִּכְתָב
such that it cannot be disclosed in writing,
וְכֵן בְּדִבּוּר אִי אֶפְשָׁר,
and likewise in speech it cannot be fully conveyed,
רַק הָרְשִׁימוּ שֶׁבַּלֵּב מִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּדִבּוּר
save that the impression within the heart clothes itself in speech,
שֶׁכְּפִי הַרְגָּשַׁת הַטַּעַם שֶׁלּוֹ בַּלֵּב כָּךְ הוּא כֹּחַ הַדִּבּוּר,
so that in proportion to his felt grasp of the rationale in his heart, such is the force of the spoken word,
וְנִיכָּר עַל הַדִּבּוּר הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב,
and the heart's impression is recognizable upon the speech,
אֲבָל אֲמִיתַּת טַעַם שֶׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת.
yet the genuine truth of the taste he perceives cannot be externally unveiled.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (בְּשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים מִזְמוֹר יב):
Therefore they stated (in Shocher Tov, Psalms 12):
"תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק הָיָה אוֹמֵר מֵ"ט פָּנִים וְכוּלֵי",
'A distinguished disciple would articulate forty-nine aspects, etc.,'
פֵּירוּשׁ, אוֹמֵר לְגַלּוֹת אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק מֵ"ט פָּנִים.
meaning: through speech to disclose, one can communicate only forty-nine aspects.
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּקִבֵּל תּוֹרָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
And so too Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who received the Torah from Heaven,
שֶׁהוּא חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
which is the divine wisdom of Hashem, blessed be He,
מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ מוּשָּׂג לִבְנֵי אָדָם לְחַדֵּשׁ מִלְּבָבָם כְּמוֹ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
which is beyond human ability to innovate spontaneously from the heart like the Oral Torah,
אֶחָד (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כא:) דְּלֹא הִשִּׂיג שַׁעַר חֲמִשִּׁים,
one gate (Rosh Hashanah 21b) he did not attain, namely the fiftieth gate,
דְּשַׁעַר חֲמִשִּׁים מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא הַרְגָּשָׁתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּלֵּב שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה
for the fiftieth gate of the Written Torah is Hashem's own feeling in the supernal Heart,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת
which is impossible to reveal,
וְ"לִבָּא לְפוּמָא לָא גַּלְיָא".
and 'the heart does not reveal to the mouth.'
אֲבָל מַה שֶּׁמְּחַדְּשִׁים חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
However, regarding that which the sages of Israel innovate,
מִי שֶׁהוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ, הוּא מַשִּׂיג בְּאוֹתוֹ דָבָר כָּל הַחֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה,
the one who innovates grasps in that specific matter all fifty gates of understanding,
וְהֵן מֵאָה דִּינֵי, חֲמִשִּׁים לְכָל צַד.
and these constitute the hundred judgments—fifty to each side.
וּבְמַחֲלוֹקֶת שֶׁהוּא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם כְּמַחֲלוֹקֶת שַׁמַּאי וְהִלֵּל,
And in a dispute that is for the sake of Heaven, such as the controversy of Shammai and Hillel,
דְּבֵית הִלֵּל הָיוּ שׁוֹנִין דִּבְרֵיהֶם וְדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֵירוּבִין יג:),
where the House of Hillel would teach their own words alongside the words of the House of Shammai (as written in Eruvin 13b),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיוּ מַשִּׂיגִין גַּם דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְהַטְּעִימָה שֶׁל הַהֵיפֶךְ,
this signifies that they grasped the words of the House of Shammai and the experiential taste of the opposing stance as well;
וּכְעִנְיַן אוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר שְׁנֵי הַפָּנִים,
mirroring that distinguished disciple who could articulate both perspectives,
כִּי מִצַּד דְּבוּקוּתוֹ בְּחָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא מַשִּׂיג בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שְׁנֵי הַהֲפָכִים שֶׁבַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה,
for through his attachment to the wisdom of Hashem, blessed be He, he comprehends within that very matter both opposites present in the Supernal Thought,
וְנִמְצָא לְכָל אֶחָד מֵאָה.
resulting in a full hundred for each.
וְזֶה טַעַם הַגְּמָרָא בְּשַׁבָּת (קכט:):
And this is the inner reason of the Gemara in Shabbat (129b):
"מֵאָה קָרֵי בְּזוּזֵי וְכוּלֵי",
"A hundred pumpkins for a zuz, etc.,"
וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
and this is not the place to elaborate further.

sections.en: Revelation through Concealment

items.h: Spiritual delight and divine revelation emerge from prior darkness, teaching that the very place of deficiency can become the source of its opposite virtue.

Seif 1 — Delight Born from Concealment
The highest spiritual light and virtue emerge from the very darkness and deficiency that initially obscure them.

p: הַשָּׂגַת הַגִּלּוּי רַק מִתּוֹךְ הַהֶעְלֵם,
The attainment of divine revelation comes only out of concealment,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, מז עַמּוּד ב):
along the lines of what they said in the Zohar (Part III, 47b):
"מַאן דְּיָתֵיב בְּצַעֲרָא וְכוּלֵי",
"One who sits in sorrow, etc.,"
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִי שֶׁמּוּרְגָּל בְּתַעֲנוּגִים,
in contrast to one who is accustomed to worldly pleasures;
וְאֵין בַּטּוֹבָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעוֹנֶג.
and in goodness, there is nothing higher than transcendent delight (oneg).
וְעִיקַּר הַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא רַק כְּפִי הָעוֹנֶג שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג מִזֶּה.
And the essence of spiritual comprehension corresponds solely to the measure of delight one derives from it.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צג.):
And this explains what they taught in Sanhedrin (93a):
"צַדִּיקִים גְּדוֹלִים מִמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת",
"The righteous are greater than the ministering angels,"
וּמָצִינוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים לְהֵיפֶךְ,
yet we find several times the opposite stated,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַב אַבְרָהָם בֶּן עֶזְרָא דְּוַדַּאי הַשָּׂגַת מַלְאָכִים גְּדוֹלָה,
as Rabbi Avraham Ibn Ezra wrote that the intellectual apprehension of angels is certainly greater,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן.
and as Maimonides (Rambam) also wrote.
רַק הֵם אֵין לָהֶם עוֹנֶג,
However, they possess no experience of sublime delight,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פט.):
just as our Sages stated in Shabbat (89a):
"כְּלוּם יֵשׁ יֵצֶר הָרָע בֵּינֵיכֶם?",
"Is there an evil inclination among you?"
דְּהָעוֹנֶג נִמְשָׁךְ רַק מִן הַהֵיפֶךְ.
for sacred delight is drawn exclusively out of its opposite.
וְזֶהוּ יִתְרוֹן הָאוֹר כְּשֶׁהוּא מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
And this is the preeminence of light when it emerges from darkness;
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּעוֹנֶג הוּא עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִן הַשֵּׂכֶל,
for as is known, oneg is the primordial depth that transcends mortal intellect,
כְּטַעַם: "תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה'",
in the spirit of: 'You shall delight upon Hashem' (Isaiah 58:14) –
פֵּירוּשׁ, שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַמּוּשָּׂג,
meaning: the Tetragrammaton (Havayah) represents the manifest expansion of that which can be comprehended,
וְהָעוֹנֶג הוּא דְּבֵיקוּת בַּמֶּה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַמּוּשָּׂג.
while delight is the mystical cleaving to that which transcends comprehension.
"וְהָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל" –
'The people walking in darkness have seen a great light' (Isaiah 9:1) –
פֵּירוּשׁ, "גָּדוֹל" הוּא מִמִּדַּת גְּדוּלָּה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
meaning: 'great' stems from the divine attribute of Gedulah (Lovingkindness/Greatness) of Hashem, blessed be He,
דְּהַיְינוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עַד אֵין שִׁיעוּר,
signifying infinite expansion without measure,
כִּי הוּא לְמַעְלָה מִן הַשִּׁיעוּר,
because it is completely beyond bounded measure,
כְּעִנְיַן (שַׁבָּת קיח.):
in the manner of Shabbat (118a):
"הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים".
"Whoever delights in the Sabbath is given a boundless heritage."
כִּי כֹּחַ הָעוֹנֶג הוּא לְמַעְלָה מִקַּו הַמִּדָּה,
For the power of delight is higher than the measuring line,
כִּי לְהַשָּׂגָה יֵשׁ מִדָּה וּגְבוּל,
since cognitive apprehension has measure and boundaries,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְעוֹנֶג.
whereas delight has no boundaries.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם "בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וְכוּלֵי" (שַׁבָּת עז:),
And this is the secret of the universe's creation, 'first darkness, etc.' (Shabbat 77b),
דִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם הָיָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה
for the creation of the world occurred precisely in this manner
לְהַשִּׂיג מִדַּת הָעוֹנֶג,
in order to attain the divine attribute of delight;
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא.
and this is achievable only through darkness coming first.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ" דַּיְיקָא, "אָז ה' אוֹר לִי",
And as it is written (Micah 7:8): specifically 'though I sit in darkness, then Hashem is a light unto me,'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים יח, יב): "יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ",
and as it is written (Psalms 18:12): 'He makes darkness His secret place,'
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִסְתַּתֵּר תּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ.
meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, conceals Himself within the darkness.
וּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הַחַשְׁכוּת וְהַהֶעְלֵם
And in proportion to the intensity of the obscurity and concealment,
כֵּן הוּא תּוֹקֶף הָאוֹר הַגָּנוּז בּוֹ
such is the magnitude of the light hidden within it
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַחַשְׁכוּת.
that one is able to attain through that very darkness.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם מִשָּׁם אֶת ה' וְגוֹמֵר", מִשָּׁם דַּיְיקָא;
And as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:29): 'And from there you shall seek Hashem, etc.'—specifically from there;
וְאוֹמֵר: "עֵת צָרָה וְגוֹמֵר וּמִמֶּנָּה יִוָּשֵׁעַ",
and Scripture states (Jeremiah 30:7): 'It is a time of trouble... but he shall be saved out of it,'
וְהַכָּתוּב אֵין קוֹרֵא צָרָה לַגּוּף לְבַד,
and Scripture does not define trouble as pertaining to the body alone,
רַק מַה שֶּׁבֶּאֱמֶת מֵיצַר גַּם בַּנֶּפֶשׁ
rather that which truly afflicts the soul as well;
מִזֶּה דַּיְיקָא הוּא הַיְשׁוּעָה לַנֶּפֶשׁ.
out of this specific inner distress emerges the ultimate salvation for the soul.
וְכֵן בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר,
And similarly throughout every single generation,
אֵין לְךָ מִי שֶׁטָּעַם מִכָּל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
you have no one who tasted of all the physical desires of this world like King Solomon, peace be upon him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר קֹהֶלֶת: "עָשִׂיתִי לִי וְגוֹמֵר וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר שָׁאֲלוּ עֵינַי וְגוֹמֵר" כַּנּוֹדָע,
and as written in the Book of Ecclesiastes (2:4, 10): 'I made for myself, etc., and whatever my eyes desired, etc.,' as is known;
וְאֵין לְךָ גַּם כֵּן לֵב נָקִי מִכָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲוָה כִּלְבָבוֹ,
and likewise you have no heart as utterly cleansed from every form of lust as was his heart,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יָדַיִם סוֹף פֶּרֶק ג):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated at the end of Yadayim (chapter 3):
עַל סֵפֶר שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים שֶׁהוּא קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים.
concerning the Song of Songs, that it is the Holy of Holies.
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה וְתַאֲוָה שָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא קְדוּשָּׁה
And wherever you find a boundary against immorality and lust, there you find holiness
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כד),
(as written in Vayikra Rabbah, Parashah 24),
דְּזֶה טַעַם קְדוּשָּׁה – פְּרִישׁוּת מִתַּאֲווֹת רַק מוּקְדָּשׁ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for this is the very definition of kedushah: separation from base desires to be consecrated solely unto Hashem, blessed be He;
כִּי זֶה הֵיפֶךְ זֶה:
because the one is the complete antithesis of the other:
הַשָּׁקוּעַ בַּתַּאֲווֹת נֶאֱמַר: "לְתַאֲוָה יְבַקֵּשׁ נִפְרָד",
regarding one immersed in lust it is stated: 'He who separates himself seeks his own desire' (Proverbs 18:1),
שֶׁהוּא נִפְרָד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
meaning that he becomes separated and alienated from Hashem, blessed be He;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה מוּקְדָּשׁ לַשָּׁמַיִם,
in contrast, in kedushah one is consecrated unto Heaven,
כְּמוֹ קִדּוּשֵׁי אִשָּׁה פֵּירְשׁוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִדּוּשִׁין ב:):
just as regarding betrothal (kiddushin) of a woman, our Rabbis explained in Kiddushin (2b):
לְשׁוֹן הֶקְדֵּשׁ, שֶׁשַּׁיָּיכָה לַבַּעַל.
it is an expression of consecration (hekdesh), designating her exclusively to her husband.
וְעִנְיַן שִׁיר הוּא מִצַּד הַחֵשֶׁק,
And the essence of song emerges from intense, passionate longing,
דְּלָכֵן נִקְרָא שִׁירֵי עֲגָבִים;
which is why love-ballads are termed shirei agavim;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר כָּלְתָה נַפְשׁוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and when a person's soul yearns away entirely toward Hashem, blessed be He,
וְהוּא חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה לוֹ,
and he is lovesick for Him,
אָז נִפְתַּח פִּיו לְשׁוֹרֵר לְפָנָיו.
then his mouth is opened to sing before Him.
וְאֵין לְךָ שִׁירִים מְעוֹרְרִים אַהֲבָה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם וְהִתְאַחֲדוּתָם כְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים.
And you have no songs that awaken the love of Israel for their Father in Heaven and their mutual union like the Song of Songs.
וְאַהֲבָה זוֹ הוּא הֵיפֶךְ אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And this sacred love is the direct opposite of worldly love,
וּלְכָךְ הוּא קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים,
therefore it is the Holy of Holies,
שַׁיָּיךְ לְגַמְרֵי לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
belonging entirely to Hashem, blessed be He,
וְנִפְרָשׁ לְגַמְרֵי מִכָּל תַּאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and completely separated from all earthly desires,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לָהֶם כְּלָל.
having no connection to them whatsoever.
וְכָךְ הוּא הַמִּדָּה:
And this is the operative spiritual principle:
דְּאוֹתוֹ לֵב שֶׁטּוֹעֵם מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ עַד קָצֶה הָאַחֲרוֹן
that the very heart which tastes of the darkness down to the outermost edge
וּמְבַקֵּשׁ מִשָּׁם אֶת ה',
and seeks Hashem specifically from that place,
טוֹעֵם הָאוֹר עַד קָצֶה הָאַחֲרוֹן,
tastes the divine light up to its ultimate boundary,
עַד שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג שֶׁאֵין חֹשֶׁךְ
until he realizes that darkness has no independent reality,
וְ"כָל חֹשֶׁךְ לֹא יַחְשִׁיךְ וְגוֹמֵר לַיְלָה כַּיּוֹם יָאִיר וְגוֹמֵר".
and that 'even darkness darkens not from You, but the night shines as the day' (Psalms 139:12).
וְכֵן בְּכָל הַמִּדּוֹת:
And similarly across all character traits:
בִּמְקוֹם צָרוּת עַיִן שָׁם הוּא טוֹבַת עַיִן,
in the very place of a stingy, narrow eye, there resides the generous, good eye;
וּבִמְקוֹם רוֹעַ לֵב – לֵב טוֹב.
and in the very place of a hardened, malicious heart resides the good and benevolent heart.

sections.en: Purim, the Lot, and the Erasure of Amalek

items.h: Purim's holiness arises through Haman's own lot, revealing how Amalek's force becomes the instrument of its destruction before renewed Temple building.

Seif 1 — The Lot that Destroys Amalek
Purim transforms Haman's lottery into the mechanism of Amalek's downfall and preparation for renewed redemption.

p: עִנְיַן פּוּרִים עַל שֵׁם הַפּוּר,
The matter of Purim is named after the lot (pur),
דִּקְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת קָבוּעַ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דִּמְקַדֵּשׁ,
for the holiness of Shabbat is established permanently by Hashem, blessed be He, Who sanctifies it,
וּקְדוּשַׁת יוֹם טוֹב וְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי,
while the sanctity of the festivals and Rosh Chodesh is sanctified by the Jewish people ('Israel sanctifies the seasons'),
אֲבָל פּוּרִים אוֹתוֹ יוֹם זָכָה בַּגּוֹרָל עַל יְדֵי הָמָן
yet concerning Purim, that very day was selected through the lottery cast by Haman
שֶׁנִּבְחַר לִמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק,
which was singled out for the obliteration of Amalek,
כִּי "מִינֵיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא וְכוּלֵי" (סַנְהֶדְרִין לט:),
for 'from the forest itself comes the axe-handle to fell it, etc.' (Sanhedrin 39b),
וְעַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ נִבְחַר
and through Haman himself it was chosen:
עַל פִּי הַגּוֹרָל נָפַל עַל יוֹם זֶה
by means of the lot it fell upon this specific day
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מוּכָן לִמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק
to be prepared for the destruction of Amalek,
וְלָנוּחַ בַּיּוֹם שֶׁאַחֲרָיו וְעָשׂוּ וְגוֹמֵר.
and to rest on the day following it, 'and they made [it a day of feasting], etc.'
וְלִכְאוֹרָה הַגּוֹרָל נִרְאֶה מִקְרֶה,
Now seemingly, a lottery appears to be mere blind chance,
רַק הַכָּתוּב מֵעִיד (מִשְׁלֵי טז, לג):
yet Scripture testifies (Proverbs 16:33):
"וּמֵה' כָּל מִשְׁפָּטוֹ",
"'and from Hashem comes its every verdict,'
דְּהַמִּקְרֶה גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
revealing that chance itself is likewise directed by Hashem, blessed be He.
עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא עִיקַּר נִיצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק
Through this profound realization occurs the principal defeat of Amalek,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ",
concerning whom it is stated: 'who happened upon you (karkha / rooted in mikreh - chance),'
וְכֵן בְּהָמָן: "אֲשֶׁר קָרָהוּ",
and likewise regarding Haman: 'all that had happened to him (karahu),'
שֶׁנִּתְלִים בַּמִּקְרֶה;
for they attribute everything to arbitrary chance;
כִּי כְּפִי שָׁרְשָׁם כָּךְ הֵם כָּל עִנְיָנָם,
since according to their essential spiritual root, so unfolds their entire character,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ.):
along the lines of what they stated (Sanhedrin 90a):
"הוּא כָּפַר בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, לְפִיכָךְ אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק וְכוּלֵי",
'He denied the resurrection of the dead, therefore he has no share in it, etc.,'
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַבְּחִירָה.
and this represents the human perspective of free choice.
וּמִצַּד הַיְדִיעָה הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ:
Yet from the perspective of supernal divine foreknowledge, it is the reverse:
שֶׁמִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים
namely, that whoever has no allotted share in the resurrection of the dead
הוּא כּוֹפֵר בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים.
ends up denying the resurrection of the dead.
וְכֵן כָּל עִנְיַן עֲמָלֵק מִקְרֶה בָּעוֹלָם,
And likewise, the whole phenomenon of Amalek is the manifestation of 'chance' in the universe,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן מִקְרֶה
for Hashem, blessed be He, deliberately created the reality of chance as well,
דְּאֵין דָּבָר חוּץ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
since there is nothing outside of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְדָבָר זֶה גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and this concept also originates from Hashem, blessed be He:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִקְרֶה מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ מְסוּדָּר כְּפִי הַסֵּדֶר שֶׁיִּסַּד.
that there should appear as 'chance' whatever is not aligned with the manifest order He established.
וְזֶהוּ עֲמָלֵק,
And this is the archetype of Amalek;
וּלְפִי שֶׁהוּא מִקְרֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ",
and because his existence is rooted in chance, as written 'who met you by chance (karkha),'
הוּא תּוֹלֶה הַכֹּל בַּמִּקְרֶה.
he attributes everything to coincidence.
וְאָמַר "אֲשֶׁר קָרָהוּ",
And Scripture says: 'all that happened to him (karahu),'
וְזֶהוּ הָיָה בְּעֵת הַסּוֹף שֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁהָלַךְ לַאֲבַדּוֹן,
and this was at the time of his ultimate downfall when he was headed for oblivion;
אָז אָמַר "אֲשֶׁר קָרָהוּ"
only then did he say 'all that happened to him,'
שֶׁתָּלָה הַכֹּל בַּמִּקְרֶה,
attributing everything stubbornly to random occurrence,
דְּכָל דָּבָר מִתְבָּרֵר בְּסוֹפוֹ,
for every entity's true nature is clarified at its culmination;
כְּמוֹ בְּבִלְעָם בַּסּוֹף בְּמַעֲשֵׂה דִּשְׁטִים
just as with Balaam at the end in the incident of Shittim,
נִתְגַּלָּה דְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ זְנוּת,
it was unveiled that his essential root was licentiousness,
וְאָז אָמַר: "הִנְנִי הוֹלֵךְ לְעַמִּי וְגוֹמֵר",
and then he said: 'Behold, I go unto my people, etc.,'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי בָּלָק, וּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י)
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Yalkut Shimoni, Balak; and Rashi's commentary)
וְנוֹדַע שֶׁנִּבְאַשׁ.
and it became universally known that he had made himself odious.
דְּבַתְּחִלָּה כָּל דָּבָר רַע הַגָּוֶון הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ,
For initially, in every evil matter the outward guise portrays the reverse,
וְגָוֶון עֲמָלֵק הוּא שֶׁאֵין נִתְלֶה בַּמִּקְרֶה,
and the deceptive guise of Amalek is that he does not seem to hang on chance,
דְּעִנְיַן הַגּוֹרָל מָצִינוּ בַּתּוֹרָה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וּבַחֲלוּקַּת הָאָרֶץ,
since the concept of the sacred lottery is found in the Torah on Yom Kippur and in the division of the Land of Israel,
דְּזֶהוּ עִנְיַן יִשְׂרָאֵל לִסְמוֹךְ עַל גּוֹרָל
where it is the hallmark of Israel to rely upon the lot
לְהַחֲזִיק שֶׁאֵין הַדָּבָר בְּמִקְרֶה.
in order to affirm that nothing occurs by chance.
וְזֶה כָּל תָּקְפּוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו:
And this constitutes the full deceitful strength of Esau:
"פּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו וְכוּלֵי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה סה),
'displaying his split hooves to appear kosher, etc.' (Bereishit Rabbah, beginning of Parashah 65),
עַד שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לוֹמַר: "אֲנִי חָשַׂפְתִּי אֶת עֵשָׂו, גִּלֵּיתִי מִסְתָּרָיו",
until Hashem, blessed be He, had to declare: 'I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places' (Jeremiah 49:10),
דְּאַחֵר לֹא יוּכַל לְגַלּוֹת זֶה.
for no other could ever expose this.
וְנֶאֱמַר: "אֵיךְ נֶחְפְּשׂוּ עֵשָׂו, נִבְעוּ מַצְפֻּנָיו" (עֹבַדְיָה א, ו),
And it is stated: 'How are the things of Esau searched out, how are his hidden treasures sought out!' (Obadiah 1:6),
מַשְׁמָע דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ מַצְפּוּנִים;
implying that he harbors deep, inscrutable concealments;
וְאֵין הַכָּתוּב קוֹרֵא מַצְפּוּן מַה שֶּׁצָּפוּן לְעֵין סְתָם בְּנֵי אָדָם,
and Scripture does not title as 'hidden' that which is merely concealed from ordinary men,
רַק מַה שֶּׁצָּפוּן גַּם מִמַּלְאָכִים וּנְבִיאִים וַחֲכָמִים,
rather that which remains veiled even from angels, prophets, and sages,
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר מֵאָדָם עַצְמוֹ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַטְעוֹת עַצְמוֹ,
and it goes without saying from man himself, who can self-deceptively mislead his own consciousness,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת זֶה
so that it is impossible to expose this
אֶלָּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַבָּקִי בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לֵב.
save for Hashem alone, Who is expertly versed in the innermost depths of the heart.
וְזֶה כָּל כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּקְרָא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם",
And this is the entire power of Amalek who is termed 'first among the nations' (Numbers 24:20),
וְנֶאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים כה, יט): "וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר תִּמְחֶה וְגוֹמֵר",
and it is stated (Deuteronomy 25:19): 'And it shall be when Hashem has given you rest, etc., you shall blot out, etc.,'
דְּכָל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
for regarding all idolaters,
אִלּוּ לֹא הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ מֵהֶם בְּלִבּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
were there no spiritual root of them latent in the hearts of Israel,
לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם מְצִיאוּת בָּעוֹלָם.
they would possess no independent existence in the world.
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן נִיצּוּחָם:
And this is the secret of their ultimate defeat:
כַּאֲשֶׁר מְנַצֵּחַ אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הָרַע שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
whenever one subdues that interior power of evil within the heart,
מִמֵּילָא הוּא מְנַצֵּחַ אוֹתָהּ אוּמָּה בַּפּוֹעַל.
he automatically overpowers that physical nation in actuality.
וְכָל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הֵם רַע נִגְלֶה,
All the other idolaters represent overt, recognizable evil;
וְ"הָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר" – שֶׁכְּבָר יִהְיֶה לוֹ נִיחָא מִזֶּה
and 'it shall be when He gives you rest, etc.' means when a person has achieved respite from this,
שֶׁלֹּא יְבַלְבְּלוּ שׁוּם רַע וְנִדְמֶה בְּעֵינָיו טוֹב,
such that no overt evil agitates him and he appears good in his own eyes,
אָז צָרִיךְ לְהִתְחַזֵּק נֶגֶד עֲמָלֵק
only then must he brace himself to battle Amalek,
שֶׁהוּא נִדְמֶה בְּעֵינָיו טוֹב,
who deceptively seems entirely upright in his eyes,
רַק שֶׁהוּא עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית דְּרַע,
whereas in truth he is the primordial root-depth of evil,
וּבִשְׁאָר הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת אֵין מוּרְגָּשׁ רַע כְּלָל.
and throughout the rest of outward manifestation no evil is sensed at all.
וּבוֹ צָרִיךְ "תִּמְחֶה",
And concerning him Scripture demands 'you shall utterly blot out,'
כִּי מַה שֶּׁרַע בַּנִּגְלֶה, הַכֹּל הוּא לְצוֹרֶךְ,
because that which is overtly evil was created for a constructive purpose,
שֶׁאֵין לְךָ רָעָה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שִׁימּוּשׁ לְצוֹרֶךְ גַּם כֵּן,
there being no base trait lacking a constructive application,
דְּלוּלֵי כֵן לֹא בָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דָּבָר זֶה בַּלֵּב.
since otherwise Hashem, blessed be He, would never have created it within the human heart.
וְתַאֲוָה וְכַעַס וְכַדּוֹמֶה
Bodily desire, anger, and the like,
הַכֹּל פְּעָמִים יֵשׁ בָּהֶם צוֹרֶךְ
all sometimes have legitimate sanctified utility
כְּשֶׁמִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶם כְּפִי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּנּוֹדָע.
when one directs them according to the will of Hashem, blessed be He, as is known.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּקְרָא מִקְרֶה
In contrast, Amalek is designated as 'chance' (mikreh)
וְאֵינוֹ מֵעֶצֶם הַבְּרִיאָה,
and does not stem from the fundamental fabric of Creation;
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא גַּם דָּבָר זֶה
for Hashem brought forth this phenomenon
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דָּבָר נִרְאֶה מִקְרֶה
merely so that there exist a reality seemingly ruled by chance,
וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִמְחוֹתוֹ לְגַמְרֵי,
and which must be eradicated completely,
כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ לֹא יִשָּׁאֵר רוֹשֶׁם לְטוֹב כְּלָל.
because from it no remnant of goodness shall ever remain.
כִּי רֵאשִׁית הַכֹּל הוּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the true Beginning of all existence is Hashem, blessed be He,
וּמִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת יֵשׁ חִלּוּקֵי מִדּוֹת שׁוֹנִים,
and across outward manifestation there are differing spiritual attributes;
אֲבָל הַ"רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם" הוּא "עֲדֵי אֹבֵד",
but the counterfeit 'first among the nations' is doomed 'unto destruction' (Numbers 24:20),
כִּי "אֲנִי רִאשׁוֹן",
for 'I am the First' (Isaiah 44:6),
וְכָל רֵאשִׁית שֶׁחוּץ מִמֶּנּוּ הוּא אֶפֶס בֶּאֱמֶת.
and any independent primacy outside of Him is absolute nothingness.
כִּי כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת "קָרוּ לֵיהּ אֱלָהָא דֶּאֱלָהָא" (מְנָחוֹת קי.),
For all other nations 'call Him the God of gods' (Menachot 110a),
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַתּוֹלִים בַּמִּקְרֶה וְ"לֵית דִּין וְכוּלֵי".
unlike those who ascribe reality to chance, claiming 'there is neither justice nor Judge, etc.'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה כֻּלּוֹ רַע
And just as within Israel that which appears entirely evil
הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כֻּלּוֹ טוֹב,
is in internal truth entirely good,
כִּי הֵם מְהַפְּכִין חֲשׁוֹכָא לִנְהוֹרָא,
for they transmute darkness into radiant light;
כָּךְ בָּאוּמּוֹת הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ:
so too among the nations it is the reverse:
מִי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כֻּלּוֹ טוֹב
he who appears outwardly entirely virtuous
הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כֻּלּוֹ רַע,
is in internal truth entirely evil,
וְאֵין בּוֹ הַשְׁאָרָה לְטוֹב כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
and contains no lingering trace of goodness whatsoever.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And the subtle root of Amalek within the heart
הַיְינוּ הֶעְדֵּר הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח,
is precisely the absence of immediate perception of the divine Presence,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא):
as written (Midrash Tanchuma, end of Parashat Ki Teitzei):
"אֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם וְאֵין הַכִּסֵּא שָׁלֵם עַד וְכוּלֵי".
"'Neither the Name is whole nor the Throne whole until [Amalek is eradicated].'"
וּשְׁלֵימוּת הַשֵּׁם הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים נ.):
And the wholeness of the Name is as written in Pesachim (50a):
"לֹא כְּשֶׁאֲנִי נִכְתָּב אֲנִי נִקְרָא",
"'Not as I am written am I pronounced,'
בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין בְּלִיטָה זוֹ לָעַיִן לְגַמְרֵי
for in this world this truth is not manifestly prominent to the eye,
אֵיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה הוֹוֶה וְיִהְיֶה וּמְהַוֶּוה הַכֹּל
as to how Hashem, blessed be He, was, is, will be, and continuously animates all,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הוֹרָאַת שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה.
which is the precise meaning of the Tetragrammaton (Havayah).
וְהַכִּסֵּא הוּא הַהַשְׁגָּחָה,
And the Throne (Kissei) embodies divine providence,
שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב כְּמֶלֶךְ עַל כִּסֵּא וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה.
enthroned as King upon a seat of judgment Whose sovereignty rules over all.
"וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר" –
And 'it shall be when He gives you rest, etc.' teaches:
דְּמִתְּחִלָּה יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים אֲחֵרִים, תַּאֲווֹת וְכַעַס וְכַדּוֹמֶה הַמַּסְתִּירִים זֶה,
that initially there exist other distractions—passions, anger, and the like—which obscure this;
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר לְבָבוֹ נָקִי
yet even when a person's heart has been cleansed
וַעֲדַיִן אֵין הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח מְאִירָה לוֹ
and nonetheless the conscious awareness of the Presence does not radiate within him,
לִהְיוֹת מַמָּשׁ תָּדִיר כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל
to stand continuously as one situated before an awesome King,
וּמוּרְגָּשׁ לָעַיִן בְּכָל דָּבָר אֵיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנְהִיג וּבוֹרֵא וְאֵין בִּלְתּוֹ –
where it is vividly felt in every detail how Hashem directs, creates, and there is none beside Him—
זֶהוּ מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק
this subtle void stems from the root of Amalek,
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִמְחוֹת בַּעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב:
which one must eradicate through interior service of the heart:
"וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר יָרִים מֹשֶׁה יָדוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת יז, יא).
'And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed, etc.' (Exodus 17:11).
וְהוּא קוֹדֶם הַכְנָסַת כָּל דָּבָר קְדוּשָּׁה גְּמוּרָה:
And this eradication must precede the entry of any manifestation of complete holiness:
קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
prior to the Giving of the Torah (at Rephidim),
וְקוֹדֶם בִּנְיַן בַּיִת רִאשׁוֹן –
and prior to the construction of the First Temple—
מִיָּד בִּמְלוּכַת שָׁאוּל הָיָה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְבִנְיַן הַבַּיִת
for right at the coronation of Saul there arose an awakening to build the Temple,
וְהֻוצְרַךְ מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק קוֹדֶם עַל יְדֵי שָׁאוּל וְדָוִד.
and the blotting out of Amalek had to occur first through Saul and David.
וְכֵן קוֹדֶם בִּנְיַן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי –
And so too prior to the building of the Second Temple—
מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק דְּהָמָן.
there occurred the downfall of the Amalekite Haman.
וְכֵן יִהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
And so shall it unfold in the ultimate future
קוֹדֶם בִּנְיַן בַּיִת הַשְּׁלִישִׁי
prior to the building of the Third Temple,
שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ, אָמֵן.
which shall be built speedily in our days, Amen.

sections.en: Exile of the Shechinah and the Beginning of Redemption

items.h: The Shechinah accompanies Israel even in distance; recognizing that hidden presence marks the first movement from exile toward final redemption.

Seif 1 — The Shechinah within Exile
Recognizing that the Shechinah accompanies Israel in exile becomes itself the beginning of redemption.

p: עִנְיַן גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה,
The matter of the exile of the Shechinah,
פֵּירוּשׁ שְׁכִינָה הוּא מִדַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
meaning: Shechinah is the divine attribute of Hashem, blessed be He, wherein He dwells within the hearts of the children of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְשָׁכַנְתִּי בְּתוֹךְ [בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל] וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is written: "And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel, etc.,"
"אֲנִי ה' שֹׁכֵן וְגוֹמֵר",
"'I am Hashem Who dwells, etc.,'"
וְהוּא מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת
and this corresponds to the attribute of Malchut (Sovereignty),
כְּטַעַם: "וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה",
in the spirit of: "And His kingdom rules over all,"
פֵּירוּשׁ "בַּכֹּל" – הַיְינוּ גַּם מַה שֶּׁהוּא מֶרְחָק רַב
meaning 'over all'—including even that which stands at a vast spiritual distance
"וּבְתוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם" (יוֹמָא נו:),
and 'in the midst of their uncleanness' (Yoma 56b),
אֲפִילּוּ בְּלֵב הַמְשׁוּקָּע מִכָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת וְזוּהֲמָא
even within a heart deeply immersed in all manner of lusts and contamination,
שֶׁהֵם הַנִּקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב טֻמְאָה,
which are designated in biblical terminology as impurity;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם "חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ",
nonetheless, 'Hashem's portion is His people,'
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא,
and 'even though he has sinned, he remains Israel,'
שָׁרְשׁוֹ דָּבוּק הוּא בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
his essential root remaining bound to Hashem, blessed be He,
וְקָדוֹשׁ שָׁרוּי בְּתוֹךְ מֵעָיו
and the Holy One rests deep within his innermost being
וּבְמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ הַנֶּעְלָם.
and within the hidden recesses of his heart.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים שֶׁרָצָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא –
And this is the primary dwelling of the Shechinah in lower realms that the Holy One desired—
הַיְינוּ בְּתוֹךְ לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
namely, within the hearts of the children of Israel.
אֲבָל בַּגָּלוּת נֶאֱמַר: "לֶב מֶלֶךְ בְּיַד ה'",
However, regarding the exile it is stated: 'The king's heart is in the hand of Hashem,' (Proverbs 21:1),
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם בְּחִירָה, רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנְהִיגָם.
for pagan kings possess no free will, rather Hashem, blessed be He, directs them.
וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ לִבָּם לְהַנְהִיג,
Yet it is not said that Hashem dwells within their heart to guide them,
דְּזֶה לֹא נִקְרָא שֶׁהוּא בְּתוֹךְ הַלֵּב כְּלָל;
for this is not considered being within the heart at all;
וְגַם בַּגָּלוּת אֵין שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶלָּא בְּתוֹךְ לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and even in exile His divine presence dwells solely within the hearts of the Jewish people,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ב, ט):
and as they said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:9):
"מֵעוֹלָם לֹא זָזָה שְׁכִינָה וְכוּלֵי".
"'Never did the Shechinah depart [from the Western Wall], etc.'"
רַק אֶצְלָם הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ,
Except that with foreign monarchs it is the reverse:
דִּלְבָבָם בְּיָדוֹ,
for their heart is in His hand,
שֶׁאֵין לִבָּם גַּם כֵּן תּוֹךְ לִבָּם,
meaning that even their own heart does not belong to them,
דְּאֵין לִבָּם בִּרְשׁוּתָם לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹנָם,
their heart not being in their own control to act as they wish,
רַק כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
rather exclusively according to the will of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְאֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל, רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם מַה שֶּׁהוּא נֶגֶד רְצוֹנָם נִקְרָא בֶּאֱמֶת רְצוֹנָם,
Whereas with Israel, Hashem's will—even that which seems contrary to their outward desire—is fundamentally their true inner will,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ״ם (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב מֵהִלְכוֹת גֵּירוּשִׁין)
as known from the words of Maimonides (end of chapter 2 of the Laws of Divorce)
בְּטַעַם "כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר רוֹצֶה אָנִי".
regarding the rationale for 'they compel him until he says: I am willing.'
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן טַעַם דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (ד.)
And this is likewise the underlying reason for the words of our Sages at the beginning of the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (4a)
הַחִלּוּק בְּעִנְיַן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ וְעַל מְנָת לְקַבֵּל פְּרָס בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם,
regarding the distinction in serving not for its own sake and on condition of receiving reward between Israel and idolaters, see there;
דִּבְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת הֵיפֶךְ רְצוֹנָם הָאֲמִיתִּי
for among idolaters, the will of Hashem is genuinely the opposite of their authentic desire,
שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which is entirely contrary to the will of Hashem.
רַק דְּהַמְּלָכִים אֵין לִבָּם בִּרְשׁוּתָם,
Only that the monarchs have no dominion over their hearts,
רַק בְּיָדוֹ וּרְשׁוּתוֹ וְכֹחוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which are kept strictly in the hand, domain, and power of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא גָּלוּת,
And this condition constitutes exile,
שֶׁגָּלְתָה שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לִפְלַטְרִין שֶׁל מְלָכִים מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
wherein His divine presence is exiled into the palaces of pagan kings,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה טו)
along the lines of what they said in Shemot Rabbah (Parashah 15)
הַמָּשָׁל: "אֲפִילּוּ אֶלֶף טֻמְאוֹת אֲנִי נִכְנָס וְכוּלֵי"
the parable: "Even into a thousand impurities I enter, etc."
עַל פָּסוּק "וְעָבַרְתִּי אֲנִי ה'".
on the verse 'And I, Hashem, will pass through' (Exodus 12:12).
דְּזֶה שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לְהִטָּפֵל בְּלִבּוֹת מְלָכִים דְּאוּמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
For having to occupy Himself with the hearts of pagan kings,
זֶה אֵין דּוֹמֶה כְּלָל לְ"תוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם" דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
is completely incomparable to being 'in the midst of the impurities' of the children of Israel;
דְּזוֹ טֻמְאָה קַלָּה לְפִי שָׁעָה
for Israel's is a temporary, light impurity
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ טָהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל ה',
which possesses purification in Hashem, the ritual pool (mikveh) of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא פה:):
as they said (Yoma 85b):
"מִי מְטַהֵרְכֶם? אֲבִיכֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם",
"Who purifies you? Your Father in Heaven,"
כַּאֲשֶׁר דְּבוּקִים בּוֹ שֶׁהוּא שָׁרְשָׁם,
for when they cleave unto Him Who is their root,
הֲרֵי זֶה כְּמוֹ הַשָּׁקָה לְמַעְיָין
it is like contact (hashakah) with a flowing natural spring,
דְּמוֹעִיל לְטַהֵר מַיִם טְמֵאִים.
which is halakhically effective to purify contaminated waters.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן טֻמְאַת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הִיא אֲבִי אֲבוֹת הַטֻּמְאָה,
In contrast, the impurity of idolaters is the ultimate progenitor of uncleanness (avi avot hatumah),
וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם מַדְרֵגוֹת:
and among them are distinct levels:
טֻמְאַת עֲמָלֵק הִיא אֲבִי טֻמְאָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ טָהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶוה כְּלָל,
the impurity of Amalek is a degree of uncleanness that has no purification in a mikveh at all,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "תִּמְחֶה";
as it is written: 'You shall blot out';
וּשְׁאָר אֻמּוֹת הוּא מַה שֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַהֲשִׁיבָם לַמַּעְיָין כְּלָל,
and other nations are of a nature that they cannot be restored to the spring at all,
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם דְּבֵיקוּת וְהַשָּׁקָה לַמַּעְיָין;
since they possess no inherent connection or confluence with the spring;
רַק בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֱמַר: "יִשָּׁקֵנִי מִנְּשִׁיקוֹת פִּיהוּ",
only regarding Israel is it stated: 'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth' (Song of Songs 1:2),
זֶהוּ הַהַשָּׁקָה לַמַּעְיָין
this being the mystic kiss/confluence (hashakah) to the spring
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה).
(and as written in Shir HaShirim Rabbah).
וּלְכָךְ, שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאוֹתָם
Therefore, Hashem's dwelling amidst the children of Israel even in the midst of their impurities
אֵינוֹ קָרוּי גָּלוּת כְּאִישׁ נוֹדֵד מִמְּקוֹמוֹ;
is not termed exile in the sense of a man wanderer from his home;
דְּהַגַּם דִּמְקוֹמוֹ מְקוֹם טָהֳרָה "כְּעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר",
for even though His pristine place is pure 'like the very heavens for clearness,'
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
unlike the coarse physical lower world,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִיָּד שֶׁהַלְּבָבוֹת נִדְבָּקִים לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
nevertheless the moment Jewish hearts cleave to Hashem, blessed be He,
שָׁבִים גַּם הֵם לִמְקוֹם טָהֳרָה.
they too immediately return to a place of purity.
וְזֶהוּ "טֻמְאֹתָם" דַּיְיקָא –
And this is why Scripture precisely says 'their impurities'—
אֶצְלָם מִצִּידָּם נִקְרָא טֻמְאָה,
meaning from their human perspective it is termed impurity,
אֲבָל אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר סְתָם "בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאָה",
yet Scripture does not say generically 'in the midst of impurity,'
דְּמִיָּד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן אֵין כָּאן טֻמְאָה.
for the moment Hashem dwells, impurity ceases to exist.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קמו.):
And along the lines of what they stated (Shabbat 146a):
"בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָתָן",
"At the time of the Giving of the Torah their defilement ceased,"
וְהוּא לְעוֹלָם בִּמְקוֹם טָהֳרָתוֹ.
and He remains eternally in His place of purity.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַטִּפּוּל בְּלֵב מְלָכִים וְשָׂרִים
In contrast, occupying Himself with the heart of gentile kings and ministers
הוּא נִקְרָא נְדִידָה מִמְּקוֹמוֹ, מְקוֹם טָהֳרָה וּנְקִיּוּת מִתַּאֲווֹת וְכָל טִנּוּפֶת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
is termed wandering from His place of purity and detachment from the lusts and filth of this world,
וְלִבָּם מָלֵא בֶּאֱמֶת מִכָּל מִינֵי טֻמְאָה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ טָהֳרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל –
since their heart is genuinely full of every kind of irremediable impurity as mentioned above—
זֶה נִקְרָא גָּלוּת.
this is what is truly called exile.
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֵּירְשׁוּ זֶה הַסּוֹד
And our Sages of blessed memory explained this mystical secret
בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א וְאֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג, י; מִדְרָשׁ אַבָּא גּוּרְיוֹן א, טו):
in what they taught (Zohar III 109a; Esther Rabbah 3:10; Midrash Abba Gurion 1:15):
"כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר 'הַמֶּלֶךְ' סְתָם בִּמְגִילַּת אֶסְתֵּר – בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר".
"Wherever 'the king' is stated without qualification in the Scroll of Esther, Scripture speaks of the King of kings."
כִּי בְּכָל הַמְּגִילָּה לֹא נִזְכַּר שׁוּם שֵׁם מִשְּׁמוֹת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
For throughout the entire Megillah not a single one of the holy Names of God is explicitly mentioned,
הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יד.):
which aligns with what our Sages said (Megillah 14a):
"אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן",
"'We are still servants of Ahasuerus,'"
וְאֵין כָּאן הִתְגַּלּוּת שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם.
and there is no overt revelation of Heaven's Name here.
רַק דְּזֶה נִגְלָה דְּלֶב מְלָכִים וְשָׂרִים בְּיַד ה',
Only that this reality was unveiled: that the heart of kings and ministers is in Hashem's hand,
דְּנִתְגַּלָּה סוֹד זֶה שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁגָּלוּ גָּלְתָה שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם,
revealing the secret that wherever they were exiled, the Shechinah was exiled with them,
שֶׁלְּמָדוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי תַּעֲנִית פֶּרֶק א הֲלָכָה ג)
which our Sages deduced (Yerushalmi Ta'anit 1:3)
עַל גָּלוּת פָּרַס מִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (יִרְמְיָה מט, לח):
concerning the Persian exile from the verse (Jeremiah 49:38):
"וְשַׂמְתִּי כִסְאִי בְעֵילָם, וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר",
"'And I will set My throne in Elam, and will destroy, etc.,'"
וּמִקְרָא זֶה דְּרָשׁוּהוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּמְגִילָּה (י סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) עַל וַשְׁתִּי וְהָמָן.
and this verse was expounded in the first chapter of Megillah (10b) as referring to Vashti and Haman.
דְּאָז נִתְגַּלָּה עִנְיַן גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה בְּלֵב מְלָכִים,
For then was revealed the exile of the Shechinah within the hearts of gentile monarchs,
שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לָקַחַת לְבָבוֹ בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַנִּיחוֹ לְהִתְנַהֵג רַק כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
wherein He was required to hold the king's heart in His hand so as not to allow him to act except according to Hashem's will.
וּכְעֵין הַנְהָגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּשְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And this parallels Hashem's governance through His Shechinah within the hearts of the children of Israel,
דְּאֵין מַנִּיחָם לְנַתֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלָל,
whom He never permits to become severed from Him at all,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּבְחֵמָה שְׁפוּכָה אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם".
as it is written (Ezekiel 20:33): 'And with fury poured out will I rule over you.'
כִּי זֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ זוּטָא פֶּרֶק ט):
For what they said (Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta, chapter 9):
"אִם יַגְדִּיל אָדָם עֲבֵירוֹת זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ וְכוּלֵי",
"If a man multiplies transgressions one upon another, etc.,"
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין מַנִּיחוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת כָּל כָּךְ עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לָשׁוּב עוֹד,
means that Hashem prevents him from sinning to such an extent that he could never repent,
כִּי חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ חֶלְקוֹ וְנַחֲלָתוֹ,
for 'Hashem's portion is His people,' His allotted heritage,
כְּנַחֲלָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יב:),
like an inheritance that has no end (Rosh Hashanah 12b),
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתֵּק
and it is impossible to sever;
וְהוּא מַנְהִיג הַלֵּב מַמָּשׁ וְלִבָּם בְּיָדוֹ.
and He guides the heart directly, their heart being in His hand.
וְכָךְ בַּגָּלוּת הֵם לִבְבוֹת מַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת בְּיָדוֹ מַמָּשׁ
And likewise in exile, the hearts of pagan kings are literally held in His hand
שֶׁלֹּא יַנְהִיג כְּלָל כִּרְצוֹנוֹ,
so that the king cannot govern according to his own malicious will at all;
הֲגַם דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אוֹיֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר מֵהָמָן
even though Ahasuerus was an enemy of Israel even more hostile than Haman,
כִּמְשַׁל רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יד.) דְּבַעַל הַתֵּל וְהֶחָרִיץ,
as in the Sages' parable (Megillah 14a) of the owner of the mound and the owner of the pit,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּעָלְכָרְחוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּטוֹבָתוֹ הֵיטִיב לָהֶם,
nonetheless, against his will and without good intention, he favored them;
וְגַם זָעַף עַל אֶסְתֵּר וּבָא מַלְאָךְ וְכוּלֵי כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
and he also raged at Esther until an angel came, etc., as our Sages expounded
(אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ו וְיַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי שָׁם).
(Esther Rabbah 6; Yalkut Shimoni there).
וְהוּא הַכֹּל מַה שֶּׁלְּבָבוֹ בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And this was entirely because his heart was in the hand of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְכָל מָקוֹם "הַמֶּלֶךְ" סְתָם – בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
And every unqualified occurrence of 'the king' points to the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
הֲגַם דִּמְבוֹאָר בִּפְשַׁט הַכָּתוּב דִּבְאַחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ מְדַבֵּר,
even though the plain meaning of the text clearly speaks of Ahasuerus,
כְּמוֹ "יָבוֹא הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהָמָן אֶל הַמִּשְׁתֶּה" וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
such as 'Let the king and Haman come to the banquet,' and similar verses,
רַק הוּא מִצַּד הַהִתְלַבְּשׁוּת בְּגָלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה.
only that it refers through the divine enclothement during the exile of the Shechinah.
וְכָל דִּבּוּרֵי אֶסְתֵּר הָיָה אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
And all of Esther's words were secretly addressed to the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יד: טו.):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Megillah 14b, 15a):
שֶׁלְּבָשַׁתְהוּ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
that the Holy Spirit clothed her,
מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ הַנִּקְרָאת מַלְכוּת,
which is this specific sefirotic level called Malchut,
דְּהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָהּ,
which is the revelation of His Shechinah within her heart,
וְכִי רַק הוּא לְבַדּוֹ שׁוֹכֵן בְּכָל קַצְוֵי אֶרֶץ,
perceiving that He alone abides across all ends of the earth,
וְאֵין עוֹד מַמָּשׁ,
and there is literally none else,
שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר מַמָּשִׁי כְּלָל זוּלָתוֹ,
there being no substantial reality at all apart from Him,
רַק הַנְהָגַת מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְבַד.
only the sovereign governance of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, alone.
וְכֵן כָּל הַסִּפּוּרִים בַּמְּגִילָּה, בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "הַמֶּלֶךְ" סְתָם,
And likewise in all the narratives of the Megillah, wherever 'the king' is stated without qualification,
הַמַּשְׂכִּיל יָבִין
the insightful person will understand
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה נִתְגַּלָּה בְּנֵס פּוּרִים,
that this truth was revealed during the miracle of Purim:
שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ סְתָם הוּא מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים.
that 'the king' unspecified is the King of kings.
וְשֵׁם זֶה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִתְגַּלָּה בְּפוּרִים,
And this specific title of Hashem was revealed on Purim,
דְּגַם מַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לִבָּם בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
demonstrating that even the heart of pagan kings is in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He.
דָּבָר זֶה נִתְגַּלָּה לְעֵין כֹּל בְּפוּרִים,
This reality was openly demonstrated before all eyes on Purim,
דְּהַגַּם דַּ"עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן",
that even though 'we are still servants of Ahasuerus,'
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָנוּ עַבְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם בְּהִשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּת זֶה דִּלְאַחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
we are nonetheless servants of Hashem even in this outward subservience to Ahasuerus,
(עֶזְרָא ט, ט) "וּבְעַבְדֻתֵנוּ [לֹא עֲזָבָנוּ אֱלֹהֵינוּ] וְגוֹמֵר".
(Ezra 9:9): 'Yet in our servitude our God has not forsaken us, etc.'
וְהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר זֶה הוּא בְּכָל פּוּרִים
And the revelation of this spiritual light returns every Purim
וּבִכְלַל הַחוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר,
and throughout the entire month of Adar in general,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּעֲנִית כט:):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Ta'anit 29b):
"הַאי מַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ דִּינָא בַּהֲדֵי [נָכְרִי] וְכוּלֵי",
"One who has litigation with a gentile, let him seek judgment in Adar, etc.,"
כִּי מִשְׁפְּטֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הוּא מִצַּד הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם,
for the judicial powers of the nations derive from their earthly kingdom,
וְאָז מִתְגַּלֶּה דְּגַם מַלְכוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and during Adar it is revealed that their kingdom is likewise in the hand of Hashem,
הַיְינוּ בְּיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל,
which means in the hands of Israel,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָם בֶּאֱמֶת
in whose hearts Hashem truly dwells,
וּמַנְהִיג גַּם כֵּן לִבְבוֹת מַלְכֵי הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת כִּרְצוֹנָם.
and directs the hearts of pagan kings according to Israel's true desire.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חוֹדֶשׁ אָב שֶׁהוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ,
In contrast to the month of Av which is the exact opposite,
דְּהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַגָּלוּת,
being the starting point of exile,
שֶׁלֹּא נִגְלָה עֲדַיִן דָּבָר זֶה דְּגָלְתָה שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם;
wherein it was not yet revealed that the Shechinah had been exiled along with them;
שֶׁגִּילּוּי דָּבָר זֶה הוּא אַתְחַלְתָּא דִּגְאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה.
for the revelation of this reality constitutes the beginning of complete redemption.
וּמִיָּד סָמוּךְ לַאֲדָר הוּא נִיסָן,
And immediately adjacent to Adar is the month of Nisan,
"מִסְמַךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִגְאוּלָּה" (מְגִילָּה ו:),
to 'juxtapose redemption to redemption' (Megillah 6b),
דִּבְנִיסָן עֲתִידִין לְהִגָּאֵל גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה.
for in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed in the ultimate, complete redemption.

sections.en: Purim and the Final Divine Attribute

items.h: Purim reveals Malchut, the final divine attribute, showing that even at the lowest level and without conscious knowledge Israel remains attached to Hashem.

Seif 1 — Purim and Malchut at the Lowest Point
Purim reveals that even at the furthest concealment, Israel remains bound to Hashem beneath conscious awareness.

p: נֵס דְּפוּרִים נִקְרָא בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג דְּיוֹמָא סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים,
The miracle of Purim is called at the beginning of the third chapter of Yoma (29a) 'the end of all miracles,'
כִּי הוּא נַעֲשָׂה בַּמִּדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה מִמִּדּוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
because it was wrought through the final attribute among His attributes, blessed be He.
שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת,
For it is known that there are seven divine emotional attributes (sefirot),
וְשֵׁשׁ מִדּוֹת הֵם נֶגְדָּם שִׁשָּׁה זְמַנִּים הַמְּפוֹרָשִׁים בַּתּוֹרָה:
and facing six of these attributes stand the six sacred seasons explicitly articulated in the Torah:
פֶּסַח, שָׁבוּעוֹת וְסֻכּוֹת יָדוּעַ דְּהֵם נֶגֶד תְּלָת אֲבָהָן;
Passover, Shavuot, and Sukkot are known to correspond to the three Patriarchs (Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet);
וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הֵם נֶגֶד תְּרֵין בַּדֵּי עֲרָבָה;
and Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur correspond to the two willow branches (Netzach and Hod);
וַעֲצֶרֶת, שֶׁהוּא רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן "כְּנִישׁוּ", נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַיְסוֹד
and Shemini Atzeret, which is a festival in its own right and translated into Aramaic as kenishu ('assembly'), corresponds to the attribute of Yesod
שֶׁלְּשָׁם מִתְאַסְּפִין כָּל הַמִּדּוֹת לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
into which all supernal attributes gather to channel the divine influx into the attribute of His Sovereignty (Malchut), blessed be He.
וְאֵלּוּ הַשֵּׁשׁ הֵם מַה דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי".
And these six appointed times are those that 'Israel sanctifies.'
אֲבָל הַשְּׁבִיעִית הִיא קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת דִּ"קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא",
However, the seventh is the sanctity of Shabbat, which is inherently 'fixed and enduring,'
דְּנִקְרָא שַׁבָּת עַל שֵׁם הַשְּׁבִיתָה מִכָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּפְעוּלַת אָדָם
for it is termed Shabbat after cessation from all human exertion and mortal initiative,
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם מָבוֹא בָּזֶה,
wherein they possess no entry or role;
דְּהוּא שׁוֹכֵן גַּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאוֹתָם,
for He abides even in the midst of their defilements,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד.),
and 'even though he has sinned, he remains Israel' (Sanhedrin 44a),
כִּי כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּת זוּגוֹ דְּשַׁבָּת
because the Congregation of Israel is the destined mate of Shabbat,
וְהֵם דְּבוּקִים בְּמִדָּה זוֹ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתְּקָם כְּלָל.
and they cling unto this attribute such that it is utterly impossible to sever them.
כִּי מִדָּה זוֹ נִקְרָא אֱמוּנָה (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רל עַמּוּד א),
For this attribute is termed Faith (Emunah / Malchut; Zohar Part III, 230a),
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים (שַׁבָּת צז.) מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים,
and Israel are called 'believers, the children of believers' (Shabbat 97a),
וְזֶרַע אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יַאֲמִין כְּלָל,
and the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob cannot possibly lack faith entirely,
כִּי זֶהוּ מִצַּד קְדוּשָּׁה דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹךְ לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
because this stems from the sanctity permanently established and enduring from Hashem, blessed be He, within the hearts of the children of Israel.
וּקְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ מִתְגַּלֵּית בְּכָל תּוֹקֶף בְּפוּרִים,
And this sanctity is revealed with ultimate intensity on Purim,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִילָּה ז:): "חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי עַד דְּלָא יָדַע",
where they stated (Megillah 7b): 'A person is obligated to become intoxicated until he knows not,'
דְּהַפֵּירוּשׁ הַפָּשׁוּט בּוֹ הוּא גִּלּוּי דָּבָר זֶה
for the straightforward meaning of this is the revelation of this reality:
דְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּבוּקִים בֶּאֱמֶת בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כְּשֶׁאֵין יוֹדְעִים בֵּין יְמִינָם לִשְׂמֹאלָם.
that the hearts of the children of Israel are truly cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He, even when they know not between their right and their left.
וּבִשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָדָם נִיכָּר (עֵירוּבִין סה:):
And in three things a person is recognized (Eruvin 65b):
בְּכוֹסוֹ וּבְשִׁכְרוּתוֹ,
in his cup and in his drunkenness,
שֶׁאָז אֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה שְׁלֵימָה לְהַסְתִּיר וּלְהַעֲלִים מַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ.
since at that moment he lacks conscious control to disguise and conceal the depths of his heart.
וְאָז מִתְגַּלֶּה מַה שֶּׁהוּא תּוֹךְ מַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב,
And then what resides within the heart's innermost depth is laid bare,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח.): "נִכְנַס יַיִן יָצָא סוֹד"
as they said (Sanhedrin 38a): 'Wine entered, the secret came out'
וְנִתְגַּלָּה,
and was unveiled,
דְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
revealing that the depth of the heart of the children of Israel cleaves to Hashem, blessed be He,
בְּלִי שׁוּם יִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת וּכְפִיָּה לִרְצוֹן הַלֵּב,
without any deliberate calculation or forced subjugation of the heart's desire;
רַק נְקוּדַּת הָרָצוֹן הָאֲמִיתִּית הִיא דְּבוּקָה בֶּאֱמֶת מֵעַצְמָהּ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
rather the authentic, innermost point of will is inherently bonded on its own unto Hashem, blessed be He.
וְעַל יְדֵי מִדָּה זוֹ נַעֲשָׂה הַנֵּס דְּפוּרִים,
And through this divine attribute was the miracle of Purim wrought,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַתִּלְבַּשׁ אֶסְתֵּר מַלְכוּת",
as it is written (Esther 5:1): 'And Esther clothed herself in royalty (Malchut),'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּמָרְדֳּכַי יוֹשֵׁב בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ", "וַיָּשָׁב מָרְדֳּכַי אֶל שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ".
and as written: 'and Mordechai sat in the king's gate,' 'and Mordechai returned to the king's gate.'
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמִדָּה זוֹ נִקְרֵאת "תַּרְעָא לְאַעֲלָא גּוֹ מְהֵימְנוּתָא" (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א, ה עַמּוּד ב; יא עַמּוּד ב),
And it is known that this attribute is termed 'the gate to enter into faith' (Zohar Part I, 5b; 11b),
וְעָלֶיהָ נֶאֱמַר: "זֶה הַשַּׁעַר לַה' וְגוֹמֵר".
and concerning it Scripture declares: 'This is the gate of Hashem, etc.'
וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה טז.) עַל פָּסוּק "וַיָּשָׁב מָרְדֳּכַי" – שֶׁשָּׁב וְכוּלֵי.
And so our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Megillah 16a) on the verse 'and Mordechai returned'—that he returned to his sackcloth and fasting.
דִּתְפִלָּה הוּא מִמַּדְרֵגָה זוֹ
For prayer derives from this specific spiritual rung,
כְּטַעַם "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד.
mirroring 'and I am prayer' (Psalms 109:4), which is the rung of David (Malchut).
כִּי "אַתָּה" נִקְרָא שֵׁירוּתָא,
For 'You' (Attah / direct presence) is designated as the beginning,
וְהוּא הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח בְּפֶסַח דְּ"רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה וְכוּלֵי".
and that was the open perception of the divine Presence on Passover when 'a maidservant saw, etc.'
וְ"אֲנִי" הוּא מִדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה,
While 'I' (Ani) represents the final attribute,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ לִבּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ
wherein Hashem, blessed be He, abides literally within the hearts of the children of Israel,
עַד שֶׁהַנָּבִיא יוּכַל לוֹמַר בְּפִיו "אֲנִי ה'",
to the extent that the prophet can articulate with his mouth 'I am Hashem,'
כִּי הוּא עַצְמוֹ לְבָבוֹ הוּא מִשְׁכַּן כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
because he himself, his very heart, serves as the tabernacle of His glory, blessed be He.
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ הַתְּפִלָּה,
And from this prayer is drawn forth;
דְּלָכֵן תִּקְּנוּ מִקּוֹדֶם "אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח וְגוֹמֵר",
which is why they instituted beforehand: 'O Lord, open my lips, etc.,'
וּבְשֵׁם הָאֲדֹנוּת,
specifically using the divine Name of Adonut (Mastery),
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר מִדַּת אֲדוֹנוּתוֹ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
signifying the attribute of His mastership and sovereignty within the lower realms;
דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֶלָּא כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פּוֹתֵחַ חַדְרֵי לְבָבוֹ וּפוֹתֵחַ שְׂפָתָיו בִּתְפִלָּה,
for it is impossible to pray unless Hashem unlocks the chambers of one's heart and opens his lips in prayer,
וְלוּלֵי זֶה אֵין מְצִיאוּת לִתְפִלָּה בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל.
and without this there is no authentic existence of prayer whatsoever.
דְּלָכֵן נִקְרָא בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (סוֹף תִּיקּוּן יג): "בְּרַתָּא דְּמַלְכָּא דָּא צְלוֹתָא",
Therefore it is designated in Tikkunei Zohar (end of Tikkun 13): 'The daughter of the King—this is prayer,'
כְּמוֹ בַּת מֶלֶךְ שֶׁאֵין הַמֶּלֶךְ מַנִּיחָהּ לָלֶכֶת לְבַדָּהּ.
like a king's daughter whom the monarch never permits to walk unescorted.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא כִּוֵּון לִבּוֹ דְּאָז מִתְפַּלֵּל וְנַעֲנָה.
And this is what is termed 'he directed his heart,' wherein he prays and is answered.
פֵּירוּשׁ "לִבּוֹ" – הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
The meaning of 'his heart' is the Holy One, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלִבִּי עֵר".
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2) on the verse 'and my heart is awake.'
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת ל.): "יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים",
And similarly they stated (Berakhot 30a): 'He shall direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies,'
דְּפֵירוּשׁ הַפָּשׁוּט שֶׁהַלֵּב מְכֻוָּון נֶגֶד קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁשָּׁם שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
where the direct meaning is that his heart is aligned facing the Holy of Holies where His Shechinah rests,
וְאָז הַלֵּב עוֹמֵד מְכֻוָּון וּמְיוּשָּׁר לִתְפִלָּה.
and then the heart stands properly aligned and oriented for prayer.
דְּלוּלֵי כֵן גַּם הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הֵם מִתְפַּלְּלִים,
For otherwise, the idolaters also pray,
אֶלָּא דְּהֵם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִתְפִלָּה מִצַּד לְבָבָם
except that they have no intrinsic attachment to prayer by virtue of their heart,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לִשְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּלָל.
which possesses no connection to the dwelling of Hashem's Shechinah whatsoever.
וְזֶה הָיָה טָעוּת בִּלְעָם בְּקָרְבְּנוֹת דְּבָלָק,
And this was the tragic error of Balaam in the sacrifices of Balak,
שֶׁחָשַׁב עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה יִפְעַל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
in that he presumed he could effect results from Hashem through prayer,
וְלֹא יָדַע דְּאֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת תְּפִלָּה אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
not knowing that the capacity for prayer belongs exclusively to Israel.
רַק מִצַּד תְּפִלָּתוֹ שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
Only through the universal prayer of King Solomon, peace be upon him,
דְּגַם הַגּוֹי כְּשֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל אֶל בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ יֵעָנֶה,
that even the foreigner when praying toward the Holy Temple would be answered,
נִיתַּן קְצָת כֹּחַ,
was some slight spiritual efficacy granted;
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א וּמִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תְּרוּמָה ט):
in accordance with what our Sages of blessed memory stated (Vayikra Rabbah 1; Midrash Tanchuma, Terumah 9):
"אִלְמָלֵי הָיוּ הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת יוֹדְעִין כַּמָּה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ יָפֶה לָהֶם וְכוּלֵי",
"'Had the idolaters known how good the Temple was for them, etc.'"
כִּי זֶה כָּל עִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ:
for this is the entire purpose of the Holy Temple:
לִהְיוֹת שְׁכִינָה קְבוּעָה וְקַיָּימָא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גָּלוּי לְעֵין כֹּל, אַף לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
that the Shechinah dwell permanently established in this world, manifest to the eyes of all, even the nations of the world.
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיָנָיו שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּנְשִׂיאַת נָשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת,
And this was the overarching design of King Solomon, peace be upon him, in marrying foreign women,
שֶׁהוּא רָצָה שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ כֻּלָּם כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתְךָ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד.
desiring that all humanity recognize the power of Your sovereignty as will unfold in the ultimate future.
וְזֶה טַעַם תְּפִלָּתוֹ זוֹ:
And this was the rationale of his prayer:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גַּם לַגּוֹיִם הַכָּרָה בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
that even the gentiles should possess an awareness of the holiness of the Temple,
שֶׁיִּפְנוּ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֵלָיו,
so that they would turn to pray toward it,
עַד שֶׁמִּכֹּחַ הַכָּרָה זוֹ יִהְיֶה לָהֶם קְצָת כֹּחַ בִּתְפִלָּה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נַעֲנִים.
such that by virtue of that recognition they would hold some measure of power in prayer to be answered.
וּבְעֵת חוּרְבַּן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
Yet during the destruction of the Temple,
דְּהַגָּלוּת הוּא הֶעְדֵּר הַכָּרַת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת זֶה,
where exile represents the total loss of that perception among the nations,
מִמֵּילָא אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת תְּפִלָּה כְּלָל, רַק לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
prayer naturally has no connection to them whatever, remaining exclusive to the children of Israel.
וּבְפוּרִים הָיָה גַּם כֵּן קְצָת הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר לָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
And on Purim there was likewise a partial disclosure of illumination toward the nations,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְרַבִּים מֵעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מִתְיַהֲדִים וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is written (Esther 8:17): 'And many from among the peoples of the land became Jews, etc.,'
וְאוֹמֵר: "לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה [אוֹרָה וְשִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשֹׂן] וִיקָר",
and Scripture states: 'For the Jews there was light and gladness, and joy and honor,'
וְדָרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה טז:): "אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ",
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Megillah 16b): 'This refers to the tefillin of the head,'
דְּ"רָאוּ כָּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כִּי שֵׁם [ה' נִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ] וְגוֹמֵר".
fulfilling 'And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of Hashem is called upon you, etc.'
וְהַיְינוּ רְאִיָּה זוֹ דְּשֵׁם ה' נִקְרָא עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And that refers to this external perception—that the Name of Hashem is invoked upon the children of Israel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי נָפַל פַּחַד הַיְּהוּדִים עֲלֵיהֶם",
as written: 'for the fear of the Jews fell upon them,'
שֶׁלֹּא הִשִּׂיגוּ שׁוּם הַשָּׂגָה מִגִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
since they did not achieve any inner comprehension of the revelation of His Shechinah,
דְּזֶה הָיָה אָז בְּהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל
because this was then veiled in profound concealment;
וְאֵין שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם נִזְכָּר בַּמְּגִילָּה כְּלָל,
and indeed the divine Name of Heaven is not explicitly mentioned anywhere in the Megillah,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת וּפִרְסוּם אֱלֹהוּת לָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
there being no overt revelation and publication of divinity to the idolaters,
רַק פִּרְסוּם גַּדְלוּת הַיְּהוּדִים אֵיךְ הֵם מוּשְׁגָּחִים בְּהַנְהָגָה עֶלְיוֹנָה.
only the public demonstration of the Jews' elevated stature, showing how they are miraculously guided by supernal providence.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד,
For in ultimate truth, the actual dwelling of Hashem's Shechinah is exclusively within the hearts of the Jewish people,
וְשַׁבָּת הוּא "אוֹת בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל",
and Shabbat is 'a sign between Me and the children of Israel,'
וְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁשָּׁבַת חַיָּיב מִיתָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין נח:).
and an idolater who observes Shabbat is liable to the death penalty (Sanhedrin 58b).
כִּי עִנְיַן הַשְּׁבִיתָה וְהֶעְדֵּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הוּא מִצַּד הַכָּרָה דִּפְעוּלַת אָדָם אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם, רַק הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the essence of resting and renouncing human exertion stems from the realization that mortal effort is nothing, everything being solely from Hashem,
וְזֶה חַיּוּתָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and this consciousness is the very life-force of Israel;
וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ מִיתָתָן שֶׁל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
whereas this very concept constitutes the spiritual demise of idolaters,
דְּכָל חַיּוּתָם הוּא מִצַּד הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּפְעוּלַת אָדָם וְהֶעְדֵּר הַהַכָּרָה,
since their entire vitality is predicated upon mortal striving, human initiative, and the absence of divine recognition,
אֲבָל מִיָּד שֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה דָּבָר זֶה דְּהַכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְשֶׁאֵין מָבוֹא לִפְעוּלַת אָדָם – אָז נֶעְדַּר חַיּוּתָם.
so the moment this truth of Hashem's omnipotence is disclosed, demonstrating that human striving has no absolute role, their vitality is annihilated.
וְכֵן הָיָה מִיתַת בְּכוֹרִים דְּמִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי מוֹרָא גָּדוֹל – זוֹ גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה,
And thus was the death of the Egyptian firstborn brought about through 'great terror'—which denotes the overt revelation of the Shechinah;
וּמִצַּד זֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן הֲרִיגַת הַשּׂוֹנְאִים וּמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק דְּפוּרִים.
and from this very perspective emerged the destruction of the enemies and the blotting out of Amalek on Purim.
כִּי עִנְיַן עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים כִּכְּרֵי כֶסֶף לִשְׁקוֹל אֶל גִּנְזֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ,
For the meaning of weighing out ten thousand talents of silver into the treasuries of the king—
דְּמֶלֶךְ סְתָם בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְדַבֵּר,
wherein 'the king' unspecified refers to the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He—
הַיְינוּ כִּי הָמָן טָעַן "יֶשְׁנוֹ עַם אֶחָד" – יָשְׁנוּ מִן הַמִּצְווֹת כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יג:).
was that Haman slandered: 'there is (yeshno) one nation'—meaning they have slept (yashnu) from the commandments, as our Sages expounded (Megillah 13b).
רַק בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב):
Yet in truth our Sages stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2):
"אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה מִן הַמִּצְווֹת כו' וְלִבִּי עֵר לַעֲשׂוֹתָן",
'I sleep from the commandments, etc., but my heart is awake to perform them,'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת יז.): "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי וּמִי מְעַכֵּב וְכוּלֵי",
and as they said (Berakhot 17a): 'It is revealed and known that our true will is [to do Your will], but what hinders us? [The leaven in the dough],'
כִּי אֲמִיתַּת נְקוּדַּת הָרָצוֹן דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, רַק יֵצֶר הָרָע מְעַכֵּב.
for the true inner point of will is bound to Hashem, blessed be He, only the evil inclination deters.
וְטָעַן הָמָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מְחִיר לָתֵת נֶגֶד הַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גַּם כֵּן כֹּחַ זֶה:
And Haman asserted that he had an equivalent price to tender counter to the Jews, claiming that he too possessed this spiritual power;
"כֶּסֶף" פֵּירוּשׁ רָצוֹן וְחֶמְדָּה,
for kesef (silver) signifies yearnful desire and longing (kosef),
וְכַיָּדוּעַ דְּכֶסֶף דַּרְגָּא דְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and as is known, silver is the spiritual rung of Abraham who is the inception of Israel's root,
וְיֵשׁ לוֹ גַּם כֵּן הַתְחָלַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה.
and he alleged that he likewise shared this primal root.
וְזֶה כָּל כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו "פּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו וְכוּלֵי טָהוֹר אֲנִי" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה סה),
And this is the entire deceitful power of Esau 'extending his hooves, etc., claiming: I am pure' (Bereishit Rabbah 65),
שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁגַּם הוּא טָהוֹר כְּמוֹהֶם.
alleging that he was just as unblemished as they.
וַ"עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים" – כִּי אֶלֶף הוּא מִסְפַּר הָרִיבּוּי
And he offered 'ten thousand'—because one thousand is the archetype of multitude,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן עַל פָּסוּק "נָתַתִּי אֶלֶף כֶּסֶף",
as the Ramban wrote on the verse 'I have given a thousand pieces of silver,'
וְיָדוּעַ דְּכָל דָּבָר מִתְחַלֵּק לְעֶשֶׂר
and it is known that every entity is subdivided into ten,
וְנִמְצָא עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים תַּכְלִית רִיבּוּי הַשְּׁלֵימוּת.
so that ten thousand represents the absolute zenith of expansive perfection.
וַעֲמָלֵק בָּא בְּעֵת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַעֲלָה עֶלְיוֹנָה,
And Amalek attacked specifically when Israel stood at the highest spiritual pinnacle,
הָיָה פְּשִׁיטוּת טְלָפָיו לוֹמַר שֶׁגַּם הוּא בְּמַעֲלָה כְּמוֹהֶם,
