and his displaying of hooves was designed to assert that he too held a lofty rank equivalent to theirs,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק מד וּפְסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי פָּרָשָׁה יב):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 44; Pesikta Rabbati 12):
בָּא בְּכֹחוֹ שֶׁל זְקֵינוֹ וְכוּלֵי
he arrived boasting in the power of his grandfather (Esau), etc.,
בְּהַשָּׂגָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
in intellect and human exertion;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיְזַנֵּב וְגוֹמֵר",
and as it is written (Deuteronomy 25:18): 'and he cut off the hindmost of you, etc.,'
וְכָל נִיצּוּחַ הוּא עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁפָּט,
and every spiritual triumph proceeds through strict judicial balance;
וַדַּאי הָיָה הוּא נָקִי בָּזֶה.
and he surely presented himself as blameless in this regard.
וּלְכָךְ מְנַצְּחוֹ הָיָה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף
Therefore his conqueror was Joshua from the seed of Joseph,
שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וְנִיצּוּחַ הַיֵּצֶר.
who represents the foundational power of holy exertion and overcoming the base inclination.
וְנֶאֱמַר רַק "וַיַּחֲלֹשׁ", וְלֹא נִיצּוּחַ גָּמוּר,
Yet it is merely stated: 'And Joshua weakened (vayachalosh) [Amalek],' not a total eradication,
רַק "לְפִי חָרֶב" – בְּפֶה שֶׁל הַחֶרֶב נָגַע בָּהֶם.
rather 'according to the edge of the sword'—touching them at the very mouth (peh) of the sword.
פֵּירוּשׁ: "פֶּה" הוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
The explanation is: 'mouth' embodies the outward disclosure of that which is in the heart,
כִּי בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַיָּדַיִם אֵין נִיכָּר הִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבַּלֵּב, רַק בַּפֶּה.
for through manual action alone the heart's inner motivation is not fully manifest, only through the mouth.
שְׁנֵי מִינֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הֵם: בַּתּוֹרָה וּבַמִּצְווֹת;
There are two forms of spiritual exertion: in Torah and in mitzvot;
וּמִצְווֹת יֵשׁ בָּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לְמַרְאִית עַיִן,
and superficial observance of mitzvot exists among idolaters to outward appearance,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא י:) עַל פָּסוּק "בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ",
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Bava Batra 10b) on the verse 'when its boughs are withered,'
וּקְרָאוּם "מִקְצָת מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת",
and they designated these 'a few light commandments,'
כִּי הֵם קַלּוֹת מְאֹד לִדְחוֹתָם,
because they are exceedingly flimsy and easily cast aside,
לְפִי שֶׁעִיקַּר כֹּבֶד וִיקַר הַמִּצְוָה הוּא מִצַּד הַכַּוָּנָה וּרְצוֹן הַלֵּב,
since the true weight and preciousness of a mitzvah derive from inward intention and heartfelt desire;
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם קְרוּיִים מִצְווֹת.
yet nevertheless they are termed mitzvot.
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
However, Torah holds no connection to idolaters,
וְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁלָּמַד תּוֹרָה חַיָּיב מִיתָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין נט.),
and an idolater who studies Torah is liable to death (Sanhedrin 59a),
וְ"הָאוֹמֵר יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה בַּגּוֹיִם – אַל תַּאֲמֵן" (אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי ב, ט).
and 'if one says to you: there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it' (Eichah Rabbah 2:9).
וְהָמָן הָיָה בְּעֵת שֵׁינָה מֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
Now Haman attacked during a period of Israel's dormancy from active exertion;
וְ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" גַּם הוּא טַעֲנָתוֹ מִצַּד דְּגַם הוּא דָּבוּק בִּרְצוֹנוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and corresponding to 'one opposite the other,' his argument was framed claiming that he too was bound in his true desire to Hashem, blessed be He,
וּמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ כֵּן הוּא מִפְּנֵי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
and that whatever fell short in him was solely due to the external evil inclination.
וְעַל זֶה נִתְחַיֵּיב מִטַּעַם עַכּוּ"ם שֶׁשָּׁבַת;
And on this premise he incurred guilt under the principle of an idolater who observes Shabbat;
כִּי דְּבֵיקוּת בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הוּא רַק לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for essential cleaving without dependent exertion belongs exclusively to the children of Israel,
וְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת יֵשׁ לָהֶם רַק שְׂכַר מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
whereas idolaters receive reward merely for superficial, light commandments, as mentioned above.
וְנִתְגַּלָּה בְּפוּרִים דְּ"נַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא אֲשֶׁר וְגוֹמֵר",
And on Purim it was unveiled that 'it was turned to the contrary, that [the Jews had rule over those who hated them],' (Esther 9:1),
שֶׁלִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ כֹּחַ, הֲגַם דִּישֵׁנִים מִמִּצְווֹת, דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
revealing that the children of Israel possess the intrinsic power that even when asleep from mitzvot, they remain cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶהוּ "סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים" –
And this is the secret of 'the end of all miracles'—
הִתְגַּלּוּת דְּבֵיקוּת זֶה שֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה בְּפוּרִים,
the revelation of this ultimate cleaving which is unveiled on Purim,
דְּגַם אִם נִשְׁתַּקַּע כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּקַּע עַד דְּלָא יָדַע לְגַמְרֵי,
that even if one has sunk as deeply as he may have sunk, reaching 'until he knows not' entirely,
וְתִינוֹק שֶׁנִּטְמַע בֵּין הָעַמִּים שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יְדִיעַת בֵּית רַבּוֹ גַּם כֵּן –
and even a child captured among the nations who possesses no knowledge of his master's house—
אַף הוּא דָּבוּק לְגַמְרֵי בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
he too remains completely bound unto Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי "סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה דָּבוּק בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה",
for 'the end of action is bonded within the initial thought,'
כַּנּוֹדָע דְּ"נָעוּץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן".
as is known: 'their end is wedged in their beginning.'

sections.en: Four Heavenly Gifts and Human Attainment

items.h: Wisdom, joy, success, and wealth reflect distinct heavenly gifts, clarifying what lies in human action and what depends upon divine assistance.

Seif 1 — Wisdom, Joy, Success, and Wealth
Heavenly gifts illuminate the boundary between human effort, revealed action, and the hidden assistance of Hashem.

p: אַרְבָּעָה מִינֵי עִנְיָנִים שֶׁל מַעֲלוֹת וַהֲנָאוֹת וּמַתָּנוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם שֶׁטּוֹב שֶׁנִּיתַּן לוֹ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם הֵם.
Four varieties of virtues, delights, and gifts belonging to man that are favorable gifts bestowed upon him from Heaven exist.
שְׁלֹשָׁה הֵם בָּאָדָם עַצְמוֹ,
Three reside within the person himself,
וְהֵם: חָכְמָה בַּמּוֹחַ,
and they are: wisdom in the brain,
וְשִׂמְחָה בַּלֵּב,
and joy in the heart,
וְהַצְלָחָה בִּכְלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בַּפּוֹעֵל, "כָּל אֲשֶׁר הוּא עֹשֶׂה ה' מַצְלִיחַ בְּיָדוֹ".
and success in practical execution, 'all that he does Hashem makes to prosper in his hand.'
וְהֵם הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב "אַל יִתְהַלֵּל וְגוֹמֵר",
And these correspond to the three concerning which Scripture states: 'Let not [the wise man] glory, etc.,'
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נִדָּה טז:):
and our Sages of blessed memory stated (Niddah 16b):
דְּנִגְזַר בִּשְׁעַת יְצִירָה: "טִיפָּה זוֹ חָכָם אוֹ טִפֵּשׁ, וְעָשִׁיר אוֹ עָנִי" –
that at the moment of conception it is decreed: 'Shall this drop become wise or foolish, wealthy or impoverished?'—
הַיְינוּ הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁזּוֹ עִיקַּר עֲשִׁירוּת,
meaning the joy within the heart, which is the very essence of true wealth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד): "אֵיזֶהוּ עָשִׁיר? הַשָּׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ",
as they stated (Avot 4:1): 'Who is wealthy? He who rejoices in his portion,'
וְאִם יַרְבֶּה כַּחוֹל כֶּסֶף וְאֵין לוֹ שִׂמְחַת הַלֵּב, הוּא קָרוּי עָנִי,
and if a person amasses silver like the sand yet lacks gladness of heart, he is termed poor;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סוֹף פֶּרֶק ח דִּתְרוּמוֹת):
and likewise they said (Yerushalmi Terumot 8:12):
"לִבָּא בְּכִיסָא תַּלְיָא",
'The heart depends upon the purse,'
דְּשַׁלְוַות הַלֵּב תָּלוּי בַּעֲשִׁירוּת.
meaning the tranquility of the heart depends upon wealth.
"וְגִבּוֹר אוֹ חַלָּשׁ" –
'And mighty or weak'—
הַיְינוּ שַׁלְוַות כְּלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, דְּהַגְּבוּרָה הוּא בַּפּוֹעַל.
this refers to the ease of the instruments of action, since might is expressed through physical deed.
וְאָמַר: "אַל יִתְהַלֵּל וְגוֹמֵר",
And Scripture states: 'Let not [the wise man] glory, etc.,'
דְּהַכֹּל בִּגְזֵירָה;
for all these three are preordained by divine decree;
"כִּי אִם בְּזֹאת יִתְהַלֵּל וְגוֹמֵר" –
'but let him that glories glory in this, etc.'—
הַיְינוּ צַדִּיק אוֹ רָשָׁע דְּלָא קָאָמַר (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם).
referring to righteousness or wickedness, which the angel does not declare (as noted there in Niddah).
וְאֵינוֹ דָּבָר מְחוּדָּשׁ,
Nor is this an isolated novelty;
רַק רָצָה לוֹמַר בְּאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה "הַשְׂכֵּל וְיָדוֹעַ אוֹתִי":
rather, Scripture means to say regarding these three: 'that he understands and knows Me'—
הֶחָכָם בְּחָכְמָתוֹ מַכִּיר וְיוֹדֵעַ שֶׁחָכְמָתוֹ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
that the wise man in his wisdom recognizes and knows that his wisdom originates from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְכֵן כֻּלָּם –
and likewise across all three virtues—
אָז יוּכַל לְהִתְהַלֵּל.
only then can he legitimately glory.
כִּי בְּכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ צַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע,
For in each of these facets there exists a righteous manifestation and a wicked one,
דְּאֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה כּוֹלְלִים כָּל קוֹמַת אָדָם:
since these three encompass the entire stature of man:
בְּחָכְמָה יֵשׁ חָכָם בַּתּוֹרָה וְיֵשׁ חָכָם לְהָרַע;
in wisdom there is one wise in Torah, and there is one wise to do evil;
וְכֵן בְּשִׂמְחַת הַלֵּב יֵשׁ שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה וְעָשִׁיר בְּדַעַת,
and likewise in joy of the heart there is the joy of a mitzvah and being rich in spiritual understanding,
וְשִׂמְחָה שֶׁל הוֹלֵלוּת וְתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת שֶׁמְּמַלֵּא כָּל חֲמוּדוֹתָיו בְּעָשְׁרוֹ;
and there is the joy of frivolity and base lusts wherein one indulges all earthly desires with his wealth;
וְכֵן בִּגְבוּרָה יֵשׁ הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ,
and so too in might there is he who conquers his evil inclination,
וְיֵשׁ גְּבוּרַת כַּעַס וּרְצִיחָה.
and there is the destructive might of wrath and murder.
וְזֶהוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה כְּתָרִים,
And these correspond to the three crowns,
"וְכֶתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב עוֹלֶה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶם" (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד מִשְׁנָה יג):
'and the crown of a good name surpasses them all' (Avot 4:13):
דְּשֵׁם טוֹב הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעִיד עָלָיו שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם,
for a good name represents that which Hashem, blessed be He, testifies regarding him that his intention is directed purely toward Heaven,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "רְאוּ קָרָאתִי בְשֵׁם וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is written (Exodus 31:2): 'See, I have called by name, etc.,'
שֶׁלָּמְדוּ בְּפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (נה.):
which they deduced in the chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 55a):
מִזֶּה דְּפַרְנָס טוֹב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְמַנֶּה.
from this, that a worthy leader is personally appointed by the Holy One, blessed be He.
וְשֵׁם טוֹב וְכָבוֹד הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְמַנֶּה,
And a good name and honor represent that which Hashem, blessed be He, assigns,
שֶׁהוּא מֵעִיד שֶׁרָאוּי לְכָבוֹד כָּל אֶחָד כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא:
wherein He bears witness that each individual is deserving of honor according to what he is:
יֵשׁ מְכֻבָּד מִצַּד חָכְמָתוֹ
there is one honored on account of his wisdom,
וְיֵשׁ מִצַּד עָשְׁרוֹ וְהוּא כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת,
and there is one honored on account of his wealth, which is the crown of kingship,
וְיֵשׁ מִצַּד גְּבוּרָתוֹ וְהוּא כֶּתֶר כְּהֻנָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה.
and there is one honored on account of his spiritual might, which is the crown of priesthood and divine service.
וְהַכָּבוֹד הוּא הַמַּעֲלָה וּמַתָּנָה הָרְבִיעִית,
And honor is the fourth virtue and gift,
וְהִיא אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ,
and it does not originate from within the person himself,
רַק מִצַּד הַזּוּלַת שֶׁחוֹלְקִין לוֹ כָּבוֹד.
rather from others who accord him honor.
וְכָל כָּבוֹד הוּא בְּהֶכְרֵחַ מִצַּד אֶחָד מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה מַעֲלוֹת הַנִּזְכָּר אוֹ מִצַּד כֻּלָּם,
And all honor necessarily stems from one of the three aforementioned virtues or from all of them together;
וְזֶהוּ "עוֹלֶה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶם",
and this is why it 'surpasses them all'—
כִּי אֵינָהּ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ רַק עַל גַּבֵּיהֶם,
because it does not stand independently but rests directly upon them,
וְהוּא עוֹלֶה עֲלֵיהֶם כִּי זוּלַת זֶה אֵין הֵם מַעֲלוֹת כְּלָל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
and it surpasses them, for without this divine honor they are not true virtues at all, as noted above.
וְהֵם תְּלָת אֲבָהָן,
And these three correspond to the three Patriarchs,
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רֶגֶל רְבִיעִי שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה
and King David, peace be upon him, is the fourth leg of the divine Chariot
כִּי הוּא זָכָה לְשֵׁם טוֹב,
for he merited the crown of a good name,
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר מִדַּת מַלְכוּת,
which is the primary essence of the attribute of Malchut (Sovereignty),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם נח.):
as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Berakhot 58a):
שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין עַל הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ וְגוֹמֵר.
that over a monarch we recite the blessing: 'Who has imparted of His glory, etc.'
אֲבָל כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת שֶׁמִּצַּד עַצְמוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם, מִצַּד הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
However, the crown of royalty that originates from within the person himself, from the joy in the heart,
זֶה דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
this is the spiritual rung of our father Jacob, peace be upon him.
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּפוּרִים: "לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה וְשִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשֹׂן וִיקָר",
And this was manifest on Purim: 'For the Jews there was light and gladness, and joy and honor' (Esther 8:16);
הֵם כָּל אַרְבָּעָה כְּתָרִים הַלָּלוּ:
these represent all four of these crowns:
"אוֹרָה" – זוֹ תוֹרָה (מְגִילָּה טז:) בְּמִקְרָא מְגִילָּה
"'Light'—this is Torah (Megillah 16b), embodied in the public reading of the Megillah,
דְּנִקְרֵאת אֱמֶת כַּאֲמִיתָּהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה,
which is termed Truth like the ultimate veracity of the Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (there):
שֶׁאָז יֵשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת חָכְמַת אֱמֶת בְּמוֹחַ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
that then occurs the disclosure of true wisdom within the intellect of the children of Israel.
"וְשִׂמְחָה" – זוֹ יוֹם טוֹב,
"'Gladness'—this is Yom Tov (the festival),"
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ (שָׁם ה:):
yet our Rabbis of blessed memory noted (Megillah 5b):
"יוֹם טוֹב לֹא קַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ",
"'The prohibition of labor on Yom Tov they did not accept upon themselves,'
וְלָכֵן פֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י עַל יָמִים טוֹבִים אֲחֵרִים,
and therefore Rashi explained that this refers to the reaffirmation of other biblical festivals;
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת:
and both interpretations are truth:
כִּי יוֹם טוֹב בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב אֵינוֹ רָצָה לוֹמַר הַשִּׂמְחָה בַּלֵּב בִּלְבַד,
for 'Yom Tov' in biblical terminology does not signify joy in the heart alone,
שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ "שִׂמְחָה וְגוֹמֵר",
for Scripture explicitly enumerates 'gladness, etc.',
וְיוֹם טוֹב עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּיוֹם טוֹב אֵינוֹ עַל הַשִּׂמְחָה לְבַד, רַק עַל מְנִיעַת עֲשִׂיַּת מְלָאכָה.
and Yom Tov perforce does not denote gladness alone, but the active cessation of performing creative labor.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים יוֹם טוֹב הַיְינוּ עַל הַשִּׂמְחָה בִּלְבַד,
In contrast, in rabbinic idiom, 'Yom Tov' refers directly to pure rejoicing,
כְּמוֹ (שַׁבָּת קיט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א, וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת): "עֲבִידְנָא יוֹמָא טָבָא לְרַבָּנַן",
as in (Shabbat 119a and other sources): 'I will make a festive day for the Rabbis,'
דְּוַדַּאי אֵין רָצָה לוֹמַר בִּיטּוּל מְלָאכָה.
where it certainly does not imply an abstention from work.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהַכָּתוּב הוּא דָּבָר הַמְּפוֹרָשׁ לַכֹּל,
And this is because Scripture deals with that which is explicit to all,
וְיוֹם טוֹב מְפוֹרָשׁ הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִגְלֶה עַל כְּלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה;
and an explicit Yom Tov means that sanctity is visibly enacted upon the instruments of practical action;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ מְפוֹרָשׁ,
whereas the words of the Sages in the Oral Torah pertain to that which is unwritten,
יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְפוֹרָשׁ.
so their Yom Tov is that which is internal rather than explicitly visible.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תְּחִלָּה "וְיוֹם טוֹב",
And this explains why the Megillah initially wrote 'and a Yom Tov,'
רַק דְּלָא קַבִּילוּ,
only that they did not accept the cessation of labor,
וּבְוַדַּאי לֹא עָלָה אֶל לְבָבָם דָּבָר רֵיק שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי לְקַבֵּל
and certainly there did not enter their holy thoughts an empty suggestion unworthy of acceptance,
וְגַם לֹא הָיָה רָאוּי לְהַזְכִּיר זֶה בַּמְּגִילָּה.
nor would it have been fitting to record such a failure in the sacred Megillah;
רַק דְּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא יוֹם טוֹב מִצַּד הַחֲכָמִים,
rather in internal truth it truly is a Yom Tov from the perspective of the Sages,
דְּאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הֵם רֹאשׁ חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנּוֹדָע,
for the Men of the Great Assembly are the leaders of Israel's sages as is known,
דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם וְהַחָכְמָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ יוֹם טוֹב בְּשִׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
meaning from the perspective of concealment and wisdom, it possesses the essential root of Yom Tov in internal heartfelt joy.
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַגִּלּוּי בְּפֵירוּשׁ לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
However, from the perspective of overt, visible revelation to all Israel,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין סו.) עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב: "כְּתוּבָה וּמוּנַּחַת",
along the lines of what they said (Kiddushin 66a) regarding the Written Torah: 'it is written and lying open,'
דְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב נִגְלֶה לַכֹּל וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לַחֲכָמִים,
meaning that what is explicitly written is manifest to everyone without requiring sages,
וְלִהְיוֹת יוֹם טוֹב מְגוּלֶּה לַכֹּל – זֶה לֹא הָיָה;
and to be an overtly evident Yom Tov to all—this was not appropriate;
כִּי נֵס דְּפוּרִים הָיָה בְּהֶעְלֵם מְלוּבָּשׁ בְּדַרְכֵי הַטֶּבַע,
because the miracle of Purim occurred in hiddenness, enclothed in the natural order,
רַק שֶׁהַחֲכָמִים וְהַמַּשְׂכִּילִים יָבִינוּ שֶׁהוּא נֵס גָּמוּר וּגְאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה,
such that only the sages and insightful thinkers understand that it was a total miracle and complete redemption,
אֲבָל לֹא הָיָה בְּגִילּוּי גָּמוּר לְעֵין כָּל בָּשָׂר.
yet it was not overtly revealed before the eyes of all flesh.
וּלְכָךְ יוֹם טוֹב זֶה נִקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "שִׂמְחָה".
Therefore, this unique Yom Tov is designated in biblical phrasing as 'simchah' (gladness).
וְהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן קִיּוּם יָמִים טוֹבִים הָאֲחֵרִים כְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י,
And this also accounts for the reaffirmation of the other festivals as Rashi explained,
כִּי כָּל דָּבָר בִּזְמַנּוֹ אָז הוּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
for each matter in its appointed season is in manifest revelation,
וּמִקּוֹדֶם הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם מוֹשֵׁךְ אוֹתוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה,
while beforehand it draws down that holiness in concealment,
כְּמוֹ בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מִשַּׁבָּת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא.
just as during the six working days vitality is drawn from the permanently established sanctity of Shabbat.
וּבְכָל הֶחֳדָשִׁים מִיּוֹם טוֹב הַקְּדוּשָּׁה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי, דְּהַיְינוּ עוֹנֶג וְשִׂמְחָה,
And across all months, the sanctity sanctified by Israel is drawn from Yom Tov—namely divine delight and joy;
וּבְיוֹם טוֹב הוּא מְפוֹרָשׁ
and on Yom Tov itself it is explicit,
וּבְכָל יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה כָּל שִׂמְחָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ מִקְּדוּשַּׁת יוֹם טוֹב.
whereas throughout the year all joy experienced by man is drawn directly from the sanctity of Yom Tov.
וּבְפוּרִים הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה דְּהַמְשָׁכַת הַשִּׂמְחָה מִיּוֹם טוֹב,
And on Purim occurs the overt revelation of this drawing forth of joy from Yom Tov,
וְהוּא קִיּוּם יָמִים טוֹבִים אֲחֵרִים.
and that is the spiritual fulfillment of the other festivals.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ,
And this is actualized through sending portions one to his fellow,
דְּזֶהוּ דֶּרֶךְ שִׂמְחָה וְשַׁלְוַות הַלֵּב.
which is the authentic way of joy and inner peace of the heart.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר שִׂמְחַת אֱמֶת, כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ לוֹ טוֹבַת עַיִן לְהַהֲנוֹת מֵחֶלְקוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים,
And this is the core of authentic joy: when one possesses a generous eye to give pleasure to others from his own allotted portion,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן צַר עַיִן אֵין קָרוּי עָשִׁיר כְּלָל,
whereas a stingy, narrow-eyed person is not termed rich at all,
כִּי אֵין שָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁעֵינוֹ צָרָה בְּשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים.
since he does not rejoice in his portion because his eye is grudging toward what belongs to others.
"וְשָׂשׂוֹן" – זוֹ מִילָה,
"'And joy (sason)'—this is circumcision (milah),"
הוּא הַהַצְלָחָה בְּמַעֲשֶׂה בִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר,
which represents success in practical action through subduing the evil inclination;
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִצְוַת הַמִּילָה שֶׁעָלֶיהָ אָמַר דָּוִד: "שָׂשׂ אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר",
and this is the root of the commandment of circumcision, concerning which David proclaimed: 'I rejoice [at Your word], etc.' (Psalms 119:162),
שֶׁאֵין הָעָרְלָה קְרוּיָה אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
for uncircumcision is designated solely by the name of idolaters,
אֲבָל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל קְרוּיִים נִימּוֹלִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב נְדָרִים לא:)
while all of Israel are termed circumcised (as written in Nedarim 31b),
כִּי כֻּלָּם גִּבּוֹרֵי כֹּחַ עוֹשֵׂי דְבָרוֹ;
for all are mighty warriors executing His command;
כִּי גַּם רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם רַק מַרְשִׁיעִים כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
since even the sinners of Israel only do wickedness in accordance with Hashem's mysterious plan,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיְּבוֹרַר לֶעָתִיד [אַחַר תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה]
as will be clarified in the ultimate future (after repentance out of love),
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַחֲטָאִים כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת פט:),
that sins will be like these solar years that are prearranged and set since the six days of Creation (as written in Shabbat 89b);
כָּךְ הַחֲטָאִים הַכֹּל מְסוּדָּר מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
so too the transgressions were all orchestrated from the six days of Creation as Hashem willed that Israel undergo.
וְכֵן כָּל עֲבֵירוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם עֲבֵירוֹת לִשְׁמָהּ הַגְּדוֹלוֹת מִמִּצְוֹת שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב נָזִיר כג:),
And so all sins of Israel are 'transgressions for Heaven's sake' that are greater than mitzvot performed not for Heaven's sake (Nazir 23b),
הַיְינוּ מִקְצָת מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת שֶׁעוֹשִׂים הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ,
referring to the sparse, light mitzvot observed by idolaters which are not for Heaven's sake,
כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת לִשְׁמָהּ שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵינוֹ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for it is impossible for theirs to be for Heaven's sake, since it is not the divine will,
דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְצַפֶּה: "בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ תִּשָּׁבַרְנָה".
Hashem anticipating: 'when its boughs wither they will be broken.'
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּבוּקִים בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
However, Israel cling unto the Name of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and all their deeds are intrinsically for the sake of Heaven, only that this remains hidden in this world.
וְעַל זֶה הִיא שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִצְוַת הַמִּילָה,
And upon this rests the root of the commandment of circumcision,
שֶׁהוּא הַכָּרָה בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַהוֹלָדָה שֶׁהֵם רְשׁוּמִים לִשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּשָׁרְשָׁם,
which is the recognition at the very source of procreation that they are inscribed unto the Name of the Holy One in their root;
וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "אִמְרָתֶךָ" – אֲמִירָה בִּלְחִישָׁה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, פח עַמּוּד ב; חֵלֶק א, רלד עַמּוּד ב)
and therefore it is called 'Your word' (imratekha)—speech in a whisper (as written in Zohar III 88b, and I 234b)
שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת.
which is not in outward disclosure.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַשָּׂשׂוֹן,
And over this specifically is the sason (joy),
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר הוֹרָאַת הַמִּלָּה בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ:
which means the significance of the word sason in the Holy Tongue:
הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב לַפּוֹעַל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה.
the active manifestation of the joy of the heart breaking forth into actual deed.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַמִּשְׁתֶּה דְּקַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ אַחַר הַשִּׂמְחָה,
And this occurs through the feast that they accepted upon themselves following gladness,
דְּ"חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי וְכוּלֵי",
namely that 'a person is obligated to become intoxicated, etc.,'
וְהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשִּׂמְחָה לַפּוֹעַל,
which is the actualization of joy into physical reality,
דְּגַם דְּלָא יָדְעֵי בֵּין וְכוּלֵי – הֵם דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם.
demonstrating that even when they know not between good and evil, they remain bound to Hashem in all their actions.
"וִיקָר" – הַיְינוּ כֶּתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב וְכָבוֹד,
"'And honor (yakar)'—this is the crown of a good name and glory,
אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ,
referring to the tefillin of the head,
דְּ"רָאוּ כָּל וְגוֹמֵר",
fulfilling: 'And all [the peoples of the earth] shall see, etc.',
דִּתְפִלִּין אֵינוֹ מִצְוָה בְּעֶצֶם הָאָדָם רַק לְבוּשׁ הַמַּלְבִּישׁ לָאָדָם,
for tefillin is not a mitzvah within the person's essence, but an outer garment adorning man;
וְכֵן הַכָּבוֹד הוּא לְבוּשׁ מִבַּחוּץ.
and likewise honor is an outward vestment from without.
רַק לְבוּשׁ יָקָר דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַתְּפִלִּין,
Only that the precious, honorable garment of Israel is the tefillin,
דְּהַיְינוּ כִּי שֵׁם ה' נִקְרָא עֲלֵיהֶם.
signifying that the Name of Hashem is invoked upon them.
וְהִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה בְּפוּרִים,
And this disclosure occurred on Purim,
כִּי "נָפַל פַּחַד וְגוֹמֵר",
for 'the fear [of the Jews] fell [upon them], etc.,'
עַל יְדֵי מִצְוַת מַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים,
through the mitzvah of gifts to the poor (matanot la'evyonim),
כִּי "מַתַּן אָדָם יַרְחִיב לוֹ, וְלִפְנֵי גְדֹלִים יַנְחֶנּוּ",
for 'a man's gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men' (Proverbs 18:16);
גְּדוֹלִים הַיְינוּ בַּחָכְמָה,
and 'great men' refers to those great in wisdom,
וּ"בְצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכָּסֶף",
for 'in the shadow of wisdom is the shadow of silver' (Ecclesiastes 7:12),
כִּי עִיקַּר הַכָּבוֹד מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה,
since true honor derives from wisdom,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ" –
as it is written: 'The wise shall inherit honor' (Proverbs 3:35)—
כְּנַחֲלָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶקֶת,
like an unending, perpetual inheritance,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פה.):
as they said (Bava Metzia 85a):
"כָּל שֶׁהוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וּבְנוֹ וְכוּלֵי אֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶקֶת",
'Whoever is a Torah scholar, and his son, etc., it never ceases from his seed,'
וּפֵירוּשׁ הוּא וּבְנוֹ וּבֶן בְּנוֹ –
and the meaning of he, his son, and his grandson is:
הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהִיא חָכְמָתוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
namely when his wisdom is in ultimate perfection,
כִּי הָאָב זוֹכֶה לִבְנוֹ בְּחָכְמָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֵדֻיּוֹת סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב),
for a father endows his son with wisdom (Eduyot 2:9),
כִּי הַבֵּן נִמְשָׁךְ מִטִּיפֵּי מוֹחוֹ.
because the son is drawn from the essence of his father's mind.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַחָכְמָה רַק מִשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ וְאֵינוֹ בְּמַעֲמַקָּיו בֶּאֱמֶת, רַק חָכָם לְמַרְאִית עַיִן,
And when wisdom is merely from the lip outward and not in his authentic depths, being wise only to appearance,
אֵינוֹ חָכָם בִּשְׁלֵימוּת וְאֵין בְּנוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
he is not truly wise, and his son will not be a Torah scholar.
וְזֶה טַעַם "שֶׁלֹּא בֵּרְכוּ בַּתּוֹרָה תְּחִלָּה" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב נְדָרִים פא.),
And this explains why 'they did not recite a blessing over the Torah first' (Nedarim 81a),
כִּי הַבְּרָכָה לְפָנֶיהָ הוּא הַכָּרָה דְּהַחָכְמָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for the blessing beforehand is the conscious recognition that wisdom comes from Hashem, blessed be He,
וּבְלָאו הָכִי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דִּמְיוֹן וְחָכְמָה לְמַרְאִית עַיִן לְבַד וְלֹא בֶּאֱמֶת.
and without this, it is merely illusion and superficial wisdom, not truth.
וְיֵשׁ מִמַּעֲמַקִּים תְּרֵין עוּמְקִין דְּאִינּוּן נִסְתָּרוֹת מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא,
And out of the depths there are two depths: the concealments of brain and heart,
וְעוֹמֶק הַשֵּׁנִי נִגְלָה בְּבֶן הַבֵּן;
and the second depth is revealed in the grandson;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַחָכְמָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת בְּכָל מַעֲמַקָּיו, שׁוּב אֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶקֶת, וְהַכָּבוֹד לוֹ לְנַחֲלָה.
and when wisdom is complete throughout all his depths, it never ceases, and honor becomes his enduring heritage.
כִּי כְּבוֹד ה' נִקְרָא הַמִּדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה הַמּוּשֶּׂגֶת לִבְרִיּוֹתָיו
For the glory of Hashem is designated as the final attribute (Malchut) comprehended by His creatures,
שֶׁהֵם מַשִּׂיגִים אֲדוֹנוּתוֹ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ
wherein they perceive His Mastership and Sovereignty,
שֶׁמִּצַּד זֶה הוּא הַכָּבוֹד מִן הַזּוּלַת כַּנּוֹדָע.
from which vantage point honor is accorded by others, as is known.
וּמִדָּה זוֹ עִיקָּרָהּ הוּא כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת,
And this attribute is essentially the crown of royalty,
וְלָכֵן עַל מְלָכִים אוֹמְרִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: "שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ" –
and therefore over kings among Israel we recite: 'Who has imparted of His glory'—
שֶׁמַּלְכוּתָם חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל,
because their kingdom is an actual portion of God from Above;
וּבְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת: "שֶׁנָּתַן מִכְּבוֹדוֹ" –
and over idolaters: 'Who has given of His glory'—
כִּי הֵם בָּשָׂר וָדָם וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לֶאֱלֹהוּת כְּחֵלֶק מִן הַכֹּל וְנִקְרָא נְתִינָה,
for they are flesh and blood and have no intrinsic connection to Godliness as a portion of the Whole, hence it is termed a mere external gift;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא מִכְּבוֹדוֹ
yet nonetheless it derives from His glory,
כִּי "לֶב מְלָכִים וְגוֹמֵר הַכֹּל בְּיַד ה'" כְּמִקּוֹדֶם,
because 'the heart of kings, etc., is all in the hand of Hashem' as mentioned above,
וּכְבוֹדוֹ הוּא הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט.
and His divine glory is what expands forth.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם נֶאֱמַר: "בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ",
Nevertheless it is stated: 'By me kings reign' (Proverbs 8:15),
וּ"מַאן מַלְכֵי? רַבָּנָן" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גִּיטִּין סב.),
and 'Who are kings? The Rabbis' (as written in Gittin 62a),
הַיְינוּ חַכְמֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
meaning the masters of the Oral Torah,
דְּמַלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ, וְחָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה.
for Malchut is the mouth, we title it the Oral Torah, and lower Wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah).
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין "שֶׁחָלַק" וְ"שֶׁנָּתַן" מֵחָכְמָתוֹ,
And this also explains why we recite the blessings 'Who has imparted' and 'Who has given' of His wisdom,
וְאֵין מְבָרְכִים גַּם כֵּן עַל גִּבּוֹר וְעָשִׁיר;
whereas we do not recite an analogous blessing over a mighty man or a rich man;
וּמָצִינוּ גַּם כֵּן תֹּאַר עָשִׁיר עַל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (רֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה) וְכַמָּה פְּעָמִים: "עָשִׁיר וְשָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְכוּלֵי",

and we also find the designation 'rich' attributed to Hashem, blessed be He, in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu (beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah) and several other places: 'rich and rejoicing in His portion, etc.';
אֲבָל מִדּוֹת אֵלּוּ בְּעֶצֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִצַּד מִדּוֹתָיו
yet these attributes within the essence of Hashem from the perspective of His higher sefirotic attributes
הֵם מִן הַמִּדּוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁלֹּא מִמִּדַּת כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט לִשְׁכּוֹן בְּדָרֵי מַטָּה.
are among the primary attributes, not belonging to the attribute of His glory that expands to dwell among earthly dwellers.
וְהָעוֹשֶׁר וְהַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁבַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים הוּא מִצַּד הַהִתְלַבְּשׁוּת עוֹשֶׁר וּגְבוּרָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה בְּמִדַּת כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
And wealth and might in the lower realm stem from the enclothement of supernal wealth and might within the attribute of His glory,
הַמִּתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בְּכָל הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ לִכְבוֹדוֹ בָּרָא,
which expands throughout all Creation which He created entirely for His glory,
וְאֵין לִקְרוֹתוֹ חֵלֶק וּנְתִינָה מֵעָשְׁרוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ מַמָּשׁ
and this cannot strictly be termed an imparting or gift of His actual wealth and might,
דְּזֶהוּ לְאֵין קֵץ,
for those are infinite,
וְעוֹשֶׁר וּגְבוּרָה דְּבָשָׂר וָדָם הוּא בִּגְבוּל
while the wealth and might of flesh and blood are bounded,
שֶׁהָעוֹשֶׁר יֵשׁ לוֹ כָּךְ וְכָךְ וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ לְאֵין שִׁיעוּר,
wherein the rich man has a quantified amount and cannot possess without limit,
וְכֵן בִּגְבוּרָה לַגִּבּוֹר הַיּוֹתֵר עָצוּם יֵשׁ דָּבָר שֶׁיְּנַצְּחֶנּוּ וְשֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לַעֲמוֹד בּוֹ,
and so too in might, for the most mighty warrior there exists a force that can overcome him which he cannot withstand,
וְאִם כֵּן אֵין לִקְרוֹתוֹ עָשְׁרוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ.
and if so, it cannot be called His absolute wealth and might.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמָה וְכָבוֹד הוּא מִצַּד מִדָּה תַּחְתּוֹנָה שֶׁהִיא הַנּוֹתֶנֶת גְּבוּל וְקִצְבָּה לַנִּבְרָאִים,
In contrast, wisdom and honor stem from the lowest attribute (Malchut) which establishes boundaries and measure for creations,
וְהִיא גַּם כֵּן בְּלִי גְּבוּל בְּעֶצֶם שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא מִמִּדַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and it is likewise inherently limitless in its essence, being an attribute of Hashem;
וְכֵן הַחָכְמָה וְהַכָּבוֹד שֶׁל בְּרִיּוֹת הֵם בְּלֹא גְּבוּל בְּעֶצֶם
and similarly the wisdom and honor of human beings are inherently boundless in their pure essence,
רַק מוּגְבָּלִים מִצַּד הָאָדָם,
being limited only from the side of the mortal recipient,
כִּי הֵם חֵלֶק מֵחָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה וְכָבוֹד הָעֶלְיוֹן.
because they are an actual portion of the lower supernal Wisdom and Supernal Honor.
וְכָל מְלוּכַת מְלָכִים בַּפּוֹעַל הֵם עַל יְדֵי חָכְמַת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And all reigning of kings in practical governance operates through the wisdom of the Oral Torah,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא רָאוּי לַמַּלְכוּת כְּהָאוֹמֵר כֵּן עַל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ (מְגִילָּה יא.),
and this is what qualifies one as 'fit for kingship,' like the sage who stated this concerning Ahasuerus (Megillah 11a),
כִּי גַּם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא חָכָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם טז.) בְּחַכְמָיו דְּהָמָן.
for among the nations of the world one can also be termed wise, as our Sages noted (there, 16a) regarding 'the wise men of Haman.'
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ יֵשׁ לוֹ עִנְיַן חָכְמָה מְיוּחָד שֶׁבַּעֲבוּרוֹ רָאוּי לְכָבוֹד,
And a monarch possesses a unique dimension of administrative wisdom on account of which he is deserving of honor;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְהָאוֹמֵר "מָמוֹנָא יַתִּירָא דִּיהֵיב וְקָם" כְּבוֹדוֹ מִצַּד הָעוֹשֶׁר דְּ"בְּצֵל וְגוֹמֵר",

in contrast to the authority who states that 'he gave excessive money and rose to power,' where his honor derived from wealth as in 'in the shadow [of money is the shadow of wisdom],' (Ecclesiastes 7:12),
כִּי כָבוֹד מִצַּד עוֹשֶׁר וּגְבוּרָה אֵינוֹ כָּבוֹד שֶׁל אֱמֶת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה יִכּוֹן לָעַד
for honor derived from wealth and physical power is not authentic honor that endures forever,
כִּי הוּא בַּעַל גְּבוּל וְיֵשׁ לוֹ הֶפְסֵק.
because it is bounded and subject to cessation.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמָה אֵין גְּבוּל כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא דָּבוּק בְּחָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה
In contrast, wisdom has no boundary when cleaving to Supernal Wisdom,
כְּמַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד מִצַּד דִּיבּוּקָם בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
like the Davidic dynasty through their adherence to the Oral Torah;
רַק "בְּצֵל וְגוֹמֵר" דְּעַל יְדֵי "מַתָּן יַרְחִיב" מִתְרַחֵב לוֹ הַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁיּוּכַל לֵילֵךְ לִפְנֵי הַחֲכָמִים, מִמֵּילָא גַּם כְּבוֹדוֹ כֵּן.
only that 'in the shadow, etc.' shows that through 'a gift makes room' the path broadens for him to walk before the wise, and consequently his honor is similarly established.
וְהָיוּ שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד בַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
And these two opposites were combined within a single subject in Ahasuerus,
כִּי "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים",
for 'both these and those are the words of the living God,'
דְּזֶה עִנְיַן פּוּרִים וְ"נַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא וְגוֹמֵר"
for this is the very essence of Purim and 'it was reversed to the opposite, etc.,'
שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד,
that two opposites coexist in a single subject,
וּמִצַּד הַסּוֹף כְּבוֹדוֹ מִצַּד חָכְמָה וּמִצַּד הַהַתְחָלָה מִצַּד עוֹשֶׁר.
and from the perspective of the end his honor stemmed from wisdom, while from the beginning it stemmed from wealth.
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ סְתָם הוּא מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)
And 'the king' unspecified is the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He (as written in Zohar III 109a),
שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת שְׁכִינָתוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה מִתְלַבֶּשֶׁת בּוֹ בְּסוֹד גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה
which is the revelation of His Shechinah enclothed within him in the mystery of the exile of the Shechinah,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה יוֹנְקִים בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן, הוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּשְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים.
from which the children of Israel drew sustenance at that time, which likewise operated through two opposites.
וּשְׁנֵי מִינֵי כָבוֹד:
And there are two categories of honor:
אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ – הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
these are the tefillin of the head—pertaining to wisdom residing in the brain,
דְּזֶהוּ לַאֲחֵרִים לְאוֹת;
which serves as a sign unto others;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן תְּפִלִּין שֶׁל יָד שֶׁהוּא מַעֲלוֹת הַלֵּב וְכֹחוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, זֶהוּ רַק "לְךָ לְאוֹת",
in contrast to the tefillin of the arm which embodies the virtues of the heart and the faculties of action, being solely 'a sign unto you,'
דְּאֵין מִצִּדָּם כָּבוֹד מִצַּד הַתְּפִלִּין דְּהַיְינוּ הַדְּבֵיקוּת בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for from their side there is no outward honor generated by the tefillin—namely inner cleaving to Hashem—
רַק מִצַּד מַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים, הַיְינוּ הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּזוּלָתוֹ, זֶה גּוֹרֵם לוֹ כָּבוֹד,
save through gifts to the poor, meaning the deficiency present in another is what causes honor to be reflected upon him;
כִּי הֶחָכָם מְכֻבָּד גַּם בֵּין חֲכָמִים,
for the wise man is honored even among fellow sages,
וַאֲפִילּוּ יִהְיוּ גְּדוֹלִים מִמֶּנּוּ מִכָּל מָקוֹם, אִם הוּא חָכָם בֶּאֱמֶת יוּכַל לוֹמַר דְּבַר חָכְמָה בֵּין חֲכָמִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ שֶׁהוּא חָכָם,
and even if they are greater than he, if he is genuinely wise he can articulate a profound insight among great scholars such that they recognize his wisdom,
כִּי אֵין שִׁיעוּר לַחָכְמָה וְהוּא יוּכַל לְחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלֶה עַל לִבָּם.
for wisdom has no limit and he can innovate something that never occurred to them.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּגְבוּרָה וְעוֹשֶׁר שֶׁהוּא בִּגְבוּל,
In contrast to might and wealth which are bounded,
מִי שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹתוֹ אֵין לוֹ כָּבוֹד נֶגְדּוֹ,
where one who equals him accords him no deferential honor,
רַק הַכָּבוֹד מִצַּד אֶבְיוֹנִים וּפְחוּתִים מִמֶּנּוּ.
the honor stemming solely from the indigent and those lower than he.
וּבְפוּרִים נִמְשָׁכִים כָּל אַרְבָּעָה מַתָּנוֹת אֵלּוּ מִלְּמַעְלָה לַיְּהוּדִים,
And on Purim all four of these heavenly gifts are drawn down from Above unto the Jews,
וַחֲכָמִים קָבְעוּ נֶגְדָּם אַרְבַּע מִצְווֹת שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם
and the Sages instituted facing them four mitzvot so that they merit this through their active exertion,
וְיִהְיֶה נִקְרָא עַל שְׁמָם דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לַזְּמַנִּים".
and it be credited to their name under the principle that 'Israel sanctifies the seasons.'
וְהַשָּׂגַת קְדוּשַּׁת הַיְקָר דִּתְפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה,
And the attainment of the sanctity of precious honor (yakar) of the head-tefillin through wisdom,
הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא בְּמַתַּן אָדָם דְּ"בְּצֵל וְגוֹמֵר"
its active human exertion is through man's charity in 'in the shadow [of money],' etc.,
וְ"לִפְנֵי גְדוֹלִים" שֶׁהוּא הוֹלֵךְ קוֹדֶם,
and 'before great men' where he walks forward beforehand,
דַּהֲלִיכַת אָדָם הַיְינוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ,
for a man's walking represents his initiative and exertion;
וְהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עִיקָּר בָּזֶה,
and exertion is primary in this,
דְּעִיקַּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דִּפְעוּלַת אָדָם הוּא בְּמַעֲשֶׂה
since the foundational sphere of human action and effort is in physical deed,
דְּבָזֶה יַד אָדָם שׁוֹלֶטֶת,
for in deed man's hand holds active sway,
וְהוּא מֵהַנִּגְלוֹת שֶׁ"לָּנוּ וּלְבָנֵינוּ".
belonging to the revealed things that are 'unto us and unto our children' (Deuteronomy 29:28).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַחָכְמָה עִיקָּרָהּ בַּמּוֹחַ וְלֵב
In contrast, wisdom has its essential core in the brain and heart,
מֵהַנִּסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁ"לַה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ",
belonging to the concealed things that are 'unto Hashem our God,'
וְרַק מִפִּיו יִתֵּן חָכְמָה בְּעֵזֶר אֱלֹהִי.
and solely from His mouth does He bestow wisdom through divine assistance.

sections.en: Divine Mitzvot, Purim, and Boundless Cleaving

items.h: Hashem Himself fulfills mitzvot in the supernal sense; Purim expresses this reciprocal bond and the total inversion required to erase Amalek.

Seif 1 — Hashem's Mitzvot and Purim's Reciprocal Bond
The supernal fulfillment of mitzvot reveals the mutual bond of Hashem and Israel that ultimately overturns Amalek.

p: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גַּם כֵּן מְקַיֵּים הַמִּצְווֹת,
The Holy One, blessed be He, likewise fulfills the commandments,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל):
as it is written in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 30):
מֶלֶךְ גּוֹזֵר גְּזֵירָה וְהוּא וְכוּלֵי,
a mortal king issues a decree and he, etc.,
לָמָּה אֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי,
why does He not observe Shabbat, etc.,
וְהֵשִׁיבוּ דְּהוּא חֲצֵירוֹ;
and they responded that the whole universe is His personal domain;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת ו.):
and similarly they stated (Berakhot 6a):
מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַנִּיחַ תְּפִלִּין?
From where do we derive that the Holy One, blessed be He, dons tefillin?
וְעוֹד טוּבָא.
and many further teachings.
וְכֵן מִצְוֹת חֲכָמִים,
And so too concerning the rabbinic commandments,
עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וְתִגְזַר אֹמֶר וְיָקָם"
regarding this Scripture states (Job 22:28): 'You shall decree a thing, and it shall be established,'
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פְּסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי פָּרָשָׁה ג):
(as written in Pesikta Rabbati, Parashah 3):
צַדִּיק גּוֹזֵר וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַיֵּים (תַּעֲנִית כג.).
a righteous person decrees and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills (Ta'anit 23a).
וְגַם הוּא מְקַיֵּים מִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת בְּפוּרִים:
And He also fulfills the sending of portions (mishloach manot) on Purim:
"אִישׁ" – הַיְינוּ "ה' אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה",
"'A man'—this is 'Hashem is a man of war' (Exodus 15:3),"
"לְרֵעֵהוּ" – הַיְינוּ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּהָרוֹאֶה (נד:)
"'to his friend'—this is in accordance with what our Sages expounded in HaRoeh (Berakhot 54b)
עַל גַּב אִישׁ זֶה מֹשֶׁה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה".
regarding 'on the back of a man'—this refers to Moses, as it is said 'And the man Moses' (Numbers 12:3).
וְיָדוּעַ דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם נִקְרָא מֹשֶׁה בְּכָל חַכְמֵי כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת,
And it is known that the essential root of a Torah scholar is designated as Moses across all sages of all generations,
כַּנּוֹדָע מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
as is well known according to the teaching of the holy Ari, of blessed memory,
עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת קא: וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת):
on the statement of our Sages (Shabbat 101b and other places):
"מֹשֶׁה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ".
'Moses, you have spoken well!'
וְהֵם שְׁתֵּי מָנוֹת לְאָדָם אֶחָד,
And these are two portions given to one person,
הַיְינוּ כָּל הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָא אָדָם אֶחָד
meaning that all the Torah scholars in Israel are considered collectively as one person,
רֵעֵהוּ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
the companion of the Holy One, blessed be He,
שֶׁכֵּן קוֹרְאוֹ: "לְמַעַן אַחַי וְרֵעָי",
for so He addresses them: 'For the sake of My brothers and companions' (Psalms 122:8),
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה כז)
and our Sages expounded (Shemot Rabbah, beginning of Parashah 27)
עַל פָּסוּק "רֵעֲךָ וְרֵעַ אָבִיךָ וְגוֹמֵר" – זֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
on the verse 'Your companion and your father's companion, etc.' (Proverbs 27:10)—this is the Holy One, blessed be He,
וּפֵירוּשׁ "אָבִיךָ" – הַחָכְמָה כַּיָּדוּעַ.
and the meaning of 'your father' is Wisdom, as is known.
וּשְׁתֵּי מָנוֹת הַיְינוּ דְּיֵשׁ שְׁתֵּי חָכְמוֹת וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה:
And 'two portions' signifies that there exist two dimensions of wisdom and Torah teachings:
תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
the Written Torah and the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהֵם חָכְמָה עִלָּאָה – מַה שֶּׁמּוּרְגָּשׁ שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
which correspond to Supernal Wisdom (Chokhmah Ila'ah)—that which is distinctly felt to originate from Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי לְהַשִּׂיג דָּבָר זֶה,
since it is impossible for mortal human intellect to attain this on its own;
וְחָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה – מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה דְּשֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי מַשִּׂיגוֹ,
and Lower Wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah)—that which appears as though human intellect comprehends it,
וְהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
yet in ultimate truth it too emanates entirely from Hashem, blessed be He.
וְהֵם הַשְּׁתֵּי מָנוֹת שֶׁמַּשִּׂיגִים בְּפוּרִים:
And these are the two portions attained on Purim:
הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת בַּלֵּב מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּגִילּוּי מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
novel renewal in the heart from words of Torah that are overtly revealed from Hashem,
וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם וְנִרְאֶה כְּהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הַלֵּב.
and that which is in hiddenness and appears merely as an internal innovation of the human heart.
וּמַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים הוּא הַתָּאֵב לְכָל דָּבָר וּמִלּוּי הַחֵשֶׁק וְרָצוֹן,
And 'gifts to the poor' (matanot la'evyonim) addresses one who hungers for something, fulfilling the yearning and desire,
וְהֵם שְׁנֵי אֶבְיוֹנִים,
and these are two distinct categories of the needy:
דְּיֵשׁ בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה וּבַעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת:
for there are masters of Torah and masters of mitzvot;
"אוֹהֵב תוֹרָה לֹא יִשְׂבַּע", וְכֵן "אוֹהֵב מִצְווֹת לֹא וְכוּלֵי"
'he who loves Torah shall never be satisfied,' and likewise 'he who loves mitzvot shall never, etc.,'
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וָאֶתְחַנַּן עַל פָּסוּק "אֹהֵב כֶּסֶף וְגוֹמֵר"),
(as written in Midrash Rabbah, Va'etchanan on the verse 'He who loves silver, etc.'),
וְהוּא אֶבְיוֹן לַדָּבָר הַהוּא,
and he is spiritually destitute and longing for that thing,
וּמִלּוּי הַחֵשֶׁק נִרְאֶה מַתָּנָה אַחַת.
and the fulfillment of this intense desire appears as one gift.
וּמִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת הוּא כָּבוֹד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חוֹלֵק לָאָדָם,
And mishloach manot represents honor that Hashem, blessed be He, imparts unto man,
כְּעִנְיַן "וַיְהִי יַעְבֵּץ נִכְבָּד מֵאֶחָיו" עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
in the manner of 'And Ya'betz was more honorable than his brothers' (I Chronicles 4:9) through words of Torah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לח).
(as written in Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 38).
וּמַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים הוּא עוֹשֶׁר שֶׁנּוֹתֵן לָאֶבְיוֹן לְהַשְׁלִימוֹ:
And gifts to the poor represents wealth that He bestows upon the indigent to make him complete:
הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם מִתְעַשֵּׁר בְּדַעַת,
the Torah scholar becomes enriched with divine perception (da'at),
וּבַעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת בְּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים.
and the masters of mitzvot are enriched with good deeds.
וְזֶהוּ הַנְּתִינָה עַל בֵּית הָמָן,
And this accounts for the placing of Esther over the house of Haman,
כִּי לְהָמָן הָיוּ שְׁנֵי אֵלּוּ,
for Haman possessed both of these outward assets,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וּמִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא מַטּוֹת):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Midrash Rabbah and Midrash Tanchuma, Matot):
שְׁנֵי עֲשִׁירִים הָיוּ בָּעוֹלָם, הָמָן בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
two exceedingly rich men existed in the world, Haman among the nations of the world.
וּכְבוֹדוֹ מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּכָּתוּב: "גִּדַּל הַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר", "לְמִי יַחְפֹּץ הַמֶּלֶךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת יְקָר וְגוֹמֵר",
And his honor is explicitly stated in Scripture: 'the king promoted [Haman], etc.,' and 'whom the king delights to honor, etc.,'
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמֶלֶךְ סְתָם בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
and it is known that 'the king' unspecified refers to the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
כִּי הָיָה חָלַק לוֹ כָּבוֹד וְעוֹשֶׁר מִלְּמַעְלָה,
because He had apportioned unto him honor and wealth from Above,
וְזָכוּ לָזֶה מָרְדֳּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר וְנִצְּחוּהוּ.
and Mordechai and Esther merited this and conquered him.
וְנֶאֱמַר: "נָתַן הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וְגוֹמֵר אֶת בֵּית הָמָן וְגוֹמֵר",
And it is stated: 'King Ahasuerus gave, etc., the house of Haman, etc.,' (Esther 8:1),
וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ: "וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וְגוֹמֵר הִנֵּה בֵית הָמָן נָתַתִּי וְגוֹמֵר".
and likewise afterward: 'And King Ahasuerus said, etc., Behold, the house of Haman I have given, etc.' (Esther 8:7).
וְנִרְאֶה כִּי "הַמֶּלֶךְ" לְבַד הוּא מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים,
And it appears that 'the king' alone represents the King of kings,
וַ"אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ" לְבַד הוּא אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ,
and 'Ahasuerus' alone denotes Ahasuerus from his own wicked perspective,
כְּמוֹ "וַיְהִי בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ" – הוּא אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ בְּרִשְׁעוֹ מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְעַד סוֹפוֹ (מְגִילָּה יא.),
as in 'And it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus'—he is Ahasuerus in his malice from beginning to end (Megillah 11a),
וְצָוְוחוּ "וַוי" בְּיָמָיו (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה), זֶהוּ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ;
and they cried out 'woe' (vay) in his days (Midrash Rabbah), reflecting his personal nature;
אֲבָל "הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ" יֵשׁ בּוֹ הַרְכָּבָה פְּעֻלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְגַם מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ.
however, 'the king Ahasuerus' contains a synthesis of Hashem's sovereign operation enclothed together with his own self.
וְהַמַּשְׂכִּילִים יָבִינוּ זֶה בְּכָל הַמְּגִילָּה.
And insightful scholars will comprehend this across the entire Megillah.
וְכֵן בַּנְּתִינָה עַל בֵּית הָמָן וַדַּאי הוּא פְּעֻלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
And so regarding the placing over the house of Haman, it is certainly the divine work of Hashem as mentioned above,
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ מִצַּד אֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ,
yet nonetheless it does not operate from the perspective of ultimate, absolute truth,
דְּזֶה שַׁיָּיךְ רַק בִּשְׁאָר אֻמּוֹת,
for taking over a fallen entity applies only to other nations,
דְּעַל יְדֵי נִיצּוּחַ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵם קוֹלְטִים הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶם שַׁיָּיךְ דְּהֵם לָקְחוּ אַרְצָם,
where through Israel's victory they absorb the latent goodness within them, which is why they rightfully inherited their land,
וְנִקְרָא אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹלָם "אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן" –
and the Land of Israel is still termed 'the Land of Canaan'—
שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל לָקְחוּ חֶלְקָם וְקָלְטוּ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶם.
meaning that Israel claimed their allotted portion and extracted the sparks of good within them.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּעֲמָלֵק שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "תִּמְחֶה וְגוֹמֵר",
In contrast to Amalek concerning whom it is stated: 'You shall utterly blot out, etc.,'
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְכִילְתָּא סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח):
and our Sages of blessed memory stated (Mekhilta, end of Parashat Beshalach):
שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ: "שׁוֹר זֶה שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק",
so that people never say: 'this ox belonged to Amalek,'
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ בָּהֶם קְלִיטַת הַחֵלֶק כְּלָל,
meaning that no extraction or absorption of any spiritual portion is applicable to them whatsoever,
רַק נִיצּוּחָם הוּא אַבְדָנָם מִכֹּל וָכֹל.
rather their defeat means their absolute, total obliteration.
וְאֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ נְתִינָה עַל בֵּית הָמָן?
How then can an inheritance or appointment over the house of Haman be relevant,
כִּי בְּאַבְדָנוֹ אֵין כָּאן עוֹד בֵּית הָמָן שֶׁיִּרְשׁוּ מֵהֶם וְלֹא קָלְטוּ מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלוּם!
since in his annihilation there is no longer any 'house of Haman' to inherit, nor did they absorb anything from him!
רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִמְחָה זֵכֶר שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר כֵּן,
Rather, in this physical world, as long as the memory of Amalek has not yet been fully blotted out, it is fitting to speak thus;
כִּי מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן הֵם גַּם כֵּן מִכְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה,
for from the perspective of worldly illusion, they too appear part of the fabric of Creation,
אִם כֵּן עַל כָּרְחֲךָ יֵשׁ בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן אֵיזֶה צוֹרֶךְ בְּרִיאָה
and if so, perforce they must also serve some purpose in Creation,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל יוּכְלוּ לִקְלוֹט שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה גַּם כֵּן.
and Israel could seemingly extract this root as well.
אֲבָל מִצַּד הָאֱמֶת אֵינָם מִכְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה כְּלָל,
Yet from the perspective of ultimate truth, they are not part of Creation at all,
שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ רַק כְּדֵי לְמַחוֹתָם מִן הָעוֹלָם.
having been created solely in order to be erased from the world.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַפּוּרִים דַּעֲשִׂיַּת מְלָאכָה לֹא קַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מְגִילָּה ה:),
And this explains the essence of Purim, that they did not accept upon themselves the prohibition of creative labor (Megillah 5b),
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת בִּיטּוּל מְלָאכָה הוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for in truth, cessation from labor originates directly from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְשׁוּם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
requiring no human striving whatsoever,
וְשַׁיָּיךְ רַק מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא.
and is applicable only from the vantage of Hashem and the fixed, enduring sanctity of Shabbat.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יוֹם טוֹב דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי" הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת;
In contrast, Yom Tov which 'Israel sanctifies' operates through active effort;
רַק טַעַם בִּיטּוּל מְלָאכָה מִשּׁוּם דִּבְיוֹם טוֹב נִיתּוֹסַף קְדוּשָׁה מְחוּדֶּשֶׁת עַל יְדֵי דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי,
and the rationale for the cessation of labor there is because on Yom Tov a renewed sanctity is added through Israel sanctifying it,
וְאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה מִשְׁתָּרֶשֶׁת בִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת
and that added sanctity takes root in the pristine sanctity of Shabbat—
דְּהַיְינוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֹּל שֶׁהַכֹּל יוֹנֵק מִזֶּה,
namely the sanctity of Hashem Who is the Root of all from which all existence suckles—
וְנַעֲשֵׂית מֵהוֹסָפַת קְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשָּׁה קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא.
and through that addition of holiness it likewise becomes a fixed and permanent sanctity.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּפוּרִים אֵין הוֹסָפַת דָּבָר,
In contrast, on Purim there is no addition of anything new,
רַק שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה אוֹר זֶה דְּאֵין צָרִיךְ הוֹסָפַת דָּבָר
save that this supreme light is revealed: that there is no need for any addition,
דְּאֵין כָּאן תּוֹסֶפֶת כִּי דְּבוּקִים בָּעִיקָּר.
there being no supplement here because they are bound essentially to the Core.
וְזֶה טַעַם "כָּל הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת בְּטֵלִים וִימֵי הַפּוּרִים לֹא יִהְיוּ בְּטֵלִים"
And this is the inner reason why 'all festivals will be annulled, yet the days of Purim will never be annulled'
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרַשׁ מִשְׁלֵי פָּרָשָׁה ט),
(as written in Midrash Mishlei, Parashah 9),
כִּי כָּל מוֹעֵד עַל יְדֵי נֵס וִישׁוּעָה נִתְחַדֵּשׁ הוֹסָפָה,
for every other festival brought an added novelty through an historical miracle and deliverance,
וּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא יִהְיֶה ה' לְאוֹר יוֹמָם וְאֵין כָּאן הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת;
whereas in the World to Come Hashem Himself will be their everlasting light, leaving no place for separate novelty;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים הוּא גַּם כֵּן אוֹר זֶה.
unlike the days of Purim which embody this exact primordial light.
וּמִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּמְקַדְּשֵׁי אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ בִּיטּוּל מְלָאכָה.
And from the perspective of Israel sanctifying it, a cessation of labor does not apply.
וְנִמְצָא בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין כָּאן הוֹסָפָה,
Consequently, in truth there is no supplement here,
רַק מִצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה יֵשׁ הוֹסָפָה
only that from the vantage of this physical world there appears to be an addition,
דְּזֶה עַצְמוֹ הוֹסָפָה שֶׁנִּיתּוֹסַף הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ דְּאֵין הוֹסָפָה כְּלָל.
since it is itself a magnificent addition that this sublime perception was added: that no addition is needed at all!
וְזֶהוּ הַנְּתִינָה עַל בֵּית הָמָן,
And this explains the appointment over the house of Haman,
דְּנִיצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ
for the triumph over Amalek is achieved through this very realization:
שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג שֶׁאֵין הוֹסָפָה כְּלָל,
attaining the awareness that there is no addition whatsoever,
הִיפּוּךְ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא הוֹמֶה וּמְהַמֶּה
the exact antithesis of Amalek who roars and agitates,
וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ אוֹתִיּוֹת "עֲלַק" – הִיא עֲלוּקָה דְּצָוְוחַת "הַב הַב".
containing the letters of alak
(ע-ל-ק
)—the insatiable leech (alukah) crying 'give, give!'
וְנִיצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַהֵיפוּךְ
And the defeat of Amalek occurs through complete inversion
וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי הַקְּלִיטָה מִמֶּנּוּ;
and not through extracting or elevating anything from him;
וְהַהֵיפוּךְ הוּא הַשָּׂגַת דְּבֵיקוּת זֶה לְגַמְרֵי
and this inversion is the attainment of total cleaving,
דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלּוֹ חַד בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ,
perceiving that the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel are utterly one in ultimate truth,
וְהֵם נַחֲלָה בְּלֹא מְצָרִים,
and they constitute a boundless heritage,
וּבְמַה שֶּׁאֵין גְּבוּל אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ תּוֹסֶפֶת.
and within that which has no boundary, no addition can ever apply.

sections.en: Shushan Purim, Walls, and Inner Restraint

items.h: Walled cities symbolize spiritual containment; Purim and Shushan Purim reveal disciplined desire, purified anger, and bodily longing directed wholly toward Heaven.

Seif 1 — Walls, Restraint, and Shushan Purim
The walled city symbolizes disciplined desire, while Purim purifies anger and bodily longing for Heaven's sake.

p: עִנְיַן שׁוּשַׁן פּוּרִים,
The matter of Shushan Purim,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עִיר פְּרוּצָה אֵין חוֹמָה אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵין מַעְצָר לְרוּחוֹ" (מִשְׁלֵי כה, כח).
is in accordance with what is written (Proverbs 25:28): "Like a breached city without a wall is a man whose spirit has no restraint."
וְכֵן בַּפָּשׁוּט אָמְרוּ (כְּתוּבּוֹת קי:):
And so in its plain sense they stated (Ketubot 110b):
"יְשִׁיבַת כְּרַכִּים קָשָׁה",
"Dwelling in walled metropolises is difficult,"

And those in walled cities are "more shielded and hidden" (Megillah 5b) from Amalek,

as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Mekhilta, "Vayavo Amalek," Parashah 1):
בִּרְפִידִים – מִיָּד "וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק",
at Rephidim (where their hands slackened from Torah) immediately "Amalek came,"

for he senses this lapse and is stirred to attack;
כִּי מִשָּׁם הוּא יְנִיקַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֵשָׂו,
because from there derives the vitality of Esau's root,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה ו.) עַל פָּסוּק "אִמָּלְאָה הָחֳרָבָה",
as our Sages taught (Megillah 6a) on the verse (Ezekiel 26:2) "I shall be filled from the ruined one,"
וּכְשֶׁזֶּה קָם זֶה וְכוּלֵי (רַשִּׁ"י תּוֹלְדוֹת כה, כג).
and 'when this one rises, the other falls, etc.' (Rashi, Genesis 25:23).
וְעַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה נְפִילָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִתְגַּדֵּל;
And through any spiritual fall, Heaven forbid, within the souls of Israel, he magnifies himself;
וְתֵיכֶף אַחַר הַהֲנָאָה מִסְּעוּדָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע – "גִּדַּל הַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר".
and immediately following their illicit pleasure from that wicked one's banquet—"King Ahasuerus promoted [Haman], etc."
וְאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג:) דְּאֵין נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף,
And they taught (Bava Batra 123b) that Amalek falls only by the hand of the offspring of Joseph,
דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ יוֹסֵף הוּא הַצִּמְצוּם וַעֲצִירָה מִתַּאֲווֹת.
for the essential root of Joseph is constriction and restraint against bodily desires.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּיֵשׁ שְׁנֵי יְצָרִים: דְּכַעַס וְתַאֲוָה, שֶׁהֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים,
And it is known that there are two core inclinations: anger and lust, which are two opposites,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מַכּוֹת י רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א) דִּבְגִלְעָד וּשְׁכֶם שְׁכִיחֵי רוֹצְחִים,
and as written (Makkot 10a) that murderers were prevalent in Gilead and Shechem,
שֶׁהֵם מְקוֹמוֹת דְּזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף
which are the tribal territories of the seed of Joseph,
דְּשָׁם יֵשׁ עֲצִירַת תַּאֲוָה.
where mastery and restraint over physical desire prevailed.
וְכֵן עִיקַּר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הִתְחִיל מִיָּרָבְעָם,
And likewise, the primary sin of idolatry began with Jeroboam (from Joseph);
כִּי בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הֵם קוֹרְאִים שְׁנֵי יְצָרִים: דִּזְנוּת וְדַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
for in the idioms of our Sages they are titled two inclinations: licentiousness and idolatry;
רַק אַחַר שֶׁבִּיטְּלוּ יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֵין מְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶלָּא בְּכַעַס וּרְצִיחָה,
only that after they abolished the inclination for idolatry, it operates solely through anger and murder,
אֲבָל הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הוּא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
yet its fundamental root is idolatry,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (קה:): "הַשּׁוֹבֵר כְּלִי בַּחֲמָתוֹ וְכוּלֵי עַד וְכוּלֵי",
as written in Shabbat (105b): "One who smashes a vessel in his wrath, etc., is like one who serves idols,"

for idolatry is likewise the metaphysical opposite of licentiousness.
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין כא:) בִּכְרַכִּים מָצוּי גָּזֵל וַעֲרָיוֹת,
And our Sages of blessed memory stated (Eruvin 21b) that in metropolises robbery and illicit relations are common,
הַיְינוּ דְּתַאֲווֹת מָצוּי בִּכְרַכִּים יוֹתֵר;
meaning that lust is more prevalent in metropolises;
דְּ"מַעְצָר לְרוּחוֹ" רָצָה לוֹמַר בְּכַעַס, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא "רוּחוֹ" בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב,
for "restraint over his spirit" signifies control over anger, which is called "his spirit" in biblical language,
דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה צָרִיךְ הֶקֵּף חוֹמָה וְהַגְדָּרָה לְגַמְרֵי,
whereas idolatry requires an absolute encompassing wall and hermetic containment;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּתַאֲווֹת אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה מז.): "שְׂמֹאל דּוֹחָה וְיָמִין מְקָרֶבֶת",
in contrast to bodily desires, concerning which our Sages taught (Sotah 47a): "the left hand pushes away while the right draws near,"
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד לֹא יֵהָרֵג יֵצֶר זֶה,
and so in the ultimate future this inclination will not be destroyed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א דַּף קלז, קלח) דְּאִקְרֵי לָבָן דְּאִתְלַבַּן, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as written in the Zohar (Part I, 137b–138a) that it is called Laban because it becomes whitened and purified, see there.
וְעִיקַּר גִּידּוּל עֲמָלֵק וְעֵשָׂו עַל יְדֵי נְפִילַת יִשְׂרָאֵל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בְּתַאֲווֹת,
And the primary ascendance of Amalek and Esau occurs through Israel's lapse, Heaven forbid, into lusts,
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֵשָׂו "עַל חַרְבְּךָ תִחְיֶה" בִּרְצִיחָה;
for Esau's root is "by your sword you shall live," grounded in murder;
וְהַגַּם דְּאֻמּוֹת כְּלוּלִים מִכָּל רָעוֹת יַחַד,
and even though the nations embody all evils collectively,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַגָּוֶון וַדַּאי בְּרוֹצֵחַ נִרְאֶה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּעַל תַּאֲוָה.
nonetheless the outward appearance of a murderer makes him seem not to be driven by bodily lust.
וּבָזֶה הוּא פְּשִׁיטַת טְלָפָיו בְּיִחוּד שֶׁיּוּכַל לִטְעוֹן נֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל.
And herein lies his specific display of split hooves, enabling him to prosecute against Israel.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם אִם הֵם נְקִיִּים מֵרְצִיחָה,
Yet nevertheless, if Israel are pure from murderous hatred,
אָז מִיגַנְיָא מִינֵיהּ מִצַּד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם עוֹדֶף נֶגְדּוֹ בָּזֶה.
then they are shielded from him because they possess superior spiritual merit against him in that area.
אֲבָל בְּצֵירוּף שְׁנֵיהֶם מִתְגַּבֵּר בְּיוֹתֵר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
However, in the confluence of both vices, he overpowers severely, Heaven forbid.
וּלְכָךְ אָז דְּהָיָה הִשְׁתַּחֲוָויָה לַצֶּלֶם
Therefore back then, because there was bowing to the idol (in Nebuchadnezzar's days),
וּבְשׁוּשָׁן הָיָה גַּם כֵּן הֲנָאָה מִסְּעוּדָתוֹ, דְּהַיְינוּ הִתְפָּרְצוּת בְּתַאֲווֹת, הִתְגַּבֵּר בְּיוֹתֵר.
and in Shushan there was also indulgence in his banquet, representing an outbreak of lust, Amalek overpowered with tremendous force.

And that which the disciples asked Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai: "Why did Israel deserve destruction, etc.?" (Megillah 12a),
עַיֵּין שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא: "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים",
see there in the Gemara: both perspectives are the words of the living God;
דְּהַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הָמָן הוּא מִפְּנֵי הַהֲנָאָה, דְּמִזֶּה מִתְעוֹרֵר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
for the initial awakening of Haman was due to the banquet's pleasure, which roused him as noted above;
וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה רַק בְּשׁוּשָׁן וְעַל מָרְדֳּכַי בְּיִחוּד,
and his initial animosity in truth was centered only in Shushan and specifically against Mordechai,

in accordance with the Sages' exposition (Megillah 12a) on the verse "according to the pleasure of every man (ish va-ish)"—referring to Mordechai and Haman,
דְּהָיָה גַּם הוּא בְּאוֹתָהּ סְעוּדָה.
for Haman was also present at that same banquet.
רַק דְּהִתְגַּבְּרוּתוֹ עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּחֲוָויָה לַצֶּלֶם, בָּזֶה כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁוִים,
Only that his overpowering force stemming from the bowing to the idol applied equally to all Israel;
לְכָךְ נִתְעוֹרֵר עַל כָּל עַם מָרְדֳּכָי.
therefore he was aroused against the entire people of Mordechai.
וְנִקְרָא בְּכָאן "עַם מָרְדֳּכָי",
And they are titled here "the people of Mordechai,"
כִּי כָּל נֶפֶשׁ יֵשׁ לוֹ עִנְיָן מְיוּחָד שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא רֹאשׁ הַדּוֹר,
because every soul possesses a unique spiritual domain in which it is head of the generation,
וּבְעִנְיַן מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק וְהָמָן בְּיִחוּד הָיָה מָרְדֳּכַי כְּנֶגְדּוֹ,
and in the specific mission of obliterating Amalek and Haman, Mordechai stood directly facing him;
וְנִקְרְאוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם "אִישׁ" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
and both were termed ish ("man") as noted above.
כִּי בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ יֵשׁ כְּנֶגְדּוֹ, "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה", נֶפֶשׁ בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
For opposite every soul exists, "one corresponding to the other," an opposing counterpart among the nations,
וְנֶגֶד מָרְדֳּכַי הָיָה הָמָן;
and opposite Mordechai stood Haman;
וּלְכָךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר גִּדַּל הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶת הָמָן, לְעֻמַּת זֶה גַּם כֵּן הָיָה הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת לְמָרְדֳּכָי.
and therefore when the king promoted Haman, parallel elevation simultaneously accrued to Mordechai.
וּמִצַּד הָמָן שֶׁהָיָה חוֹשֵׁב בְּלִבּוֹ "לְמִי יַחְפֹּץ הַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁהוּא הָעִיקָּר בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ,
And from the arrogant perspective of Haman who assumed in his heart "whom would the king delight [to honor more than myself]," viewing himself as the center of the entire world,
נִקְרְאוּ גַּם כֵּן הַיְּהוּדִים לְנֶגְדּוֹ "עַם מָרְדֳּכָי", שֶׁהוּא הָעִיקָּר בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ.
the Jews confronting him were likewise called "the people of Mordechai," he being the true spiritual center of the universe.
וְהִנֵּה יָדוּעַ דְּעִיקַּר יְשׁוּעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִיצּוּחָם אֵיזֶה דָּבָר הוּא עַל יְדֵי נִיצּוּחָם אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ בַּלֵּב,
And behold, it is known that the essential salvation of Israel and their victory over any adversary comes through subduing that very spiritual force within the heart;
וְהָיוּ צְרִיכִים אָז כְּבִישַׁת שְׁנֵי הַכֹּחוֹת:
and they needed at that time to subdue both powers:
הַיְינוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכַעַס,
namely, all Israel regarding the inclination of idolatry and anger,
וְשֶׁבְּשׁוּשָׁן בְּיִחוּד בְּיִצְרָא דְּתַאֲווֹת גַּם כֵּן.
and those in Shushan specifically regarding the inclination of physical desire as well.
וּלְכָךְ בִּקְּשָׁה אֶסְתֵּר לִינָּתֵן לַיְּהוּדִים אֲשֶׁר בְּשׁוּשָׁן עוֹד יוֹם לְנִיצּוּחַ הָאוֹיְבִים.
Therefore Esther requested that the Jews in Shushan be granted an additional day to defeat the enemies.
וּפוּרִים הוּא יוֹם הַנַּיָיחָא שֶׁאַחַר הַטִּרְדָּא, כִּי כָּל זְמַן הַנִּיצּוּחַ הוּא בְּטִרְדָּא;
And Purim is the day of restful relief (neicha) following turmoil, for the entire duration of active combat is filled with agitation;
וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין מַעְצָר לְרוּחָם וְזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף הֵם הַמְּמַהֲרִים בְּנִיצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק,
and those who have no restraint over their spirit, along with the seed of Joseph, hasten to crush Amalek,
וְדַי לָהֶם יוֹם אֶחָד לְבַד לִשְׁפּוֹךְ חֲמָתָם עֲלֵיהֶם לְבִלְתִּי הַשְׁאִיר שׁוֹרֶשׁ וְעָנָף,
and a single day is sufficient for them to pour out their wrath upon them so as not to leave root or branch;
כִּי מִיָּד שֶׁמִּתְבָּרְרִים שֶׁכַּעַס יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין דּוֹמֶה לְכַעַס הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
for as soon as it becomes clarified that Israel's holy anger bears no resemblance to the anger of idolaters—
שֶׁהֵם כּוֹעֲסִים רַק עַל הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדְעוּ אֶת ה' וּבִמְקוֹם שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹצֶה לִכְעוֹס –
in that they rage solely against nations that have not known Hashem and where the Holy One desires wrath—
מִכָּל מָקוֹם שׁוֹפְכִים כַּעֲסָם עַל עֲמָלֵק וְאֵין נִשְׁאָר מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלוּם, כִּי חֲמָתָם הוּא חֲמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
they pour their wrath upon Amalek until nothing of him remains, for their indignation is the indignation of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶהוּ כָּל עִיקַּר שִׁימּוּשׁ הַכַּעַס וּרְצִיחָה שֶׁנִּבְרָא בָּעוֹלָם,
And this is the sole constructive purpose of anger and lethal force created in the world,
שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ צוֹרֶךְ כְּלָל רַק לְזֶרַע עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם "תִּמְחֶה" – שָׁם צָרִיךְ לְשַׁמֵּשׁ בִּרְצִיחָה.
having no utility whatsoever except against the seed of Amalek of whom it is commanded "you shall blot out"—there lethal violence must be applied.
וְנֶעֱנַשׁ שָׁאוּל עַל שֶׁהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ שָׁם בְּרַחֲמָנוּת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא כב:),
And Saul was penalized for exercising misplaced compassion there (Yoma 22b),
וּלְעָתִיד דְּיִמָּחוּ וְיִתְבַּטְּלוּ, יִתְבַּטֵּל גַּם יֵצֶר זֶה מֵהָעוֹלָם.
and in the future when Amalek is blotted out and erased, this destructive inclination will likewise be eliminated from the world.
וּדְכְרַכִּים דְּמִיגַנְיָא שֶׁנְּקִיִּים מִזֶּה וְלֹא יוּכַל לְקַטְרֵג כָּל כָּךְ נֶגְדָּם,
And regarding the inhabitants of walled cities who are shielded, being clean of unbridled rage so that he cannot prosecute heavily against them,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נֶגֶד זֶה אִם מָצָא מְקוֹם קִטְרוּג, נִיצּוּחוֹ מִתְאַחֵר אֶצְלָם יוֹתֵר,
nevertheless, if he does find grounds for prosecution, his defeat is delayed longer among them,
וּצְרִיכִים לְהִתְבָּרֵר גַּם בְּתַאֲווֹת.
and they must undergo spiritual clarification regarding bodily lusts as well.
וּפוּרִים הוּא הַנַּיָיחָא שֶׁאַחַר מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק,
And Purim is the holy repose following the erasure of Amalek,
דְּלָכֵן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרַשׁ מִשְׁלֵי פָּרָשָׁה ט) דִּלְעָתִיד גַּם כֵּן לֹא יִתְבַּטֵּל;
which is why our Sages stated (Midrash Mishlei, Parashah 9) that in the future it will never be nullified;
כִּי בִּיטּוּל דִּלְעָתִיד הַכֹּל נִתְלָה בִּמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק שֶׁיִּתְחַדֵּשׁ אָז, שֶׁיִּמָּחֶה לְגַמְרֵי,
for the future nullification of the evil impulse depends entirely upon the eradication of Amalek which will then be completed, when he is utterly erased,
דְּהוּא עַצְמוֹ בִּיטּוּל יִצְרָא דְּכַעַס וְלִיבּוּן יֵצֶר דְּתַאֲוָה, דְּהַכֹּל נִמְשָׁךְ מִזֶּה.
which itself constitutes the eradication of anger and the purification of desire, everything flowing from this.
וּפוּרִים הוּא הַנַּיָיחָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ.
And Purim is the serene rest that follows afterward.
וְהַנַּיָיחָא שֶׁל בִּיטּוּל הַכַּעַס וּרְצִיחָה מִן הַלֵּב הוּא קְדוּשַּׁת הַפּוּרִים דְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר,
And the repose of removing anger and violence from the heart is the sanctity of Purim on the fourteenth of Adar,
שֶׁמִּתְבָּרֵר דְּגַם בְּעֵת הַבִּיסּוּם עַד דְּלָא יָדַע אֵין לוֹ רְצִיחָה אֶלָּא עַל עֲמָלֵק, וּבְרָכָה וְטוֹבַת עַיִן לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל.
wherein it is clarified that even while intoxicated 'until he knows not,' he harbors lethal fury solely against Amalek, and blessing and goodwill toward the seed of Israel.
וּקְדוּשַּׁת יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר מְאִירָה דְּכָל תַּאֲווֹתָיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם.
And the sanctity of the fifteenth day (Shushan Purim) radiates the realization that all of his bodily desires are dedicated purely for the sake of Heaven.

sections.en: Darkness before Light

items.h: Creation advances through darkness that becomes the condition for greater light; even sin and collapse can become the ground from which Torah, awe, and holiness emerge.

Seif 1 — Light that Emerges from Darkness
The pattern of creation is descent before ascent, so prior failure can become the condition for deeper holiness.

p: הַסֵּדֶר שֶׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּבְּרִיאָה: "בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא" (שַׁבָּת עז:).
The order that Hashem, blessed be He, established in Creation is: "first darkness and then light" (Shabbat 77b).
כָּךְ הוּא בְּכָל יְמוֹת עוֹלָם,
So it is throughout all the days of the world:
אֵין לְךָ שׁוּם אוֹר מִתְגַּלֶּה אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ הַקָּדוּם לוֹ.
you have no light revealed except out of the darkness that preceded it.
דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל: מַתַּן תּוֹרָה קָדַם לוֹ יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם,
By way of example: the Giving of the Torah was preceded by the Exodus from Egypt,
וְעַד שֶׁשָּׁקְעוּ וְכוּלֵי;
and until they had sunk into the forty-nine gates of defilement, etc.;
וּבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ עַל יְדֵי שְׁבִיַּת הָאָרוֹן לִפְלִשְׁתִּים, שֶׁהוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ לְגַמְרֵי,
and the building of the Holy Temple came about through the capture of the Ark by the Philistines, which was the total opposite;
וְהַגּוֹרֵם לָזֶה חֵטְא בְּנֵי עֵלִי,
and the cause of this was the sin of the sons of Eli,
הוּא מַמָּשׁ חֵטְא דְּנָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא שֶׁגָּרְמוּ קְדוּשָּׁה לַמִּשְׁכָּן,
which was literally like the sin of Nadav and Avihu who caused holiness to rest upon the Mishkan,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זְבָחִים קטו:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְנִקְדַּשׁ בִּכְבֹדִי".
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Zevachim 115b) on the verse "and it shall be sanctified by My glory."
וְעִיקַּר בִּנְיַן הַמִּשְׁכָּן גָּרַם חֵטְא הָעֵגֶל,
And the very building of the Mishkan was caused by the sin of the Golden Calf,
שֶׁבִּקְשׁוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל "אֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר יֵלְכוּ וְגוֹמֵר" מוּרְגָּשׁ לָעַיִן,
wherein Israel sought "gods that will walk [before us], etc." tangible and sensible to the physical eye,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה פָּעֲלוּ קְדוּשַּׁת מִשְׁכָּן וְאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד,
and through this they brought about the sanctity of the Mishkan and the Tent of Meeting,
שֶׁהוּא מָקוֹם מוּרְגָּשׁ לָעַיִן הוֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם שֶׁשָּׁם הַשָּׂגַת אֱלֹהוּת, "וְהָיָה כָּל מְבַקֵּשׁ ה' וְגוֹמֵר".
which is a tangible place apparent to the eye going before them where divine perception resides, "and it came to pass that everyone who sought Hashem, etc."
וְאַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן נִבְחַר עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִכְהֻנָּה גְּדוֹלָה,
And Aaron the Priest was chosen through this for the High Priesthood,
כִּי מֹשֶׁה אָמַר לוֹ: "הֵבֵאתָ עָלָיו חֲטָאָה גְדֹלָה",
for Moses said to him: "You have brought a great sin upon them,"
וּמִתּוֹךְ צְעָקָה זוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה בְּלִבּוֹ עַל כָּךְ
and out of this anguished cry that was in his heart over it,
וְהָיָה צוֹעֵק לַה' לְתַקֵּן זֶה
and he would cry out to Hashem to rectify this,
וּמְבַקֵּשׁ לְהָבִיא עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל זְכִיּוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת,
and sought to bring great merits upon Israel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק א): "מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן וְכוּלֵי וּמְקָרְבָן לַתּוֹרָה",
and as they said (Avot 1:12): "the trait of Aaron, etc., and drawing them near to the Torah,"
עַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לִכְהֻנָּה גְּדוֹלָה, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא הַמְכַפֵּר שֶׁל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
through this he merited the High Priesthood, meaning that he serves as the atoner for all Israel.
וְכֵן כָּל דָּבָר, מִתּוֹךְ חֹשֶׁךְ יוֹצֵא אוֹר שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ אוֹתוֹ הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
And so with every matter, out of darkness emerges a light that is the literal opposite of that very darkness,
בֵּין בַּדּוֹרוֹת בֵּין בִּפְרָטֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
whether across the generations or within individual souls.
וְגוּף עִנְיַן הַמִּשְׁכָּן וּמִזְבֵּחַ וְסֵדֶר עֲבוֹדָה
And the essential nature of the Mishkan, the altar, and the sacrificial order
הוּא הוֹרָדַת הַשְּׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
is the drawing down of the Shechinah into the lower realms,
וְסֵדֶר הַתִּיקּוּנִים וְכַפָּרוֹת שֶׁל חֲטָאִים,
and the order of rectifications and atonements for sins,
וְקִינּוּחַ לְכָל מִינֵי לִכְלוּכִים,
and the wiping away of all types of defilements,
וְיִפּוּי וְקִישּׁוּטֵי הַכַּלָּה,
and the beautification and adornments of the Bride;
וְהוּא נִמְשָׁךְ עַל יְדֵי שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
and this is drawn down through the dwelling of His Shechinah, blessed be He, in the lower world;
דְּמֵאַחַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for once there is a revelation of His Shechinah within the hearts of the children of Israel,
מִמֵּילָא מִתְנַקֶּה כָּל לִכְלוּךְ וְנִדְחֶה הָרַע וְהַחֹשֶׁךְ,
automatically every impurity is cleansed and evil and darkness are dispelled,
דְּ"עִמֵּיהּ שְׁרֵי נְהוֹרָא",
for "light dwells with Him" (Daniel 2:22),
וְזֶהוּ "מִשְׁכָּן" – רָצָה לוֹמַר מְקוֹם שְׁכִינָה.
and this is Mishkan—meaning the dwelling place of the Shechinah.
אֲבָל "מִקְדָּשׁ" – רָצָה לוֹמַר מְקוֹם קְדוּשָּׁה,
However, Mikdash—meaning a place of kedushah (holiness)—
הוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ מִשְׁכָּן,
is the literal antithesis of Mishkan;
דִּקְדוּשָּׁה רָצָה לוֹמַר הַבְדָּלָה וְהַפְרָשָׁה שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר נִבְדָּל,
for kedushah denotes transcendence, separation, and withdrawal as a secluded entity,
אֲבָל שְׁכִינָה הוּא הַשּׁוֹכֵן וּמִתְחַבֵּר וְאֵין נִבְדָּל,
whereas Shechinah represents that which indwells, connects, and does not remain separate,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַשֹּׁכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם" (וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא נו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
as it is written: "Who dwells with them in the midst of their uncleanness" (and as written in Yoma 56b),
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קְדוּשָּׁה הוּא הַבְדָּלָה מִטֻּמְאָה.
in contrast to kedushah, which is separation from impurity.
וּמָצִינוּ מִשְׁכָּן דְּאִקְרֵי מִקְדָּשׁ, וּמִקְדָּשׁ אִקְרֵי מִשְׁכָּן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רֵישׁ עֵירוּבִין),
And we find that the Mishkan is called Mikdash, and the Mikdash is called Mishkan (as written at the beginning of Eruvin 2a),
דְּכוּלָּא חַד וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת בְּיַחַד,
for all is one and both truths coexist simultaneously:
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגַם נִבְדָּל מֵהֶם,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells within the children of Israel and is also transcendent above them,
כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁאִיתָא בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג):
like that which is found in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (beginning of Chapter 3):
"אֲנִי יָרֵאתִי מִתּוֹךְ שִׂמְחָתִי, וְשָׂמַחְתִּי מִתּוֹךְ יִרְאָתִי".
"I feared out of my joy, and I rejoiced out of my fear."
הַשִּׂמְחָה הוּא אִישׁ בְּרֵעֵהוּ וְכַדּוֹמֶה מִתּוֹךְ הָאַהֲבָה וְהַהִתְחַבְּרוּת,
Joy arises between a man and his friend and the like out of love and intimacy,
וְהַיִּרְאָה הוּא מִצַּד הַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ מֵאָדָם שֶׁגָּדוֹל וְנִבְדָּל מִמֶּנּוּ.
while fear/awe stems from respectful deference toward one who is great and elevated above him.
וְאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵם שְׁנֵיהֶם יַחַד,
And regarding Hashem, blessed be He, both aspects exist together,
וְהָא בְּלֹא הָא לָא סַגִּי,
and neither can suffice without the other;
דְּיִרְאָה לְבַד מֵבִיא שְׁטוּת, כְּעִנְיַן "הֲלֹא יִרְאָתְךָ כִּסְלָתֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
for awe alone brings folly, in the vein of "Is not your fear your foolish confidence, etc." (Job 4:6),
וְשִׂמְחָה לְבַד מֵבִיא קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ,
and joy alone brings frivolity,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת לא סוֹף עַמּוּד א): "מוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ",
and concerning this they said (Shabbat 31a end): "It were better you had not brought it up,"
דְּבַתּוֹרָה נֶאֱמַר: "מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב",
for regarding Torah it is said: "gladdening the heart,"
וְעַל יָדָהּ הוּא הַהִתְחַבְּרוּת לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and through it comes intimate connection to Hashem, blessed be He.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּתְפִלָּה נִקְרָא: "וְנִקְדַּשְׁתִּי בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל",
In contrast, regarding prayer it is called: "and I will be sanctified among the children of Israel,"
דְּלָכֵן מִצְוַת תְּפִלָּה בְּצִבּוּר,
which is why the mitzvah of communal prayer,
שֶׁהוּא הַכָּרַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה וְשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִבְדָּל,
which represents the recognition of holiness and that Hashem is transcendent,
הוּא עַל יְדֵי רִיבּוּי הַמִּתְאַחֵד;
is actualized through a unified plurality;
וְ"כָל בֵּי עֲשָׂרָה שְׁכִינְתָא שַׁרְיָא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין לט.),
and "wherever ten gather, the Shechinah rests" (Sanhedrin 39a),
שֶׁהֵם קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה,
for they constitute an entire spiritual stature,
דִּבְנֵי אָדָם אֵין דַּעְתָּן שָׁוָה,
since people's minds are not identical,
