וְאַף חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יד) "בְּעָוֹן מָלֵא" לְעִנְיַן תַּאֲוָה.
Even regarding the most pious of the pious, our Sages of blessed memory said (Vayikra Rabbah 14) that he is “full of iniquity” with respect to desire.

וְנֶאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי כז, ד): "מִי יַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי קִנְאָה"; וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בְּכָבוֹד, שֶׁמָּצִינוּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה הֵעִידָה עָלָיו שֶׁהוּא עָנָו מִכָּל הָאָדָם, וַחֲשָׁדוּהוּ לְמִשְׂתָּרֵר.

And it is said (Proverbs 27:4), “Who can stand before jealousy?” All the more so with regard to honor: we find that although the Torah testified that Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, was humbler than every person, people still suspected him of seeking authority.
וְזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִסָּה הַמְעַכֵּב, וְאַף חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים יוּכַל לְפָגְעוֹ לִפְעָמִים עִנְיַן קִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד, שֶׁלֹּא יִנָּצֵל.
This is the root of the “leaven in the dough” that obstructs a person; even the most pious can at times be struck by jealousy, desire, or honor and not entirely escape them.

אֲבָל הָעִקָּר הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר שֹׁרֶשׁ הַלֵּב. וּמִסְּתָמָא בִּלְעָם הָרָשָׁע, שֶׁהָיָה מִנְּבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, וְאֵין הַנְּבוּאָה שׁוֹרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא עַל חָכָם, גִּבּוֹר וְעָשִׁיר (שַׁבָּת צב.), כָּל שֶׁכֵּן בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.

But the essential measure follows the root of the heart. Presumably, the wicked Balaam, who was one of the prophets of the nations—and prophecy does not rest even in Israel except upon one who is wise, mighty, and wealthy (Shabbat 92a)—would all the more require such qualities among the nations.

וְעָשִׁיר הוּא הַשָּׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְאֵינוֹ רַע עַיִן; וְגִבּוֹר — הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּעַל נֶפֶשׁ רְחָבָה בְּתַאֲוָה; וְחָכָם בַּתּוֹרָה — הֵפֶךְ גַּס הָרוּחַ, שֶׁהוּא סִימָן לַעֲנִיּוּת דְּתוֹרָה, דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה יוֹרְדִים לְמָקוֹם נָמוּךְ וְרוּחַ נְמוּכָה, וְיָדוּעַ דְּכָל גֵּאֶה שׁוֹטֶה.

“Wealthy” means one who rejoices in his portion and is not stingy-eyed; “mighty” means one who conquers his inclination and is not broad-souled in desire; and one who is wise in Torah is the opposite of the arrogant, for arrogance signals poverty in Torah, since words of Torah descend to a low place and to a lowly spirit, and it is known that every arrogant person is foolish.

וְאִם כֵּן וַדַּאי בִּלְעָם הָיָה גַּם כֵּן נָקִי מִכָּל אֵלֶּה, וְהָיָה גַּם כֵּן מְלַמֵּד דֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּעֵין אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהֲרֵי הָיָה נָבִיא לַהַשֵּׁם וְיוֹדֵעַ מֵאֲמִתּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁהֲרֵי נְבוּאָתוֹ הָיְתָה נְבוּאַת אֱמֶת שֶׁנִּכְתְּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה.

If so, Balaam too must outwardly have been free of all these defects and capable of teaching the way of the Blessed One, in a manner resembling our father Abraham, peace be upon him; for he was a prophet to God and knew the truth of the Blessed One, as his prophecy was true prophecy recorded in the Torah.

רַק כָּל זֶה הָיָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ; אֲבָל מַעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ הוּא גּוֹי, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּכוּת בֶּאֱמֶת לְכָל שָׁלֹשׁ הַמַּעֲלוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרוֹת, וּכְשֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְנִסָּיוֹן נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁהוּא הַהֵפֶךְ מִכֻּלָּם.

Yet all of this existed only in the revealed layer of his heart. In its depths he remained a gentile with no genuine connection to those three qualities; when he was tested, it became clear that inwardly he was their opposite.
וְכֵן הוּא מִתְבָּרֵר בַּתַּלְמִידִים, שֶׁהֵם דֻּגְמַת בָּנִים; דְּשָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁהֵם מַעֲמַקֵּי לֵב דְּאָב, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
The same becomes clarified through his disciples, who are analogous to children; for I heard that children reveal the deepest recesses of the father’s heart, as I have written elsewhere.

וּלְכָךְ הַחִלּוּק דְּאֵלּוּ נוֹחֲלִין עוֹלָם הַבָּא; כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא רוֹמֵז לְבִינָה — לִבָּא — וְהוּא מִצַּד דְּבֵקוּת הַלֵּב, דְּלָכֵן כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.

Hence the distinction that these disciples inherit the World to Come. As is known, the World to Come alludes to Binah—the heart—and comes through the heart’s attachment; therefore all Israel have a share in the World to Come.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן תַּלְמִידָיו שֶׁל בִּלְעָם, דְּבִלְעָם עַצְמוֹ נִמְנֶה בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
This is unlike Balaam’s disciples, for Balaam himself is counted among those who have no share in the World to Come.
וּכְבָר כָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר דִּזְכִיָּה גְּדוֹלָה הִיא לְבִלְעָם בְּמַה שֶּׁנִּמְנָה בַּמִּשְׁנָה דְּ"אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא" בַּהֲדֵי גְּדוֹלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
I have already written elsewhere that it was a great privilege for Balaam to be counted in the Mishnah’s list of those who “have no share in the World to Come” alongside prominent figures of Israel.

וְנִרְאֶה לִי בָּרוּר דְּזֶה שֶׁאָמַר "תָּמֹת נַפְשִׁי מוֹת יְשָׁרִים וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁהִקְשָׁה בְּלִקּוּטֵי תוֹרָה מֵהָאֲרִ"י, כֵּיוָן דְּלֹא עָלְתָה לוֹ כֵּן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, קצד עַמּוּד ב), לָמָּה נִכְתְּבוּ דִּבְרֵי בַטָּלָה שֶׁלּוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה.

It seems clear to me that this explains Balaam’s words, “May my soul die the death of the upright, etc.” Likkutei Torah in the name of the Ari asks: since this did not in fact occur for him, as stated in the holy Zohar (III, 194b), why were his apparently futile words written in the Torah?
וּלְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי יֵשׁ לוֹמַר עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת י עַמּוּד א: "מֵת אַתָּה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא תִחְיֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא".
According to what I have written, this can be understood in light of Berakhot 10a: “You are dead in this world, and you will not live in the World to Come.”
הָכָא נָמֵי, מַה שֶּׁאָמַר "תָּמֹת" — "מוֹת" רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר, מִיתַת נַפְשׁוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא יִהְיֶה תּוֹךְ מִיתַת "יְשָׁרִים", הֵם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹתָם שֶׁאָבְדוּ עוֹלָם הַבָּא.

So too here: when he said “may [my soul] die,” “death” means that the death of his soul with respect to the World to Come should be included among the “death of the upright”—those Israelites who lost their share in the World to Come.

דִּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה כָּל עִקַּר נְבוּאַת בִּלְעָם הָיְתָה רַק עַל אוֹתָם פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאָבְדוּ עוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא נִסְתַּכֵּל רַק לְהַזְכִּיר חֶטְאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְדִבֵּר רַק מֵהַחוֹטְאִים.

For it appears that the entire focus of Balaam’s prophecy was precisely those sinners of Israel who lost the World to Come, since he looked only to invoke Israel’s sins and spoke specifically of the sinners.

וְגַם אֵין שׁוּם בְּרִיָּה מַשִּׂיג מַה שֶּׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִמֶּנּוּ. וְאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת לד:): "צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים — עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה"; וְהַיְנוּ עֵין נְבִיאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִם כֵּן נְבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם — אַף בַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה בִּכְלַל "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה".

Moreover, no created being can perceive what stands above its own level. Our Sages of blessed memory said (Berakhot 34b), regarding the completely righteous, “no eye has seen”; this means even the eye of Israel’s prophets. All the more so, for prophets of the nations even the level of true penitents lies within “no eye has seen.”
וְהוּא, שֶׁהָיָה מֵאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וַדַּאי לֹא הִשִּׂיג מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן אֶלָּא מַדְרֵגַת אוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
Since Balaam himself belonged to those with no share in the World to Come, he could certainly perceive within Israel only the level of those who likewise had no share in the World to Come.

וְעַל זֶה הָיְתָה עִקַּר טַעֲנַת בָּלָק: "כִּסָּה אֶת עֵין הָאָרֶץ" — רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר הָאָרֶץ הַיְדוּעָה, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא", שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְעַמֵּךְ וְגוֹמֵר, לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ"; הֲרֵי דְּ"אֶרֶץ" רוֹמֵז לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.

This was the core of Balak’s claim: “it has covered the eye of the land”—meaning the well-known “Land,” as in the teaching, “All Israel have a share in the World to Come,” based on the verse, “Your people… shall forever inherit the land.” Thus “land” alludes to the World to Come.
וְזֶה הָיָה רְאִיַּת בָּלָק, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וַיַּרְא וְגוֹמֵר", מַשְׁמַע דְּהוּא לְבַד רָאָה וְלֹא אֲחֵרִים.
This was Balak’s unique perception, as the verse says, “And [Balak] saw, etc.,” implying that he alone saw what others did not.

וְהַיְנוּ דְּעִנְיַן הָאֱמֹרִי, שֶׁהִפְלִיג הַכָּתוּב כַּמָּה פְעָמִים בְּשִׁבְחוֹ: "אֲשֶׁר כְּגֹבַהּ אֲרָזִים גָּבְהוֹ וְחָסֹן וְגוֹמֵר"; וְכֵן נִזְכָּר בְּהַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל מִלְחֶמֶת סִיחוֹן וְעוֹג — "כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ" — שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה חֶסֶד עוֹלָמִי.

This also explains the matter of the Amorites, whom Scripture repeatedly describes in lofty terms—“whose height was like the height of cedars, and he was strong, etc.” Likewise, the Great Hallel mentions the wars with Sihon and Og under the refrain “for His kindness is everlasting,” indicating an eternal kindness embodied in their defeat.
וְגַם מַה דְּנִתְיָרֵא מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֵעוֹג, וַדַּאי אֵינוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל גְּבוּרָתָם לְבַד, דִּכְלַפֵּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין חִלּוּק בֵּין גִּבּוֹרִים לַחַלָּשִׁים.
Moshe Rabbeinu’s fear of Og certainly was not merely because of physical might, for before the Blessed One there is no distinction between the strong and the weak.
גַּם מַה שֶּׁשָּׁלַח לְסִיחוֹן לְשָׁלוֹם, וַהֲרֵי הוּא מִשִּׁבְעָה עַמְּמִין שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
The same question applies to Moses’ sending Sihon an offer of peace, even though he belonged to the seven nations assigned to Israel.
רַק יָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב עַל עוֹג דְּפָלַט מִדּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, דְּוַדַּאי אֵינוֹ בְּחִנָּם, רַק שֶׁהוּא הָיָה נָקִי מֵחֶטְאֵי דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל — עַד כָּאן.

Rather, it is known what is written of Og, that he escaped the generation of the Flood. This surely was not without reason; rather, he was free of the sins of the generation of the Flood—end of that citation.

וְיָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, רטז, רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב), דְּהָיָה רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, וְהָיָה אָז גַּם כֵּן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם — "בְּשַׁגַּם" בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "מֹשֶׁה" — אִלְמָלֵי זָכוּ; רַק שֶׁבְּחֶטְאָם נִתְהַפֵּךְ שֶׁפַע מֵי הַתּוֹרָה לְמֵי הַמַּבּוּל.

It is also known from the Zohar (III, 216b, beginning of the page) that the Torah could have been given in the generation of the Flood, and that the root of Moshe Rabbeinu was present then as well—“beshagam” has the numerical value of “Moshe”—had they merited it. Through their sin, however, the flow of the waters of Torah was transformed into the waters of the Flood.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בִּזְבָחִים (קטז.) דִּבְשָׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה נִתְקַבְּצוּ אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְבִלְעָם.
And they likewise said in Zevachim (116a) that at the time of the giving of the Torah the nations of the world gathered to Balaam. –

וּלְפִי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:) דְּבִלְעָם בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשָׁלֹשׁ נֶהֱרַג, וְהוּא בִּשְׁנַת אַרְבָּעִים לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, אִם כֵּן נוֹלַד שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה.

[[Yet according to what they said in Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 106b), Balaam was thirty-three years old when he was killed, which occurred in the fortieth year after the Exodus; if so, he was born seven years after the giving of the Torah.]

וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר: כְּמוֹ דְּשֹׁרֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִקְרָא "מֹשֶׁה", כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, דְּהָיָה בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, וְכֵן בַּתַּלְמוּד (שַׁבָּת קא:) "מֹשֶׁה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ" עַל אֵיזֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם בַּדּוֹר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מֵחָכְמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.

[The answer must be that just as the root of Moshe Rabbeinu’s soul is called “Moshe,” as noted above, and was already present in the generation of the Flood—and likewise the Talmud (Shabbat 101b) can address a Torah scholar of a later generation with the words “Moshe, you have spoken well,” because he possesses something of Moshe Rabbeinu’s wisdom—]
כָּךְ בִּלְעָם הוּא כְּנֶגֶד הַדַּעַת דְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא; הַהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּדַעְתָּן נִקְרָא שֶׁנִּתְקַבְּצוּ לְבִלְעָם.
[so Balaam denotes the counter-root of da’at on the side of impurity; the nations’ intellectual apprehension through their own da’at is therefore described as their gathering to “Balaam.”]

וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָזֶה מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סוֹטָה יא.) דְּהָיָה מִיּוֹעֲצֵי פַרְעֹה, וּלְפִי זֶה הֶאֱרִיךְ יָמִים הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד; וַהֲרֵי אִיתָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:) "אַנְשֵׁי דָמִים וּמִרְמָה לֹא יֶחֱצוּ יְמֵיהֶם".

[The same principle applies to their teaching (Sotah 11a) that Balaam was among Pharaoh’s advisers. Taken literally, this would make him extraordinarily long-lived, whereas Sanhedrin 106b applies to him the verse, “men of bloodshed and deceit shall not live out half their days.”]

וּבְסֵפֶר הַיָּשָׁר כָּתוּב דְּיוֹעֵץ פַּרְעֹה הָיָה בִּלְעָם אַחֵר, זְקֵנוֹ שֶׁל זֶה; אֲבָל לְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה לֹא מַשְׁמַע כֵּן. וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו.) עַל "וַיַּרְא אֶת הַקֵּינִי וְכוּלֵי" — "עִמִּי הָיִיתָ בָּעֵצָה וְכוּלֵי".

[Sefer HaYashar states that Pharaoh’s adviser was another Balaam, the grandfather of this Balaam, but the wording of our Sages does not imply that. The same is true of their interpretation (Sanhedrin 106a) of “he saw the Kenite, etc.”—“you were with me in that counsel, etc.”]

אֲבָל הַכַּוָּנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי, דְּשֹׁרֶשׁ הַדַּעַת דְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא נִקְרָא "בִּלְעָם", בֵּין שֶׁהָיְתָה מְלֻבֶּשֶׁת בְּאֵיזֶה נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִית, בֵּין שֶׁהָיְתָה בְּדַעַת פַּרְעֹה בְּעַצְמוֹ.]
[Rather, the intent is as I have written: the root of da’at on the side of impurity is called “Balaam,” whether it was clothed in a particular individual soul or expressed within Pharaoh’s own mind.]
"שֶׁמָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא מַבּוּל" — שֶׁכְּפִי עִנְיָנָם הָיוּ חוֹשְׁבִים שֶׁפַע מֵי תּוֹרָה הַבָּא לָעוֹלָם לְמֵי מַבּוּל.

Thus they asked, “Perhaps the Holy One, blessed be He, is bringing a flood,” because in accordance with their own orientation they mistook the influx of the waters of Torah entering the world for the waters of a flood.

וְאִם כֵּן, עוֹג שֶׁנִּצּוֹל מִמַּבּוּל הֲרֵי הָיָה לוֹ קְצָת שַׁיָּכוּת בְּהֶכְרֵחַ לַתּוֹרָה. וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן לְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק טז) דְּהוּא אֱלִיעֶזֶר עֶבֶד אַבְרָהָם, שֶׁהָיָה דּוֹלֶה וּמַשְׁקֶה מִתּוֹרַת רַבּוֹ (יוֹמָא כח:).

If so, Og, who survived the Flood, necessarily possessed some connection to Torah. This is all the more so according to Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chapter 16), which identifies him with Eliezer, Abraham’s servant, who “drew forth and gave others to drink” from his master’s Torah (Yoma 28b).
וְאָמְרוּ בְּנִדָּה (סא.): "סִיחוֹן וְעוֹג אַחִים, בְּנֵי אֲחִיָּה בַּר שַׁמְחֲזַאי"; נִרְאֶה דְּגַם סִיחוֹן כָּמוֹהוּ פָּלַט מִמַּבּוּל.
And they said in Niddah (61a), “Sihon and Og were brothers, sons of Ahiyah bar Shamhazai”; it therefore appears that Sihon too, like Og, survived from the generation of the Flood.
וְזֶה כָּל שִׁבְחָם לִמְלָכִים גְּדוֹלִים וְאַדִּירִים בְּגֹבַהּ וְחֹסֶן — הַיְנוּ בְּמַעֲלוֹת רוּחָנִיּוֹת וּגְבוּרָה דִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר.
This is the meaning of their praise as great and mighty kings, lofty and powerful—namely, that they possessed spiritual attainments and strength in subduing the inclination.

וְזֶהוּ עִקַּר חֶסֶד הַשֵּׁם לָעוֹלָם: שֶׁמִּשֶּׁנִּתְּנָה תּוֹרָה וְנִבְחֲרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאֻמָּה אַחֶרֶת לְהִתְקָרֵב לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ מְכִילְתָּא: "עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְחֲרוּ וְכוּלֵי".

This, then, is the essential everlasting kindness of God: once the Torah was given and Israel was chosen, no other nation can enter that covenantal nearness before Him except through joining Israel, as stated at the beginning of the Mekhilta, “before they were chosen, etc.”

וַאֲפִלּוּ יִשְׁמֹר כָּל מִצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה, צָרִיךְ לְהִתְגַּיֵּר וְלִהְיוֹת מְכֻנֶּה בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל; וּבְלֹא זֶה, עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה חַיָּב וְכוּלֵי, דְּהִיא "מוֹרָשָׁה לִקְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב" דַּוְקָא.

Even if a person from the nations were to observe the Torah’s commandments, he would still need conversion and the name Israel in order to enter this covenantal identity; without that, the Talmud’s restriction concerning a gentile’s Torah study applies, for Torah is specifically “an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.”
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁשָּׁלַח לְסִיחוֹן לְשָׁלוֹם — הַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּתְגַּיֵּר; וְהוּא הָלַךְ לַמִּלְחָמָה כִּי הוּא טָעַן שֶׁהוּא הַנִּבְחָר, וְכֵן עוֹג.
This is why Moses sent peace to Sihon—meaning, an opening to join the covenant through conversion. Sihon instead went to war because he claimed that he himself was the chosen one; so too Og.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִתְיָרֵא מֵהֶם וַדַּאי לֹא לְחִנָּם, כִּי יָדַע עֹצֶם כֹּחָם וּמַעֲלָתָם בְּסוּר מֵרָע דְּכָל חֶטְאֵי דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל.

Moshe Rabbeinu’s fear of them was therefore certainly not baseless: he recognized the magnitude of their strength and their attainment in turning away from the evils that characterized the generation of the Flood.
וּבְמִשְׁפַּט בְּנֵי נֹחַ הֵם הָיוּ צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים, שֶׁאֵין כְּמוֹתָם בַּדּוֹר בִּבְנֵי נֹחַ.
Measured by the law applicable to the descendants of Noah, they were completely righteous—without equal among the non-Israelite peoples of their generation.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר "כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ": דְּתוֹרַת חֶסֶד שֶׁנָּתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, שֶׁמִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵהֶם אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם.

Concerning this the Psalm says, “for His kindness is everlasting”: the Torah of kindness that the Blessed One gave specifically to Israel endures forever, so that one who remains wholly outside that covenant has no standing within this particular inheritance.

items.h:
Seif 2 — Balak, Balaam, and the Boundary of Israel
Balak and Balaam approach holiness from outside but cannot enter the inherited covenant rooted within Israel.

p: וְזֶה הָיָה רְאִיַּת בָּלָק גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה אָז גָּנוּז עֲדַיִן נִיצוֹץ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁיָּצָא מֵחֲלָצָיו מֵרוּת (נָזִיר כג:), וְהִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָרוֹמֶזֶת לָאָרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה.

This too was Balak’s perception: the spark of King David, peace be upon him, who would descend from him through Ruth (Nazir 23b), was still hidden within him, and he sensed that he had some connection to the Land of Israel, which alludes to the supernal Land.
וְכֵן קָרְבְּנוֹתָיו הֲרֵי הָיוּ לְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁם, וְחָשַׁב שֶׁגַּם הוּא יַעֲבֹד עֲבוֹדָה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְלָמָּה נִבְחֲרוּ אֵלּוּ דַּוְקָא.
His offerings too were brought to God, and he thought: I too will serve the Blessed One—why were these people alone chosen?

בְּמַה שֶּׁרָאָה וְהֵבִין מִמַּה שֶּׁעָשָׂה לָאֱמֹרִי, דְּמִי שֶׁחָפֵץ בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צָרִיךְ לְהִתְגַּיֵּר וּלְהִתְכַּנּוֹת בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּוְקָא — שֶׁהוּא "כִּסָּה אֶת עֵין הָאָרֶץ".

From what he saw had been done to the Amorites, he understood that one who desires the service of the Blessed One must convert and be designated specifically by the name Israel—and this is what he meant by “it covered the eye of the land.”
פֵּרוּשׁ, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשׁוּם אֻמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן לְהַבִּיט לָאָרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה בְּגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה וְהַשָּׂגַת עוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁהוּא מְכֻסֶּה כֻּלּוֹ עַל יְדֵי הָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית.

That is: no other nation or tongue can gaze directly upon the supernal Land—the revelation of the Divine Presence and attainment of the World to Come—because that entire access is, as it were, covered by the Israelite nation.
וְזֶה הָיָה כָּל עִקַּר חֵפֶץ בָּלָק לְגָרְשׁוֹ מֵאֶרֶץ זוֹ, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַדָּבָר הֶפְקֵר כְּקוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה: הָרוֹצֶה לִזְכּוֹת לָאָרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה — יִזְכֶּה.

Balak’s essential desire was therefore to drive Israel from this “Land,” so that the matter would again be open to all as before the giving of the Torah: whoever wished to attain the supernal Land could do so.

וְעַל זֶה שָׁלַח אַחַר בִּלְעָם, שֶׁהוּא הָיָה לְעֻמַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כַּיָּדוּעַ. וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הַדַּעַת הַמְחַבֵּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה, שֶׁהֵם מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא.
For this purpose he sent for Balaam, who, as is known, stood opposite Moshe Rabbeinu. Moshe represents da’at, which joins Chochmah and Binah—the mind and the heart.

זֶהוּ עִנְיַן הַתּוֹרָה, לְשׁוֹן הוֹרָאָה, שֶׁמּוֹרָה הַלֵּב לִהְיוֹת נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר הַחָכְמָה שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ; דְּזוּלַת זֶה, כְּשֶׁאֵין מוֹרֶה לַלֵּב, אֵינוֹ נִקְרָא "תּוֹרָה" אֶלָּא "חָכְמָה" לְבַד.

This is the meaning of Torah, from the language of instruction: it instructs the heart to follow the wisdom of the Blessed One. Without that guidance of the heart, wisdom is not yet called Torah; it remains wisdom alone.
וְזֶה כֹּחַ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁבָּא וְהוֹרִיד הַתּוֹרָה לָאָרֶץ וְהִנְחִילָהּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה לִהְיוֹת הַלֵּב נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר חָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
This is Moshe Rabbeinu’s power: he brought the Torah down to earth and bequeathed it to Israel, endowing Israel with the capacity for the heart to be drawn after Divine wisdom.

אֲבָל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּכוּת לָזֶה. וּבִלְעָם, שֶׁהָיָה נֶגֶד זֶה, הִתְפָּאֵר "וְיֹדֵעַ דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן": שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ וּמַשִּׂיג דַּרְגָא דְּדַעַת זוֹ, אֶלָּא שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ "דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן" — פֵּרוּשׁ, עֶלְיוֹן מַה שֶּׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגַת מוֹחוֹ וְלִבּוֹ, דְּאֶצְלוֹ הָיָה זֶה לְמַעְלָה מִן הַטֶּבַע.

The nations, however, do not naturally possess this connection. Balaam, who stood opposite Moshe, therefore boasted that he “knows the knowledge of the Most High”: he could intellectually know and apprehend the level of da’at, yet called it “higher knowledge,” meaning something above the natural level of his own mind and heart.
וְהַיְנוּ, אַף שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ רִבּוֹנוֹ וּמִתְנַהֵג גַּם כֵּן בְּדֶרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה בִּשְׁמִירָה מִקִּנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד, בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה מְשֻׁקָּע בָּהֶם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.

Thus, although he knew his Master and outwardly conducted himself in the way of Torah, guarding against jealousy, desire, and honor, inwardly he was in fact immersed in those very traits, as explained above.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר אָז בְּאוֹתוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ כָּל שָׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת רָעוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ. וְאַף שֶׁהִשִּׂיג שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּחַר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל — רָצָה הוּא לְהֵפֶךְ.
That episode revealed that all three negative traits truly existed in the depths of his heart. Even though he understood that the Blessed One had chosen Israel, he wanted the opposite.

וְעַל יָדוֹ הָיָה כָּל בֵּרוּר עִנְיָן זֶה: שֶׁאַף שֶׁהוּא רָצָה לְעוֹרֵר חֶטְאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁגַּם בָּהֶם נִמְצָא הַמַּגְדִּילִים הַחֵטְא עַד שֶׁאוֹבְדִים חֵלֶק עוֹלָם הַבָּא, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַעֲלָתָם גְּדוֹלָה בֶּאֱמֶת.

Through Balaam himself this entire point was clarified: although he sought to arouse Israel’s sins, and some Israelites magnify sin to the point of losing their share in the World to Come, their underlying spiritual stature nevertheless remains profound.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (קד:): "דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת אָמְרוּ, כֻּלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא". פֵּרוּשׁ "רְשׁוּמוֹת" הוּא מִצַּד הָרְשִׁימָה שֶׁלָּהֶם, דְּכָל אוֹר שֶׁהָיָה, אַף שֶׁנִּתְנַתֵּק, מַנִּיחַ רְשִׁימָה.

As they said in Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 104b), “The expounders of traces said: all of them have a share in the World to Come.” “Traces” means the spiritual imprint that remains: every light that once existed leaves a trace even after it is severed.

וְאֵלּוּ, אַף שֶׁלְּרֹב חֶטְאָם אָבְדוּ וְנִתְּקוּ אוֹר עוֹלָם הַבָּא — הַיְנוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ דְּבֵקוּתָם בַלֵּב בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ — מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר הָיָה זֶה בְּשָׁרְשָׁם בְּתוֹלָדָה, וַעֲדַיִן נִשְׁאַר הָרְשִׁימָה, וּמִצַּד הָרְשִׁימָה דָּרְשׁוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.

These individuals, although through the magnitude of their sins they lost and severed the light of the World to Come—the root of the heart’s attachment to the Blessed One—possessed that attachment innately at their root. Its imprint still remained, and from that imprint the Sages expounded that they do have a share in the World to Come.
וְהֵם דָּרְשׁוּ רַק עַל שִׁשָּׁה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא עַל בִּלְעָם, דְּאֶצְלוֹ לֹא הָיְתָה רְשִׁימָה מֵעוֹלָם.
They applied this teaching only to the six Israelites in that list, not to Balaam, for Balaam had never possessed that inner imprint.

וְאַף שֶׁהוּא זָכָה לְמַה שֶּׁבִּקֵּשׁ — "תָּמֹת וְכוּלֵי" — דְּמִצַּד מִיתַת נַפְשׁוֹ וַאֲבֵדָתוֹ מֵעוֹלָם הַבָּא נִכְלַל בִּכְלַל אוֹתָן מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּמְנוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד חֲזָרָתָן עַל יְדֵי דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת לֹא נִכְלַל עִמָּהֶם כְּלָל.

Thus, although Balaam attained what he requested—“may my soul die, etc.”—in the sense that his soul’s loss of the World to Come placed him in the same Mishnah alongside those Israelites who were listed as having no share, he was not included with them when the “expounders of traces” restored their share through the enduring imprint within them.

items.h:
Seif 3 — Parashat Balak and the Souls at the Edge
Even deniers remain represented within Torah, revealing that Israel's deepest identity survives apparent separation from Moshe's da'at.

p: וְזֶהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק: לְבָרֵר עִנְיָן זֶה, מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, אַף אוֹתָם רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא כְּלָל, שֶׁהֵם כּוֹפְרִים בַּתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי.

This is the entire purpose of Parashat Balak: to clarify Israel’s distinctive spiritual stature relative to the idolatrous nations—even with respect to those wicked Israelites who are said to have no share in the World to Come at all, such as those who deny the Torah, etc.
וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּכוּת לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא הַדַּעַת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד חִבּוּר לְבָבָם לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהֵם נִתְּקוּ מֵעַצְמָם זֶה.
They have severed themselves from the level represented by Moshe Rabbeinu—the da’at of Israel that joins their heart to the Blessed One.
וְלָכֵן לֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ דְּבָרִים אֵלּוּ עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, רַק עַל יְדֵי בִּלְעָם.
For that reason these matters were not originally spoken through Moshe Rabbeinu, but through Balaam.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יד:): "מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כָּתַב סִפְרוֹ וּפָרָשַׁת בִּלְעָם וְכוּלֵי" — נִרְאֶה מִזֶּה כְּאִלּוּ פָּרָשַׁת בִּלְעָם הִיא חוּץ מֵהַתּוֹרָה.

Thus Bava Batra (14b) says, “Moshe Rabbeinu wrote his book and the section of Balaam, etc.,” language that makes the section of Balaam sound as though it were somehow outside the ordinary body of Torah.

וְהַיְנוּ דְּהַתּוֹרָה נִקְרֵאת "תּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה", וְ"סִפְרוֹ" הוּא הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמָתוֹ; אֲבָל פָּרָשַׁת בִּלְעָם אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת לְחָכְמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא מְדַבֵּר מֵאֲנָשִׁים שֶׁכָּפְרוּ בַּתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי.

The Torah is called “the Torah of Moses,” and “his book” corresponds to the reach of Moshe’s wisdom. The Balaam section, however, speaks about people whose condition lies outside the ordinary reach of that wisdom—people who denied Torah, etc.

אֲבָל הֵם בְּדַרְגָא דְּבִלְעָם "יֹדֵעַ דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן": שֶׁהַדַּעַת, דַּרְגָא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַתָּקוּעַ בִּכְלָלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, הוּא אֶצְלָם "עֶלְיוֹן" וּלְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָתָם בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבָּם בְּהַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב, רַק בִּידִיעָה בְּעָלְמָא.

They are instead at Balaam’s level of “knowing the knowledge of the Most High”: the da’at represented by Moshe, embedded in Israel as a whole, is for them “higher”—above what they can inwardly feel in the depths of the heart, remaining only abstract knowledge.

וּבִלְעָם הוּא הַמַּבְחִין מַעֲלָתָם בְּשָׁלֹשׁ נְבוּאוֹת שֶׁאָמַר כְּנֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה כֹּחוֹת הַלֵּב דְּקִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד, שֶׁהִבְחִין אָז שֶׁהוּא הַהֵפֶךְ מִכֻּלָּם עַל יְדֵי שָׁלֹשׁ הַכָּאוֹת דְּאָתוֹן.

Balaam himself becomes the instrument for discerning their stature through the three prophecies he uttered corresponding to the three powers of the heart—jealousy, desire, and honor—when the three blows involving his she-donkey revealed him to be the opposite of all three virtues.
דִּרְכִיבַת הַחֲמוֹר רוֹמֵז עַל מַה שֶּׁהוּא רוֹכֵב עַל הַחֹמֶר הַגּוּפָנִי וּמַנְהִיגוֹ כִּרְצוֹנוֹ; וּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא לֹא הָיָה מַנְהִיגוֹ כִּרְצוֹנוֹ, רַק נִמְשָׁךְ אַחֲרָיו.
Riding the donkey symbolizes riding upon and governing one’s physical materiality. In truth, however, Balaam did not govern his material nature; he was drawn after it.

וּנְבוּאָה רְבִיעִית דְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים הוּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הָרְשִׁימָה. אָז אָמַר "הִנְנִי הוֹלֵךְ לְעַמִּי", שֶׁאָז הִרְגִּישׁ דְּאַף דְּ"תָּמֹת נַפְשִׁי וְכוּלֵי", עִם כָּל זֶה הוּא אָמַר "הִנְנִי הוֹלֵךְ לְעַמִּי", שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אוֹר הָרְשִׁימָה בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים.

The fourth prophecy, concerning the end of days, relates to the revelation of the residual imprint. Then Balaam said, “Behold, I am going to my people”: even after saying “may my soul die [the death of the upright],” he sensed that at the end of days he still goes to his own people, for he lacks Israel’s inner imprint.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר "לְכָה אִיעָצְךָ וְגוֹמֵר" — דְּזֶה עֵצָה לְבָלָק בְּהַפְקָרַת בְּנוֹתָיו, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו.).
This is the meaning of “Come, I will advise you, etc.”: he advised Balak to make the daughters of Moab sexually available, as our Sages of blessed memory explained (Sanhedrin 106a).
הַיְנוּ דְּכָל חֵשֶׁק בָּלָק לִהְיוֹת כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל — יְעָצוֹ לִקְלֹט זֶה עַל יְדֵי הַפְקָרַת בְּנוֹתָיו, דְּיִקְלְטוּ אוֹר מֵהֶם.
Since Balak’s whole desire was to become like Israel, Balaam advised him to absorb something of Israel’s light through such unions with the daughters of Moab.
אַף דְּיָדַע דְּהַבּוֹעֲלֵי אֲרַמִּית הֵם מִפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵרוּבִין (יט.) דְּלָא מְבַשְׁקַר לְהוּ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְאֵין עוֹלִין מִגֵּיהִנָּם.

He knew that those who cohabit with an Aramean woman are among the grave sinners of Israel, to the point that Eruvin (19a) says that our father Abraham does not recognize them and they do not ascend from Gehinnom.

אֲבָל אַחַר שֶׁגִּלָּה לוֹ "אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה הָעָם הַזֶּה" כְּמַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבַּע — הֵם אוֹתָם רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ הַשָּׂגָה בָּהֶם לִהְיוֹת כְּמַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבַּע — דְּגַם הֵם קְדֻשָּׁתָם רַבָּה בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים.

But after revealing to Balak “what this people will do” as though pointing with a finger—referring to those very wicked Israelites who have no share in the World to Come, the level Balaam was capable of perceiving—he showed that even their holiness will be great at the end of days.

עַד שֶׁאַף הוּא, שֶׁהָיָה נָבִיא הַגָּדוֹל מִנְּבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת לָהֶם וְהוֹלֵךְ לְעַמּוֹ נֶגְדָּם. אִם כֵּן מִמֵּילָא נִצְמַח מִזֶּה עֵצָה לְבָלָק בְּהַפְקָרַת בְּנוֹת מוֹאָב.

So great is that residual holiness that even Balaam, foremost among the prophets of the nations, has no share in their destiny and instead returns to his own people. From this, however, Balaam derived his scheme involving the daughters of Moab.

אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא לֹא יָדַע הַהֲלָכָה דְּ"בִּנְךָ הַבָּא מִן הַגּוֹיָה אֵינוֹ קָרוּי בִּנְךָ אֶלָּא בְּנָהּ" (יְבָמוֹת יז.), וְצָרִיךְ לְהַבְדִּיל גַּם הַנּוֹלָד מֵהֶם, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.

He did not know the halakhic principle that “your child born from a gentile woman is not called your child but hers” (Yevamot 17a); even the offspring must therefore be distinguished as not halakhically belonging to Israel through the father.

וּלְפִי שֶׁאוֹתוֹ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא נִרְאֶה שֶׁהוּא הָיָה בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיָצָא מֵהֶם לִהְיוֹת כִּבְנֵי נֵכָר — מִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ מְצִיאוּת יְצִיאַת טִפָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית לְהִתְהַוּוֹת מִמֶּנָּה בֶּן נֵכָר.

Because an Israelite who loses the World to Come appears to have begun within Israel and then gone out to become like a foreigner, this creates the conceptual possibility of an Israelite seed giving rise to offspring who are legally foreign to Israel.

וּכְשֶׁהִשִּׂיג בִּלְעָם דַּרְגָא דְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים, שֶׁאַף אוֹתָן דְּאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכֻנּוּ, חָשַׁב דְּגַם אוֹתָן טִפּוֹת הֵם כֵּן, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין מְצִיאוּת לְטִפָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת כְּלָל.

When Balaam perceived that at the end of days even those with no share in the World to Come are still called by the name Israel, he mistakenly thought the same would apply to such seed, reasoning that an Israelite point could never truly change.

וּבֶאֱמֶת וַדַּאי אוֹתָן טִפּוֹת בָּאִים גַּם כֵּן בַּחֲזָרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק לֹא כְּמַחֲשֶׁבֶת אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע שֶׁבָּזֶה יִהְיֶה עֵצָה וְתִקּוּן לְאֻמַּת מוֹאָב, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לַקְּדֻשָּׁה שַׁיָּכוּת גַּם אֶצְלָם; דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר, כִּי "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי".

In the deeper providential process those sparks can indeed ultimately return to Israel, but not as Balaam imagined—that this would provide a rectification for Moab by making holiness belong within Moab itself. That cannot be, for “He did not do so for any nation.”
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהַטִּפּוֹת בְּלוּעוֹת בַּגּוֹיִם הֵם מִכְּלַל הַגּוֹיִם וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּכוּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק כְּשֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ לְהִקָּלֵט בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
As long as those sparks are absorbed among the nations, they are counted there and have no active connection to Israel; their return occurs only when they are reabsorbed into Israel.
וּבֶאֱמֶת עֵצָה זוֹ דַּיְקָא הָיְתָה הֲכָנָה לְ"מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה הָעָם הַזֶּה וְגוֹמֵר" וּ"מָחַץ פַּאֲתֵי מוֹאָב" — קוֹדֵם לַכֹּל לְהוֹצִיא בִּלְעָם מִפִּיהֶם.

In truth, that very scheme became the preparation for “what this people will do, etc.” and “he shall crush the corners of Moab”—first of all, by extracting from Moab the holiness that Balaam sought to capture.
וְהוּא לֹא יָדַע בְּעַצְמוֹ מַה שֶּׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר: דְּ"לְכָה אִיעָצְךָ, אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה וְגוֹמֵר" — דְּבָרִים כִּכְתָבָן, שֶׁהוּא הָיָה נוֹתֵן לוֹ עֵצָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה הָעָם וְגוֹמֵר.

Balaam himself did not grasp the prophetic irony of his own words: “Come, I will advise you—what this people will do…” literally meant that the advice he was giving would itself bring about what Israel would ultimately do to Moab.

וּלְפִי שֶׁבְּעִילַת אֲרַמִּית הִיא הִתְעָרְבוּת בָּאֻמּוֹת גַּם כֵּן הֵפֶךְ דַּרְגָא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא בָּא מִצַּד חֶסְרוֹן הַדַּעַת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ה הֲלָכָה ב): "אִם אֵין דֵּעָה — הַבְדָּלָה מִנַּיִן".

Since cohabitation with an Aramean woman is itself a form of intermingling with the nations, it stands opposite the level of Moshe and arises from a deficiency of da’at, as the Yerushalmi teaches (Berakhot 5:2): “If there is no understanding, from where can there be separation?”
וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דֵּעָה, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהִדָּבֵק עִם גּוֹיָה כְּלָל.
Such a person fails to apprehend the distinction between Israel and the nations; one who possesses true da’at cannot attach himself in that way.
וְלָכֵן נֶעְלַם מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הֲלָכָה זוֹ דְּבּוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית מַה דִּינוֹ, שֶׁהוּא אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת לָזֶה כְּלָל.
For this reason the law governing one who cohabits with an Aramean woman was hidden from Moshe Rabbeinu: his own spiritual level had no experiential connection to such confusion.

עַד שֶׁבָּא פִּינְחָס, שֶׁאָמְרוּ עָלָיו שְׁבָטִים "בֶּן פּוּטִי וְכוּלֵי", שֶׁמִּצַּד הַזֶּה שֶׁבָּא מִיִּתְרוֹ הָיָה לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת לַהֲלָכָה זוֹ, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (לט:): "מִינֵּיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא וְכוּלֵי".

It was Pinchas who acted, and the tribes disparaged him as “the son of Puti, etc.” Precisely because one side of his ancestry came through Yitro, he had a point of contact with this law, in the spirit of the saying in Sanhedrin (39b), “from within it and by means of it…”
וְלָכֵן נִכְתַּב גַּם זֶה בְּסִיּוּם פָּרָשַׁת בִּלְעָם, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת לְחָכְמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְהַשָּׂגָתוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
Therefore this episode too appears at the conclusion of the Balaam section, a realm that is not naturally related to Moshe Rabbeinu’s own mode of wisdom and attainment, as explained above.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם, אַחַר שֶׁגִּלָּה בִּלְעָם דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ, הוֹצִיא מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּלְעוֹ מִפִּיו וְנִכְתְּבוּ בַּתּוֹרָה עַל יָדוֹ.
Nevertheless, once Balaam had revealed these matters, Moshe Rabbeinu extracted what Balaam had “swallowed” and incorporated it into Torah through his own writing.
אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה דִּבְאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים מִצַּד הָרְשִׁימוּ גַּם הֵם בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, מִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּכוּת לַתּוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן.
Once it was revealed that at the end of days, by virtue of the residual imprint, even those estranged sinners remain included within Israel, it follows that they too possess a connection to Torah.
וְכָל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה כַּנּוֹדָע; וְנַפְשׁוֹת הַכּוֹפְרִים וְהַמְשֻׁמָּדִים הֵם מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁבְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ.
All Jewish souls are rooted in the letters of the Torah, as is known; the souls of deniers and apostates correspond to the letters contained in this very section.
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁהוּא חוּץ לְתוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם הוּא מִכְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה מַמָּשׁ, וְאֵין שׁוּם הֶבְדֵּל בֵּין פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ לְפָרָשַׁת "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל".

Although this section appears to stand outside “the Torah of Moses,” it is in truth fully part of Torah itself; in sanctity there is no difference between this section and the section beginning “Hear, O Israel.”

items.h:
Seif 4 — Why Balak Could Have Entered the Shema
Parashat Balak teaches that even extreme sinners remain within Israel's unity, though this truth need not be rehearsed daily.

p: וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יב:) דְּבִקְּשׁוּ לִקְבֹּעַ פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, הַיְנוּ לְכַוָּנָה זוֹ: שֶׁאַף פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּכְלַל אַחְדוּת הָאֻמָּה, וְיֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק בַּ"הַשֵּׁם אֶחָד", וְנִבְדָּלִים מֵעַמִּים כָּאָמוּר.

They said (Berakhot 12b) that the Sages wished to establish Parashat Balak as part of the daily Shema. The intention was precisely this: even the sinners of Israel remain within the unity of the nation, have a share in “God is One,” and remain distinct from the nations as described above.

וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה טָמְנוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם בְּרֶמֶז כְּדַרְכָּם, מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם) דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם — רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר שֶׁאָז הַתְחָלַת הֶבְדֵּל הָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית, "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי", אַף שֶׁהַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵי (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כג).

Our Sages of blessed memory concealed this idea in allusion, as was their way, when they explained there that the section contains the Exodus from Egypt: that event marked the beginning of Israel’s separation as a nation, “a nation from the midst of a nation,” even though “these worshipped idols and those worshipped idols, etc.” (Vayikra Rabbah 23).
וְ"כָרַע שָׁכַב כַּאֲרִי" — הַיְנוּ אַף דְּהֵם בְּדִיּוֹטָא הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, שְׁכִיבָא לְעַפְרָא, הֵם כַּאֲרִי.
And “he crouched, he lay down like a lion” means that even when Israel is on the lowest rung, lying in the dust, they still retain the inner identity of a lion.

וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע "בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ" — רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר, בֵּין שֶׁהֵם בְּמַעֲלָה עֶלְיוֹנָה, בֵּין בְּמַדְרֵגָה תַּחְתּוֹנָה, אֵינוֹ נִתָּק מִקַּבָּלַת עֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁעָלָיו וְהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּ"הַשֵּׁם אֶחָד".

This is the meaning of the Shema’s phrase “when you lie down and when you rise”: whether Israel stands on a lofty level or a low one, the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven upon them and their bond to the One God is not severed.

וְלֹא קְבָעוּהָ מִפְּנֵי טֹרַח צִבּוּר, דְּ"כָל פָּרָשָׁה דְּלָא פַסְקֵיהּ מֹשֶׁה וְכוּלֵי" — רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר, דְּסִדּוּר הַפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת וַדַּאי הַמְכֻוָּן דְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן אֵינוֹ נִשְׁלָם אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי כָּל הַפָּרָשָׁה כֻּלָּהּ דַּוְקָא, דְּלָכֵן לֹא פַסְקֵיהּ מֹשֶׁה.

They did not institute it because of the burden it would place on the congregation, since “any passage that Moses did not divide…” This means that the Torah’s paragraph structure is deliberate: this theme is completed only through the entire section, which is why Moses did not break it into a shorter liturgical unit.

וּפָרָשַׁת בָּלָק, שֶׁהוּא גִּלּוּי קֶשֶׁר יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אַף הַמּוֹרְדִים וּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתַכְלִית הַתֹּקֶף, בֵּרוּר זֶה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּפִי סֵדֶר הַפָּרָשָׁה, עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּבְהִתְבּוֹנְנוּתָם בְּדַעַת שֶׁלָּהֶם הֵם מְבָרְרִים לָעַיִן מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּזֶה.

Parashat Balak reveals the bond between Israel and the Blessed One even at the extreme point of rebellion and sin. This clarification emerges only through the full order of the parashah: the nations’ attempt to become like Israel, and their own intellectual reflection, ultimately make Israel’s unique inner stature visible.

וְכֵן בְּכָל דּוֹר כֵּן הוּא סֵדֶר הַבֵּרוּר, עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁטּוֹעֲנִים "אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא, כִּי תִשָּׂא לד).

The same pattern of clarification recurs in every generation, through movements among the nations that claim, in effect, “we are Israel,” as our Sages of blessed memory described (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 34).
וְלָכֵן נִקְרֵאת הַפָּרָשָׁה עַל שֵׁם בָּלָק, לֹא עַל שֵׁם בִּלְעָם, כִּי בָּלָק הוּא הָיָה הַמִּתְעוֹרֵר בָּזֶה.
Therefore the parashah is called after Balak, not Balaam, because Balak was the one who initiated this challenge. –
וְסִיּוּמָהּ דְּ"בִלְעָם שָׁב לִמְקוֹמוֹ" — הַיְנוּ לְעַמּוֹ, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק לִמְקוֹמוֹ בַּאֲרָם, שֶׁהוּא בַּאֲחוֹרַיִם דִּקְדֻשָּׁה כַּנּוֹדָע.

[[The ending, “Balaam returned to his place,” means that he returned to his own people, for he has no connection to Israel, but only to his place in Aram, associated in Kabbalistic language with the “back side” of holiness.]

אֲבָל "בָּלָק הָלַךְ לְדַרְכּוֹ" — הוּא הַדֶּרֶךְ הַנִּזְכָּר בַּכָּתוּב לִרְדֹּף אַחַר קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל; דְּעַל כֵּן הִזְנָה בְּנוֹת מוֹאָב, כִּי נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה מְכַשְׁכֵּשׁ בְּמֵעָיו וְלֹא הָיָה מַנִּיחוֹ לִשְׁקֹט מִזֶּה.]

[But “Balak went on his way”: he continued on the path described in the verse, pursuing a connection to Israel’s holiness. Hence his involvement with the daughters of Moab, for the holy spark of King David, peace be upon him, was stirring within him and would not allow him to rest from this pursuit.]

וְשֵׁם שֶׁל כָּל סִדְרָה שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה, כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁנָּהֲגוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִקְרוֹתָהּ, הוּא הַמְכֻוָּן שֶׁל כָּל הַסִּדְרָה, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּשְׁמוֹת בְּנֵי אָדָם וְכָל הַשֵּׁמוֹת דִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַחַיּוּת דְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר.

The name by which Israel customarily calls each Torah portion expresses the inner intent of the entire portion, just as our Sages teach regarding human names and, more broadly, all names in the Holy Tongue: the name is the root of a thing’s life-force.
מִסְּתָמָא כֵּן גַּם בִּשְׁמוֹת סִפְרֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ כֻּלָּם, וְכֵן בִּשְׁמוֹת פָּרָשׁוֹת הַתּוֹרָה.
Presumably the same is true of the names of all sacred books and of the names of the Torah portions.

וְזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר זֶה הַטָּמוּן בְּרִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ בָּלָק — שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הָרְדִיפָה דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְגָרֵשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכִּסּוּי עֵין הָאָרֶץ.

This is the root by which the hidden light within Israel’s sinners becomes revealed: through the force represented by Balak—the drive of the nations to become like Israel and to dislodge Israel from its unique relation to the “eye of the Land.”

וְהִתְגַּלּוּת כֹּחַ זֶה בָּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁחוֹטְאִים כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁאָבְדוּ חֵלֶק עוֹלָם הַבָּא וְנִתְגָּרְשׁוּ מֵהָאָרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה; עַל יְדֵי זֶה צוֹמֵחַ כֹּחַ אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לִטְעֹן שֶׁגַּם הֵם כֵּן.

This claim gains force among the nations only when some Israelites sin so severely that they seem to have lost the World to Come and been expelled from the supernal Land; this creates room for the nations to argue that they too can occupy the same spiritual place.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה עַצְמוֹ מִתְבָּרֵר וּמִתְגַּלֶּה מַעֲלַת אוֹתָן רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאוֹר הָרְשִׁימָה שֶׁלָּהֶם.
Yet that very challenge becomes the means by which the deeper stature of those Jewish sinners and the light of their residual imprint are clarified and revealed.

וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יד:) קְרָאוּהָ "פָּרָשַׁת בִּלְעָם"; דְּמִצַּד מַה שֶּׁנִּכְתְּבָה הַפָּרָשָׁה בַּתּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַמָּשׁ, הוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבַּסּוֹף, וְ"סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה" — שֹׁרֶשׁ הַהִתְגַּלּוּת נִצְמַח מִבָּלָק.

Our Sages of blessed memory (Bava Batra 14b) called it “the section of Balaam.” From the perspective of its having been written into the Torah as actual words of Torah, the section represents the final revelation; and since “the end of the deed is first in thought,” the root of that revelation began with Balak’s challenge.

אֲבָל רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁדִּבְּרוּ מִמֶּנָּה כְּאִלּוּ הִיא חוּץ מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה, קְרָאוּהָ עַל שֵׁם בִּלְעָם "הַיֹּדֵעַ דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן", כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַדַּעַת שֶׁלֹּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַשָּׂגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּלָל.

But when the Sages speak of it as though it stands outside the ordinary “Torah of Moses,” they name it for Balaam, “the one who knows the knowledge of the Most High,” because it concerns a mode of da’at wholly unlike Moshe Rabbeinu’s inward attainment.

וּמִצַּד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל הַכְּשֵׁרִים שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעוּ לְמַדְרֵגַת "אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא", חַס וְשָׁלוֹם — אֵין שַׁיָּכוּת לָהֶם לָזֶה כְּלָל, וְכַנִּכְתָּב לְעֵיל.

Moshe Rabbeinu and upright Israelites who, God forbid, have never descended to the level described as “having no share in the World to Come” have no direct experiential relation to this theme, as explained above.
וְלָכֵן זֶה נֶחְשָׁב לְטֹרַח צִבּוּר, דִּכְלַל הַצִּבּוּר אֵינָם פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְזִכְרוֹן כָּל פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ הוּא טֹרַח לָהֶם, וְכָאָמוּר.

For this reason including the whole section in the daily Shema would count as an undue burden on the congregation: the community as a whole is not composed of such extreme sinners, and rehearsing this entire process each day would be burdensome for them, as stated.

sections.en: Affliction, Consolation, and the End of the Year

items.h: The year closes through darkness followed by consolation, teaching that suffering itself is ultimately reread as part of the divine movement toward light.

Seif 1 — Affliction before Consolation
The year's closing haftarot mirror creation's movement from darkness to light, revealing suffering itself within divine consolation.

p: עִנְיַן סִיּוּם הַשָּׁנָה בִּתְלָת דְּפוּרְעָנוּתָא וְשֶׁבַע דְּנֶחֶמְתָּא, שֶׁמַּפְטִירִין בְּעֶשֶׂר שַׁבָּתוֹת אַחֲרוֹנִים דְּכָל שָׁנָה,
The significance of concluding the year with the Three Haftarot of Affliction and the Seven of Consolation, which are read during the final ten Shabbatot of every year,
שֶׁהִיא סִיּוּם הַקּוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה וּזְמַן שֶׁל כְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה,
is that the year represents the completion of an entire structure and the full cycle of creation as a whole.
שֶׁהִיא (שַׁבָּת עז:) כִּבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא,
It follows the pattern of the world's creation (Shabbat 77b): first darkness, and afterward light.
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סו): צַדִּיקִים תְּחִלָּתָן יִסּוּרִין וְסוֹפָן שַׁלְוָה.
This accords with what they taught (Bereishit Rabbah 66): the righteous begin with suffering, but their end is tranquility.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּהַהַתְחָלָה מְחוּלָק לְשָׁלֹשׁ, וְהַסּוֹף בְּהוֹצָאַת הַדָּבָר לַפּוֹעַל מְחוּלָק לְשֶׁבַע,
It is known that the beginning is divided into three, while the end—the stage in which the matter is brought into actuality—is divided into seven.
כַּנּוֹדָע מִסֵּדֶר הָעֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת, שֶׁשָּׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת הֵם כֹּחוֹת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, וְשֶׁבַע תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת הֵם כֹּחוֹת הַהַמְשָׁכָה לַפּוֹעַל.
This is known from the order of the Ten Sefirot: the first three are the powers of thought, and the lower seven are the powers through which thought is extended into action.
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: בַּתְּחִלָּה עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה לִבְרוֹא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין, וְאַחַר כָּךְ שִׁיתֵּף מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים.
This follows the teaching that at first it arose in the Divine thought to create the world through the Attribute of Judgment, and afterward He joined to it the Attribute of Mercy.
וּמִזֶּה מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (מְנָחוֹת כט:) בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: כָּךְ עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה לְפָנַי,
This is also the meaning of what was said concerning Rabbi Akiva (Menachot 29b): 'Thus it arose in thought before Me.'
רָצָה לוֹמַר, כְּפִי הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין.
That is to say, this was in accordance with the level of thought, where creation was conceived through the Attribute of Judgment.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, לֹא חָשִׁיד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא דְּעָבֵיד דִּינָא בְּלָא דִּינָא, אַף בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין;
Nevertheless, the Holy One, blessed be He, is not suspected of administering judgment without justice, even when acting through the Attribute of Judgment.
וְהוּא טָעַן: זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְזוֹ שְׂכָרָהּ, שֶׁאֵין מַגִּיעַ לוֹ בְּדִין זֶה.
Moshe's protest—'This is Torah and this is its reward?'—was precisely that such a judgment did not appear to be deserved.
וְאָמְנָם בֶּאֱמֶת יָדוּעַ דְּכֹחוֹת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, שָׁם הַדִּין בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם,
Yet in truth it is known that within the powers of thought, judgment exists in the most concealed form.
וְאֵין גִּילּוּי דִּין כְּלָל אֶלָּא בַּיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל, וְזֶה לִכְאוֹרָה הֵיפֶךְ הַנִּזְכָּר.
Judgment becomes manifest only when it emerges into actuality, which at first glance seems the reverse of what was just explained.
אֲבָל עִנְיַן חִילּוּק בֵּין מַחֲשָׁבָה לַסּוֹף הַיְנוּ לִהְיוֹת: "עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים הָאָדָם יָשָׁר, וְהֵמָּה בִקְשׁוּ וְגוֹמֵר", בְּמַה שֶּׁמָּסַר הַבְּחִירָה.
The distinction between thought and the final outcome is rooted in the verse, 'God made man upright, but they sought, etc.,' for God entrusted man with free choice.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה שֶׁיִּבְחוֹר רַק בַּטּוֹב, וְזֶהוּ תַכְלִית מְכֻוָּן שֶׁל מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּבְּרִיאָה;
The Blessed One desired that man choose only the good, and this was the ultimate intention of His thought in creation.
אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁמָּסַר הַבְּחִירָה לָאָדָם, הֲרֵי סִילֵּק רְצוֹן מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בָּזֶה.
Yet once He gave free choice to man, He seemingly withdrew the compelling force of that original intention.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, עַל הָאֱמֶת גַּם אַחַר שֶׁמָּסַר הַבְּחִירָה, עֲדַיִן הַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ,
Nevertheless, in ultimate truth, even after free choice was entrusted to man, everything still comes from Him.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי מִמְּךָ הַכֹּל וְגוֹמֵר" לְעִנְיַן הַטּוֹבָה, וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן הַהֵפֶךְ: "לָמָּה תַתְעֵנוּ וְגוֹמֵר".
Thus Scripture says, 'For everything is from You, etc.,' regarding good, and likewise regarding its opposite, 'Why do You cause us to stray, etc.'
וְזֶהוּ תַכְלִית הַבְּחִירָה: לְהַגִּיעַ עַל יָדָהּ לִידִיעָה בְרוּרָה שֶׁאֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ גַּם מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם.
This is the ultimate purpose of free choice: through it one must arrive at the clear knowledge that there is nothing besides Him, even within the created world.
וְזוֹ הִיא צוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁחֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
This is the form of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, which is engraved upon the Throne of Glory.
שֶׁצּוּרָתוֹ הִיא כּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל הַצּוּרוֹת וְהַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
His form encompasses all the forms and souls of Israel.
וְזֶהוּ קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי הַמְחַבֵּר שֶׁבַע תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת עִם שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת, לִהְיוֹת כּוּלָּא חַד מַמָּשׁ.
This is the middle line that joins the seven lower Sefirot with the first three, so that all is literally one.
וְהִנֵּה כְּפִי הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַכֹּל עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַטּוֹב, הִנֵּה זֶה נִקְרָא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין,
According to the original thought that everything should proceed in the way of good, this itself is termed the Attribute of Judgment.
דְּתַכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה לְהֵטִיב, וּכְשֶׁהַטּוֹב מַגִּיעַ בְּמִשְׁפָּט, וַדַּאי שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאוֹד".
For the purpose of creation is to bestow good, and when that good is attained by right and judgment, it is certainly called 'very good.'
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט), דְּזֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע וּמָוֶת וְשֵׁינָה,
This is what our Sages of blessed memory taught (Bereishit Rabbah 9), that 'very good' includes the evil inclination, death, and sleep.
שֶׁכָּל זֶה בִּיטּוּל לְהַטּוֹב, רַק דְּכָל זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ מִן הַ"טּוֹב מְאוֹד";
All of these appear to negate the good, yet they themselves flow from the level of 'very good.'
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה לִהְיוֹת טוֹב מְאוֹד, וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֹּחַ בְּחִירָה וְיֵצֶר הָרָע, וְהֵם יִבְחֲרוּ בַּטּוֹב.
That is, the Blessed One desired that the good be 'very good,' which is possible when there is free choice and an evil inclination, and human beings nevertheless choose the good.
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר כָּךְ מַה שֶּׁנִּמְשָׁךְ, וְלִהְיוֹת גַּם אַחַר כָּךְ כּוּלָּא חַד, מִמֵּילָא גַּם אַחַר כָּךְ זֶה נִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאוֹד".
From this came all that subsequently unfolded; and because even afterward everything is ultimately one, the later course of events too is included within 'very good.'
וְהַיְינוּ לֶעָתִיד, כְּשֶׁיְּבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח וְיִתְבַּעֵר יֵצֶר הָרָע, יְבוֹרַר אֵיךְ זֶה מִכְּלַל "טוֹב מְאוֹד", שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הִגִּיעַ הַטּוֹב בְּמִשְׁפָּט.

In the future, when death is swallowed up forever and the evil inclination is eradicated, it will become clear how all of this belonged to 'very good,' for through it the good was attained through judgment.
וְהִנֵּה וַדַּאי הָיָה בִּתְחִלַּת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה חִלּוּקֵי מַדְרֵיגוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
Certainly, from the beginning of the Divine thought there were to be differing levels between Israel and the nations.
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן, מֵאַיִן נִתְהַוָּה זֶה אַחַר כָּךְ? וְכָךְ בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: חֲשׁוֹכָא וּנְהוֹרָא.
For if not, from where could this distinction later have arisen? This too is the pattern of creation: darkness and light.
אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הָיָה הַכֹּל טוֹב, וַדַּאי גַּם הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לֹא הָיָה הַמְכֻוָּן שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵם.
Yet since the original Divine thought was entirely good, the intention for the nations was certainly not that they remain as they later became.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּמִּיתִי לַעֲשׂוֹת לָהֶם, אֶעֱשֶׂה לָכֶם", וְלֹא אָמַר "כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי";
Regarding this it is said, 'And it shall be, as I intended to do to them, so I shall do to you'—it does not say, 'as I did.'
שֶׁכְּבָר עָשָׂה רַע לְעַמְמִין בְּפוֹעַל, שֶׁלֹּא לְהַחֲיוֹת כָּל נְשָׁמָה, אוֹ עוֹנְשֵׁי שְׁאָר אוּמּוֹת; חָלִילָה לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
For He had already brought actual destruction upon nations, such as the command not to leave alive any soul, and the punishments of other peoples; Heaven forbid that such a thing be done to Israel.
כִּי אֲבַדּוֹן הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הוּא אֲבַדָּן נִצְחִי.
For the destruction of the nations, in that sense, is a lasting destruction.
וְרַק "כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּמִּיתִי" — וְרָצָה לוֹמַר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁעָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה,
Rather, the verse says only 'as I intended'—meaning, as they existed in the original Divine thought.
דְּמִצַּד מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּבוּקִים בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מַמָּשׁ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ לֶעָתִיד,
For according to His thought, Israel were to be actually bound to Him, as they will be in the future.
הָיָה שֶׁהָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת יִהְיוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵם יִשְׂרָאֵל עַכְשָׁיו: שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לְקַבֵּל רוֹב טוֹבָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְסוֹף סוֹף גַּם הֵם יִזֻכְּכוּ.
The nations, in that design, would have been on the level Israel occupies now: unable to receive an abundance of good in this world, yet ultimately destined for refinement.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא הֵם נִכְרְתוּ לְגַמְרֵי, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁבוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
Through sin, however, the nations became entirely cut off, while Israel came to occupy the position that the original thought had assigned to the nations.
שֶׁאֵין הַכֹּחוֹת וְהָרְצוֹנוֹת וְהַפְּעוּלוֹת נִמְשָׁכִים כָּל כָּךְ אַחַר רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אַךְ עִם כָּל זֶה שׁוֹרְשָׁם דָּבוּק בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים.
Their powers, desires, and actions do not always follow the Blessed One's will completely, yet their root remains attached to the living God.
וְנִמְצָא, מַה שֶּׁאֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכוֹלִים לְקַבֵּל רוֹב טוֹבָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא רַק מִצַּד שֶׁהֵרֵעוּ אֶת מַעֲשָׂם וְקִיפְּחוּ אֶת פַּרְנָסָתָם, רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן.
It follows that Israel's inability to receive an abundance of good in this world results only from having impaired their deeds and thereby diminished their sustenance—may the Merciful One save us.
אֲבָל בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ: שׁוֹרְשָׁם, אִם הָיוּ כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הָיָה רָאוּי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן;
With the nations, however, the matter is the reverse: at their root, had they remained according to the Divine will, this limited worldly condition would have been appropriate to them.
וּמִצַּד שֶׁהֵרֵעוּ מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם יֵשׁ לָהֶם מִשַּׁלְוַת הָרְשָׁעִים לְקַפְּחָם מֵעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
Because they corrupted their deeds, they are granted the tranquility of the wicked in this world in a manner that deprives them of the World to Come.
וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, שֶׁהָיָה בֶּן גֵּרִים, עַל זֶה אָמַר: "כָּךְ עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה",
Regarding Rabbi Akiva, who descended from converts, this is the meaning of the response, 'Thus it arose in thought.'
שֶׁעוֹנְשָׁיו אֵינוֹ מִצַּד בְּחִירָה דְּרַע בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק מִצַּד שׁוֹרְשׁוֹ בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה.
His suffering was not rooted in an evil choice in this world, but in the dimension of his root within the primordial thought.
וְזֶהוּ "שְׁתוֹק", דְּבַמַּחֲשָׁבָה אֵין שָׁם דִּבּוּר, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג דָּבָר אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מַגִּיעַ לְאוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵיגָה שֶׁהוּא הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַדִּבּוּר.
This is the meaning of 'Be silent': at the level of thought there is no speech, and it cannot be grasped unless one reaches that level where speech falls away.
וּבֵיאוּר זֶה, כִּי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הוּא יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, כַּיָּדוּעַ, שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת לַיְלָה;
The explanation is that Rabbi Akiva is the foundation of the Oral Torah, as is known, and the Oral Torah corresponds to the quality of night.
דְּהַיְינוּ הַשָּׂגַת יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דְּחוֹמֶר וּלְבֵינִים, לִבּוּן הִלְכְתָא הָאָמוּר בַּזּוֹהַר (חֵלֶק א כז עַמּוּד א),
That is, it is Israel's mode of attainment in this world through exertion—the 'mortar and bricks' of clarifying halakhah, as stated in the Zohar (I, 27a).
כִּי אוֹר יוֹם, שֶׁכֵּן יִהְיֶה אוֹר הַלְּבָנָה דְּלֶעָתִיד, הַכֹּל אוֹר עַצְמִי, הוּא אוֹרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמֵּאִיר לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם.
The light of day—like the light of the moon in the future—is intrinsic light: the Blessed One's own light illuminating all who enter the world.
וְזֶהוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, וְהִיא כְּתִיבָא וּמַנְּחָא לְכָל מִי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה,
This corresponds to the Written Torah, which is written and laid openly before anyone who wishes to approach it.
עַד שֶׁאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אוֹמְרִים: אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תִּשָּׂא לד), דְּמִי שֶׁיְּגַלֶּה מִסְטוֹרִין וְכוּלֵי.
Indeed, the nations can claim, 'We are Israel,' as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Midrash Tanchuma, Tisa 34), regarding one who reveals the hidden mysteries, etc.
תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא הַמְבָרֵר הַחִילּוּק, רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁאַף בְּהֶעְלֵם: "וְכִי אֵשֵׁב בַּחוֹשֶׁךְ, הַשֵּׁם אוֹר לִי",
The Oral Torah is what clarifies the distinction: even within concealment, 'Though I sit in darkness, the Lord is a light for me.'
בְּאוֹר הַלְּבָנָה הַמְקַבֵּל מֵאוֹר הַחַמָּה, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹנִין לָהּ, כִּי "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי".
It is the moonlight that receives from the sun, and Israel reckons its calendar by the moon, for 'He has not done so for any nation.'
וְהוּא מִצַּד הַדִּבּוּר, שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה לַפּוֹעַל;
This belongs to the level of speech, which is the revelation of thought as it emerges into actuality.
וּמִצַּד הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, הֲרֵי הָיָה אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם רְאוּיִם לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹ עַכְשָׁיו יִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק שֶׁבַּהִתְגַּלּוּת נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁאֵין כֵּן.
From the perspective of the original thought, the nations could have occupied the level Israel occupies now; only in the stage of revelation was it clarified that this is not so.
וְהַבִּירוּר עַל יְדֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּיִחוּד, שֶׁהָיָה רֹאשׁ חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּדוֹרוֹ,
This clarification came particularly through Rabbi Akiva, who was the foremost Sage of Israel in his generation.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת טז.) שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ הוֹלֵךְ מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ; וַדַּאי הִילּוּךְ הַשֵּׁם הַיְינוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחוֹתָיו, הָיָה בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ,
As they said (Yevamot 16a), his name went from one end of the world to the other. The spread of his name signifies the extension of his spiritual powers throughout the world.
כִּי הוּא כּוֹלֵל הַדּוֹר, שֶׁכֵּן אוֹתִיּוֹת שְׁמוֹ יַעֲקֹב-א, כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִיא כּוֹלֶלֶת נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל דּוֹר וָדוֹר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
For he encompassed his generation; the letters of his name allude to Yaakov plus alef, since the root-soul of Jacob our father, peace be upon him, encompasses the souls of every generation of Israel.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא בֶּן גֵּרִים, וַדַּאי הָיָה בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן אֵיזֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ מֵאֲבוֹתָיו,
In truth, the root of his soul was a soul of Israel; nevertheless, because he descended from converts, some root from his ancestors was certainly present within him as well.
וְהוּא אֵיזֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ טוֹב שֶׁהָיָה גָּנוּז בָּהֶם מִצַּד שֶׁעָלוּ בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה.
That was the hidden root of good within them, deriving from the way they had existed in the original Divine thought.
וְכָל מַעֲלַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הֵם מִצַּד הַדִּבּוּר בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהוּא הַיְּסוֹד,
All of Rabbi Akiva's distinctive greatness belongs to the level of speech in the Oral Torah, of which he is the foundation.
וּבוֹ נִתְבָּרֵר תַּכְלִית הַבִּירוּר בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים, שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם חֵלֶק מֵהֶם כְּלָל.
Through him the ultimate distinction between Israel and the nations was clarified: in this revealed level he contains no portion of them at all.
רַק מִצַּד הַהִתְעַלּוּת מֵעוֹלַם הַדִּבּוּר לַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, דְּשָׁם יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב הַנִּמְצָא בָהֶם שֶׁקְּלָטָהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
Only when rising from the world of speech to the level of thought is there a certain good found among them, which Rabbi Akiva absorbed.
מִצַּד אוֹתוֹ קְלִיטַת טוֹב דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הִגִּיעַ לוֹ הָעוֹנֶשׁ.
It was from that absorption of the good rooted in the primordial thought concerning the nations that his suffering came.
אַף דְּזוֹ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּדִבּוּר, שֶׁהָיָה הוֹגֶה יוֹם וָלַיְלָה, וּמִצַּד הַדִּבּוּר לֹא שַׁיֵּיךְ לָזֶה,
Although his Oral Torah was expressed through speech, which he studied day and night, and from the standpoint of speech there was no connection to this ancestral root,
וּבַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָכָה לְ"טוֹב מְאוֹד", וְהוּא הַנְּהוֹרָא דְּעִמֵּיהּ שַׁרְיָא;
at the level of thought he attained the 'very good'—the hidden light that rested with him.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, "יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ": דְּכַלְפֵּי דִידֵיהּ הוּא נְהוֹרָא וְ"טוֹב מְאוֹד", אֲבָל כְּלַפֵּי דִידַן הוּא בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא.
Nevertheless, 'He makes darkness His concealment': from His perspective it is light and 'very good,' while from our perspective it first appears as darkness.
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַהֶעְלֵם בָּאִים לַגִּילּוּי, וְ"וְכִי אֵשֵׁב בַּחוֹשֶׁךְ" דַּיְיקָא, אָז "הַשֵּׁם אוֹר לִי".
Only by passing through concealment does one come to revelation; specifically when 'I sit in darkness,' then 'the Lord is a light for me.'
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (גִּיטִּין מג.): אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשַׁל,
This is as they said (Gittin 43a): a person does not fully comprehend words of Torah unless he has first stumbled in them.
עַד שֶׁדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה נִקְרָא "הַמִּכְשֵׁלָה הַזֹּאת", וְזֶה פֶּלֶא, כְּאִלּוּ דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה מַכְשִׁילִין, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
Indeed, words of Torah are even called 'this stumbling block.' This is astonishing, as though Torah itself causes a person to stumble—Heaven forbid.
רַק הוֹאִיל וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמוֹד בָּעִנְיָן אַחֵר, הֲרֵי הַמִּכְשׁוֹל הֲכָנָה אֶל הָעֲמִידָה עַל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.
Rather, because there is no other way to arrive at full understanding, the stumbling itself becomes a preparation for grasping the words of Torah.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה "בְּרֹאשׁ הוֹמִיּוֹת תִּקְרָא" לִרְדּוֹף אַחֲרֶיהָ, וְכֹחָהּ יָפֶה לְהַזְמִין כָּל מִינֵי סִיַּיעְתּוֹת לָאָדָם לַעֲמוֹד עַל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה,
Since the Torah 'calls at the head of the noisy streets,' summoning a person to pursue it, it has the power to arrange every form of assistance that will enable him to attain its words.
גַּם זֶה מִכְּלַל הַסִּיַּיעְתּוֹת: לְהַזְמִין לְפָנָיו בַּהַתְחָלָה מִכְשָׁלוֹת, כְּדֵי לַעֲמוֹד עַל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.
Even this is included among those forms of assistance: that stumbling blocks are placed before him at the beginning so that he can ultimately stand firmly in the words of Torah.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, כָּךְ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבָּהּ נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, וְהוּא הַדְּפוּס שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית,
Just as this is the pattern of the world's creation, so it is with the Torah through which the world was created, for Torah is the blueprint of the work of Creation.
מִסְּתָמָא גַּם הִיא כְּעִנְיַן בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם מַמָּשׁ.
It follows that Torah itself must reflect precisely the same pattern as the creation of the world.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פט:): "חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית",
This is what they said (Shabbat 89b): 'Your sins are like these years, ordered and coming from the six days of Creation.'
הַיְנוּ שֶׁכָּךְ הוּא סֵדֶר יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית.
That is, this itself belongs to the ordered pattern of the days of Creation.
וְנִמְצָא, כָּל הָעֲוֹנוֹת וְעוֹנְשֵׁיהֶם, הַכֹּל "כָּךְ עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה" בַּהֲכָנַת הַיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל,
It follows that all sins and their punishments were included in the sense of 'thus it arose in thought,' as part of the preparation for the eventual emergence into actuality.
שֶׁמִּתְבָּרֵר אַחַר שֶׁיּוֹצֵא לַפּוֹעַל: כְּשֶׁעוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה אַחַר שֶׁנִּכְשַׁל, אָז מֵבִין אֵיךְ הַמִּכְשׁוֹל הָיָה בּוֹ צוֹרֶךְ וְסִיבָּה לָזֶה.

Only afterward, once the process has unfolded and he attains the Torah after first stumbling, does he understand how the stumbling itself was necessary and served as the cause that enabled this attainment.
וְזֶהוּ הַנֶּחָמָה לַפּוּרְעָנֻיּוֹת, שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לְשׁוֹן נֶחָמָה, כְּמוֹ "וַיִּנָּחֶם" וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן חֲרָטָה;
This is the consolation for the calamities. The root of the word nechamah, as in 'and He reconsidered, etc.,' can denote regret or a changed perspective.
וְכָךְ הַמִּתְנַחֵם מִפּוּרְעָנֻיּוֹת הוּא שֶׁמִּתְחָרֵט עַל צַעֲרוֹ אָז.
So too, one who is consoled after affliction comes to reconsider the anguish he experienced at the time.
וְזֶה כְּשֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר לוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה כְּלָל פּוּרְעָנֻיּוֹת מֵעוֹלָם, וּבְחִנָּם נִצְטַעֵר.
This occurs when it is later revealed to him that, in its ultimate purpose, it had never truly been a calamity at all, and his anguish had arisen from not yet seeing its end.
כִּי הַבִּירוּר שֶׁהוּא הָיָה הֲכָנָה לַטּוֹב, הֲרֵי כָּל דָּבָר נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם תַּכְלִיתוֹ, נִמְצָא גַּם זֶה הָיָה טוֹב.
For once it becomes clear that the event was a preparation for good—and everything is defined by its ultimate purpose—it follows that this too was good.
וְזֶהוּ סְמִיכוּת שֶׁבַע דְּנֶחֶמְתָּא לְשַׁבַּת תְּשׁוּבָה, כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ הִתְהַפְּכוּת זֶה הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה,
This explains why the Seven Haftarot of Consolation are followed closely by Shabbat Teshuvah, for the root of this transformation is teshuvah.
שֶׁהִיא גַּם כֵּן חֲרָטָה עַל הָרַע שֶׁמִּצַּד הָאָדָם.
Teshuvah too is a reconsideration and regret concerning the evil that came from man's side.
וְזֶהוּ בְּרֵאשִׁית שָׁנָה, שֶׁהוּא תְּחִלַּת הַזְּמַן: הַהַתְחָלָה הוּא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, וְסוֹפוֹ הוּא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא — "וְאָשׁוּבָה אֲלֵיכֶם".

At the beginning of the year, which is the beginning of the cycle of time, the beginning comes through an awakening from below, while its culmination is an awakening from Above—'and I will return to you.'
זֶהוּ הַנֶּחָמָתוֹת: לְהִתְחָרֵט אַפּוּרְעָנֻיּוֹת דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁנִּצְטַעֲרוּ, שֶׁזֶּה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
This is the meaning of the consolations: to come to a changed understanding of the afflictions sent by the Blessed One over which they had grieved, recognizing that these too came from Him.
וְכֵן הַנֶּחָמָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "נַחֲמוּ" וְגוֹמֵר, "יֹאמַר" וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁהוּא הַמּוֹלִיד זֶה בַּלֵּב.
Likewise, the consolation comes from the Blessed One Himself—'Comfort, etc.,' 'shall say, etc.'—for He is the One Who brings this new realization into the heart.
וְהַדְּבָרִים עֲמוּקִים; לֹא אוּכַל לְהַאֲרִיךְ כָּעֵת יוֹתֵר.
These matters are profound, and I cannot elaborate further at present.

sections.en: The Shofar: Voice, Prayer, and Expansive Understanding

items.h: The shofar expands a narrow inner voice into broad revelation; its cries, numbers, and forms connect Torah, prayer, and the transformation of constriction into understanding.

Seif 1 — The Shofar as an Expanding Voice
The shofar broadens a narrow inner sound, joining Torah's plain voice with prayer's cry between them.

p: עִנְיַן הַשּׁוֹפָר בַּטֶּבַע הוּא מַרְחִיב הַקּוֹל וּמַגְבִּיהוֹ, שֶׁהַמַּשְׁמִיעַ לְתוֹכוֹ קוֹל נָמוּךְ בְּצִדּוֹ הַקָּצָר.
The nature of the shofar is to broaden and amplify a sound: one sounds a low voice into its narrow end.
עַל יְדֵי הַרְעָדַת חֶלְקֵי הָאֲוִיר בַּחֲלַל הַשּׁוֹפָר, הוּא נִשְׁמָע קוֹל גָּבוֹהַּ לַחוּץ דֶּרֶךְ צִדּוֹ הָרָחָב, כַּנּוֹדָע לַטִּבְעִיִּים.
By vibrating the particles of air in the hollow of the shofar, the sound emerges outward as a louder voice through its broad end, as is known to students of nature.
וְהוּא כְּלִי אֶמְצָעִי בֵּין הַמַּשְׁמִיעַ לַשּׁוֹמֵעַ, שֶׁיּוּכַל הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ לְקַבֵּל בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת רְחָבָה מַה שֶּׁהַמַּשְׁמִיעַ מַשְׁמִיעַ מִן הַמֵּצַר.
It is therefore an intermediary instrument between the one who sounds and the one who hears, enabling the listener to receive in broad expansion what the sounder produces from a constricted place.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כַּשּׁוֹפָר הָרֵם קוֹלֶךָ", שֶׁהַנָּבִיא אֶמְצָעִי בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם בְּהַשְׁמָעַת הַקּוֹל,
This is the meaning of the verse, “Raise your voice like a shofar”: the prophet stands as an intermediary in transmitting the voice between Israel and their Father in Heaven,
דֻּגְמַת הַשּׁוֹפָר, שֶׁהוּא מְקַבְּלוֹ בִּלְחִישָׁה מִלְמַעְלָה.
like the shofar, receiving the message above in a whisper and giving it expanded expression.
"וַהַשֵּׁם יִתֵּן אֹמֶר, הַמְבַשְּׂרוֹת צָבָא רָב" — שֶׁדִּבּוּר אֶחָד שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא מִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּפִי הַנָּבִיא לְפָרָשָׁה שְׁלֵמָה.
Thus, “The Lord gives the word; the women who proclaim it are a great host”: a single Divine utterance expands in the mouth of the prophet into an entire passage.
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹפָרוֹת דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִשְׁמִיעָנוּ אֶת קוֹלוֹ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, "וְהָיָה קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר הוֹלֵךְ וְחָזֵק מְאֹד" — הַיְנוּ כֹּחַ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתוֹ.
This is the shofar of the Giving of the Torah: the Blessed One caused us to hear His voice from heaven, and “the sound of the shofar grew continually stronger”—meaning the power of its expansion.
כִּי מִקְרָא אֶחָד יוֹצֵא לְכַמָּה טְעָמִים (סַנְהֶדְרִין לד.),
For a single verse can yield many meanings (Sanhedrin 34a),
וְלֵיכָּא מִידִי בִּנְבִיאִים וּבְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, וְכֵן בְּכָל חַכְמֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, דְּלָא רְמִיזִי בְּאוֹרַיְתָא (תַּעֲנִית ט.),
and there is nothing in the Prophets, in the teachings of our Sages of blessed memory, or in the words of the sages of the Oral Torah that is not alluded to in the Torah (Ta’anit 9a).
וְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לוֹ הַשָּׂגָה אַחֶרֶת בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.
Every Jew therefore has a distinct apprehension within the words of Torah.
שֶׁקּוֹלוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה הוּא בְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל, שֶׁקּוֹל נָמוּךְ שֶׁלּוֹ נִתְרַחֵב לַשּׁוֹמְעִים בְּהַרְחָבָה גְּדוֹלָה לְאֵין שִׁעוּר.
His voice within Torah is thus the voice of a great shofar: His concentrated voice expands for its hearers without limit.
וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, שֶׁאָנוּ בָּאִים בְּקוֹל תְּפִלָּה, קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא יָהֵיב עֵיטִין בְּכֹלָּא לְקַבֵּל בְּרַחֲמִים וּבְרָצוֹן אֶת תְּפִלָּתֵנוּ,
On Rosh Hashanah, when we approach with the voice of prayer, the Holy One, blessed be He, provides counsel in every matter so as to receive our prayer with mercy and favor,
הַבָּאָה בְּקוֹל נָמוּךְ מְאֹד בְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּקּוּנִים (תִּקּוּן ו): "צָוְחִין כְּכַלְבָּא: הַב לָן" וְכוּלֵי.
even though it comes in an exceedingly low voice, from the utmost lowliness, as the Tikkunim (Tikkun 6) describes people crying “like a dog: Give us…” and so forth.
וְאַף הַמַּאֲרִיךְ בִּתְפִלָּה וּמְעַיֵּן בָּהּ בְּכַוָּנָה שְׁלֵמָה — מִי יִצְדַּק לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּדִּין?
Even one who prays at length and concentrates with complete intention—who could be justified before Him in strict judgment?
וּלְעוֹלָם: "מִן הַמֵּצַר קָרָאתִי יָהּ", שֶׁהַקְּרִיאָה הִיא בַּמֵּצַר מְאֹד — הֵיכָן תּוֹרָה וְהֵיכָן מִצְווֹת דְּמַגְּנֵי עֲלָן?
Thus it is always, “From the narrow place I called to God”: our calling is from profound constriction—where is our Torah, and where are the mitzvot that can protect us?
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹנֶה בַמֶּרְחָב.
Only the Blessed One answers us with expansiveness.
וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה לָבוֹא בְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר שֶׁלָּנוּ שֶׁאָנוּ תּוֹקְעִין, לְהַרְחִיב הַשְׁמָעַת קוֹלֵנוּ לְמַעְלָה יוֹתֵר מִכְּפִי דִּבּוּרֵנוּ.
The counsel for this is to come with our shofar blast, so that the sounding of our voice Above is broadened beyond the measure of our actual words.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּל מִינֵי הַשָּׂגוֹת וְשִׂכְלִיּוֹת דִּבְנֵי אָדָם וְכָל הַנִּבְרָאִים בְּהַשָּׂגָתָם כְּלוּלִים בְּקוֹל תּוֹרָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Just as every kind of human understanding and intellect, and the apprehension of every created being, is included within the Divine voice of Torah,

כָּךְ הַכֹּל כָּלוּל בְּקוֹל תְּפִלָּה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי הַכֹּל אֶחָד, כַּנּוֹדָע מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים קיח.; בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא): "אֲנִי יָחִיד בָּעֶלְיוֹנִים וְהוּא יָחִיד בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים".

so too everything is included within the voice of Israel’s prayer, for all is one, as in the teaching (Pesachim 118a; Bereishit Rabbah 21), “I am unique in the upper worlds, and he is unique in the lower worlds.”
כִּי סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה.
For the final act was first in thought.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא כּוֹלֵל הַכֹּל, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ חִיּוּתָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם",
Just as the primordial Divine thought includes all things and is the source of their life—“You give life to them all”—
כָּךְ הָאָדָם נִקְרָא עוֹלָם קָטָן שֶׁכּוֹלֵל הַכֹּל, וְכָל הַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים כְּלוּלִים בּוֹ, וְהוּא כָּלוּל בָּהֶם,
so man is called a microcosm that includes everything: all the powers of created beings are included within him, and he is included within them.
וּמַשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם מִצַּד סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה, הַיְנוּ מִצַּד הַהַשְׁקָפָה אֶל הַתַּכְלִית.
He in turn influences them from the standpoint of the final act—that is, from the perspective of creation’s ultimate purpose. –
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר: כְּמוֹ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כּוֹלֵל כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד הַהַתְחָלָה שֶׁהוּא שָׁרְשָׁם, כָּךְ מָשִׁיחַ כּוֹלְלָם מִצַּד הַתַּכְלִית.

[[As explained elsewhere: just as our father Jacob, peace be upon him, includes all the souls of Israel from the standpoint of their beginning and root, so Mashiach includes them from the standpoint of their ultimate purpose.]
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֹׁרֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ מֵהָאָבוֹת, כָּךְ יֵשׁ בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ מִנֶּפֶשׁ מָשִׁיחַ גַּם כֵּן].
[And just as every Jew contains a root of soul from the Patriarchs, so too he contains a root from the soul of Mashiach.]
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה אָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא עה:): עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִקְרוֹא לַצַּדִּיקִים בִּשְׁמוֹ,
From this standpoint they taught (Bava Batra 75b) that in the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will call the righteous by His Name,
הַיְנוּ שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה, שֶׁהוּא הָרוֹמֵז שֶׁמְּהַוֶּה אֶת הַכֹּל וְכוֹלֵל הַכֹּל.
namely the Name Havayah, which signifies that He brings everything into being and encompasses everything.
וְכָךְ הַצַּדִּיקִים, אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ח) עַל פָּסוּק "הֵמָּה הַיּוֹצְרִים", שֶׁהָיוּ שֻׁתָּפִים כִּבְיָכוֹל בִּבְרִיאַת עוֹלָם.
So too regarding the righteous, our Sages of blessed memory said (Bereishit Rabbah 8), on the verse “These were the potters,” that they were, as it were, partners in the creation of the world.
הַכַּוָּנָה מִצַּד הַתַּכְלִית, שֶׁאֲלֵיהֶם הָיְתָה מְכֻוֶּנֶת כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה לְצַוּוֹת לָזֶה, וְנִמְצָא כֹּחָם הוּא הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ כְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה.
The meaning is from the standpoint of purpose: all creation was directed toward serving such a person, and therefore their power becomes a source of influence for creation as a whole.
וְהַדִּבּוּר הוּא חִיּוּת הָאָדָם, כַּנּוֹדָע: "לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה" — לְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא.
Speech is the life-force of man, as is known from the rendering of “a living soul” as “a speaking spirit.”
וְדִבּוּר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית הוּא הַמְחַיֶּה כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה, כַּנּוֹדָע, כִּי חִיּוּת הַכֹּל נִמְשָׁךְ מֵחִיּוּת חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים, וְחִיּוּתוֹ הוּא דִּבּוּרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
The Divine speech of Creation gives life to the entire universe, for the life of all things is drawn from the Life of the worlds, and His life, as it were, is His Divine speech.

וְזֶהוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַדִּבּוּר דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי קוֹל שׁוֹפָר דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, דְּבְאוֹרַיְתָא בָּרָא הָעוֹלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה וּבַזֹּהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים.

This is the expansion of Divine speech through the shofar-sound of the Giving of the Torah, for the world was created through Torah, as stated at the beginning of Bereishit Rabbah and many times in the Zohar.
וּבִשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה נִתְבַּסֵּס הָעוֹלָם, הַיְנוּ יָשַׁב עַל כַּנּוֹ.
At the Giving of the Torah the world became established—set firmly upon its foundation.
שֶׁהַדִּבּוּר הוּא רוּחָנִי וְהוּא דָּבָר הָרוֹפֵף, וּכְשֶׁבָּא לְפֹעַל בִּכְתָב הוּא דָּבָר הַקַּיָּם שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹפֵף.
Speech is spiritual and fluid; when it becomes actualized in writing it takes on a fixed and enduring form.
וּבִשְׁעַת בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם הָיָה רַק דִּבּוּר וּמַאֲמָר, וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ (גִּיטִּין ס:): "דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בִּכְתָב".
At creation there was only speech and utterance, corresponding to the rule (Gittin 60b), “Matters of the Oral Torah you are not permitted to recite in written form.”
