וְגַם אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כֵּן,
And likewise with the Blessed Name it is so,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה: "לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם",
and as it is written in the Torah: "I have given you good merchandise,"
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מַתָּנָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא "לֶקַח",
for even though it is a gift, it is nevertheless called "merchandise taken,"
כְּאִלּוּ הֵם לְקָחוּהָ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם.
as though they acquired it through their own striving.
וְאַף יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, אַף דִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ קְבוּעָה וְקַיָּימָא,
And even the Sabbath day, although its holiness is fixed and established from on High,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם צִוָּה בְּדֶרֶךְ מִצְוָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
He nevertheless commanded it by way of a commandment to Israel,
וְשֶׁהֵם מְצֻוִּים לְקַדְּשׁוֹ בְּקִדּוּשׁ הַיּוֹם כְּאִלּוּ הֵם מְקַדְּשֵׁי לֵיהּ.
and that they are commanded to sanctify it through the Kiddush of the day, as though they themselves sanctify it.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם זָכוּ לִקְדֻשָּׁה זוֹ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָבוֹת: אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק, וְיַעֲקֹב,
For in truth, they merited this holiness through the striving of the Patriarchs: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה,
from level to level,
עַד מַדְרֵגַת יַעֲקֹב, הַבָּחוּר שֶׁבָּאָבוֹת,
up to the level of Jacob, the chosen of the Patriarchs,
שֶׁזָּכָה לַהַכָּרָה הַשְּׁלֵמָה דַּה' אֶחָד.
who merited the complete realization that the Lord is One.
וְהַכָּרָה זוֹ נִשְׁרְשָׁה בְּכָל בָּנָיו אַחֲרָיו בְּשָׁרְשָׁם,
And this realization was rooted in all his children after him in their very spiritual essence;
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא רַק בְּרָכָה בִּמְאוֹר פָּנִים,
and therefore it is called specifically a blessing in the light of the countenance,
דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמְּאוֹר פָּנִים יֶשְׁנוֹ גַּם בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
for the root of the radiant countenance exists even during the six workdays,
אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת הוּא מִתְבָּרֵךְ.
only that on the Sabbath it becomes blessed and amplified.

items.h:
Seif 6 — Blessing as Expansion of Divine Light
Shabbat expands Israel's awareness that every blessing flows from Hashem, the sole source of all bounty.

p: וְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם הֶאָרַת פָּנִים,
And the nations of the world, who possess no illumination of the countenance,
כִּי שָׁרְשָׁם מִצַּד הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
because their root is from the side of darkness,
שֶׁהוּא הַשִּׁקּוּעַ בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַדּוֹמֶה לְחֹשֶׁךְ וְלַיְלָה,
which is immersion in the affairs of this world that resembles darkness and night,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ פְּסָחִים (ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳),
as they said at the beginning of Pesachim (2a),
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹר פָּנִים גַּם בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
it is impossible for them to attain the light of the countenance even on the Sabbath day,
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּכוּת לָזֶה כְּלָל;
for they have no connection to this whatsoever;
רַק בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם דְּבוּקִים בְּעֶצֶם הָאוֹרָה,
it is found only among the children of Israel, who are cleaved to the essence of the light,
וּשְׁחַרְחוּרִיתָם הוּא רַק שֶׁ"שְּׁזָפַתְנִי הַשָּׁמֶשׁ" —
and their darkness is only that "the sun has tanned me" —
כָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁתַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ,
referring to all affairs of this world that are beneath the sun,
וּבִמְעַט לִבּוּן מִתְלַבְּנִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה,
and with a little cleansing they become white and pure again, as they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah,
וּלְעוֹלָם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ אוֹר גַּם בִּזְמַן הַחֹשֶׁךְ.
and forever there remains within them a root of light even in the time of darkness.
בְּשַׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
On Shabbat, which is a foretaste of the World to Come,
אוֹתוֹ אוֹר הַנֶּעְלָם מִתְבָּרֵךְ וּמִתּוֹסֵף
that concealed light is blessed and increased,
עַד שֶׁבָּא לִכְלַל גִּלּוּי,
until it reaches full manifestation,
לִהְיוֹת בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ דָּבָר זֶה,
so that this matter becomes openly revealed within his heart:
כִּי הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
that everything is from the Blessed Name,
וְהוּא הַנּוֹתֵן כֹּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת חָיִל,
and He is the One Who gives the power to attain wealth and accomplishment,
וּמִמֵּילָא פָּנָיו מְאִירִים מִשִּׂמְחַת לְבָבוֹ.
and automatically his face radiates from the joy of his heart.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא מִתְבָּרְכִים גַּם כָּל פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו דְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
And through this, all his activities of the six workdays are likewise automatically blessed,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁהֵם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹר הַבְּרָכוֹת.
since he recognizes that they stem from the Blessed Name, Who is the Source of all blessings.
וְזֶהוּ הַבְּרָכָה דְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
And this is the blessing of the Sabbath day:
הַיְינוּ שֶׁבּוֹ יִהְיֶה הִתְגַּלּוּת הַכָּרָה זוֹ דְּ"אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ" בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת,
namely, that on it there should be the revelation of this recognition that "there is none else besides Him" in expansive diffusion,
כִּי עִנְיַן בְּרָכָה הוּא הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַשֶּׁפַע.
for the concept of blessing is the expansion and flow of divine bounty.

items.h:
Seif 7 — Holiness as Separation and Restraint
Alongside expansive blessing, holiness preserves Israel's distinctness and prevents divine closeness from being misused.

p: וְהַקְּדֻשָּׁה הוּא הֵיפֶךְ מִזֶּה,
And holiness is the opposite of this,
דְּעִיקַּר הוֹרָאָתוֹ עַל הַהַבְדָּלָה וְהַהַפְרָשָׁה,
for its primary meaning denotes separation and withdrawal,
לִהְיוֹת הַדָּבָר מוּגְדָּר וּמוּבְדָּל מִדָּבָר אַחֵר.
so that the matter remains bounded and set apart from anything else.
וְגַם זֶה דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב שֶׁנִּקְרָא "קָדוֹשׁ",
And this too is the spiritual level of Jacob, who is called "holy,"
כִּי הוּא הַמּוּבְדָּל מִכָּל הָעַמִּים,
for he is the one set apart from all the nations,
דְּמִמֶּנּוּ הַתְחָלַת קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה.
since from him began the holiness of Israel throughout all his seed after him, whose bed was whole and pure.
לְפִי שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַכָּרָה זוֹ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַפּוֹעֵל הַכֹּל וּדְשָׁוְא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם,
Because through this realization that the Blessed Name works all things and that human effort is futile,
יוּכַל לָבוֹא לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת לְכָל הֲבָלִים שֶׁיִּרְצֶה,
one might come to unrestricted expansion into whatever vanities he desires,
וְיַחְשׁוֹב כִּי הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְהוּא עִמּוֹ.
and imagine that everything is from the Blessed Name and that He is with him.
וְהַגַּם דְּהָאֱמֶת כֵּן,
And even though the truth is indeed so,
דְּ"גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא" וְגוֹמֵר "אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
that "even when I walk in the valley..." and so forth, "You are with me," —
הַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁאֵירְעוּ מַה שֶׁאֵירְעוּ,
this applies only after what has happened has already happened,
אַל יִתְיָאֵשׁ מִן הָרַחֲמִים וְאַל יַפְרִיד עַצְמוֹ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
let him not despair of mercy and not separate himself from the Blessed Name;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק "אַל תִּרְשַׁע הַרְבֵּה":
and as they said in Shabbat (31b) concerning the verse "Do not be excessively wicked":
מִי שֶׁאָכַל וְכוּלֵי,
one who ate garlic, and so forth,
שֶׁלֹּא יַחְשׁוֹב שֶׁכְּבָר נִפְרַד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְלִהְיוֹת כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם,
that he should not think that he has already become separated from the Blessed Name, Heaven forbid, and act like all the nations,
רַק בֶּאֱמֶת לְעוֹלָם "אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
for in truth, forever "You are with me."
אֲבָל חָלִילָה לֵילֵךְ מִפְּנֵי כֵן בְּגֵיא וְכוּלֵי, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם;
However, God forbid that one should purposefully walk for this reason in the valley of darkness, Heaven forbid;
דְּאַדְּרַבָּה, כֵּיוָן שֶׁ"אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
for on the contrary, since "You are with me,"
הֲרֵי זֶה כְּמַכְנִיס, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים עִמּוֹ לִמְקוֹם הַטִּנּוֹפֶת.
it is considered as if one brings, Heaven forbid, the King of kings of kings together with himself into a place of filth.

items.h:
Seif 8 — Kiddush: Joining Blessing with Holiness
Kiddush transforms wine from a source of frivolity into a vessel for joy bounded by sanctity.

p: וְעַל כֵּן עִם הַבְּרָכָה צָרִיךְ קְדֻשָּׁה גַּם כֵּן,
Therefore, together with the blessing, holiness is also required,
לִהְיוֹת מוּגְדָּר וּמוּבְדָּל בִּמְאוֹר פָּנִים,
to remain bounded and set apart in the light of the countenance,
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל הוֹלֵלוּת;
so that it does not become a joy of frivolous revelry;
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא נִיתְּנָה לַגּוֹיִם,
which is why the Sabbath was not given to the nations,
שֶׁהֵם יָבוֹאוּ מִזֶּה לְקַלּוּת רֹאשׁ,
for they would arrive from this at levity,
לִהְיוֹת אוֹכְלִים וְשׁוֹתִים וּפוֹחֲזִים,
becoming people who merely eat, drink, and behave licentiously,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם (פָּרָשָׁה ל״ט אוֹת ח׳) עַל גּוֹיִם שֶׁבְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ
as they said in Bereishit Rabbah there (parashah 39, ot 8) concerning the gentiles outside the Land,
וְקֹדֶם שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and prior to the arrival of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, in the Land of Israel.
וּקְדֻשָּׁה בְּכָל מָקוֹם הוּא גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה
And holiness everywhere denotes a fence against sexual immorality
וְהַגְדָּרָה מִתַּאֲוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and restraint from the physical appetites of this world,
וְזֶהוּ הַקְּדֻשָּׁה שֶׁאַחַר הַבְּרָכָה,
and this is the holiness that follows the blessing:
לְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ בִּמְאוֹר פָּנִים זֶה.
to sanctify oneself within this radiant countenance.
כִּי אֵצֶל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּרָכָה זוֹ הָיָה מוֹלִיד פַּחֲזוּת וּפְרִיקוּת עוֹל
For among the nations of the world, such a blessing would spawn wantonness, casting off of the yoke,
וְהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּתַאֲוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
and deeper sinking into the desires of this world;
וְאֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אַדְּרַבָּה, מוֹלִידָה קְדֻשָּׁה בַּלֵּב.
whereas among the children of Israel, on the contrary, it generates holiness in the heart.
וְאוֹר הַפָּנִים הַמֵּעִיד עַל הָעֹז שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And the light of the countenance that testifies to the inner fortitude in the heart
אֵינוֹ מִכֹּחַ שַׁלְוָה שֶׁל הוֹלֵלוּת,
does not derive from the power of a frivolous tranquility,
רַק מִכֹּחַ שַׁלְוָה הַמְּלֵאָה קְדֻשָּׁה
but only from the power of a tranquility filled with holiness
וְהַגְדָּרָה מִכָּל מִינֵי שַׁלְוָה שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and restraint from all kinds of merely worldly tranquility.
וּבִרְכַּת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת מְקַבְּלִים בִּתְפִלָּה,
And the blessing of the Sabbath day is received through prayer,
שֶׁהוּא בִּרְכוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
which constitutes the blessings of the Blessed Name,
וּמִבִּרְכוֹתָיו יְבֹרַךְ בֵּית עֲבָדָיו.
and from His blessings the house of His servants shall be blessed.
וְהַקְּדֻשָּׁה — בְּקִדּוּשׁ עַל הַיַּיִן,
And holiness is received through the Kiddush over wine,
שֶׁהוּא "יְשַׂמַּח לֵב"
which ordinarily "gladdens the heart"
וּמוֹלִיד שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל הוֹלֵלוּת לַשּׁוֹגִים בָּהּ;
and produces a joy of frivolous revelry for those who err through it;
אֲבָל יַיִן דְּמִצְוָה, אַדְּרַבָּה, מוֹלִיד קְדֻשָּׁה בַּלֵּב
however, wine used for a mitzvah, on the contrary, generates holiness in the heart
וְהַגְדָּרָה מִשִּׂמְחַת הוֹלֵלוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and restraint from the frivolous joy of this world.

sections.en: Chanukah, Written Torah, and the Living Oral Torah

items.h: Chanukah reveals the vitality of Oral Torah beyond fixed writing, tracing how divine speech, rabbinic wisdom, hidden providence, and Israel's living interpretation illuminate the darkness of exile.

Seif 1 — Why Chanukah Was Not Written into Scripture
Chanukah's unwritten miracle distinguishes fixed written revelation from a later light rooted in the Oral Torah.

p: עִנְיַן הַנֵּס דַּחֲנֻכָּה,
The matter of the miracle of Chanukah,
שֶׁהוּא לְבַדּוֹ מֵהַנִּסִּים שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב,
in that it alone among the miracles was not permitted to be committed to canonical writing,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְבַּע זִכְרוֹנוֹ לְדוֹרוֹת.
and nevertheless its remembrance was established for all generations.
וּבְיוֹמָא כ״ט עַמּוּד א׳:
And in Yoma 29a:
מָה שַׁחַר סוֹף כָּל הַלַּיְלָה,
just as the dawn is the end of the entire night,
אַף אֶסְתֵּר סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים.
so too Esther is the end of all miracles.
וְהָאִיכָּא חֲנֻכָּה?
And does there not remain Chanukah?
"נִתְּנָה לִכְתֹּב" קָאָמְרִינַן.
We are speaking of miracles that were permitted to be written.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה, מַה בְּכָךְ דְּלָא נִכְתַּב,
And at first glance, what does it matter that it was not written?
סוֹף סוֹף הָיָה נֵס,
Ultimately there was a miracle,
וַעֲדַיִן אֵין אֶסְתֵּר הַסּוֹף כַּשַּׁחַר.
and yet Esther would not truly be the end like the morning dawn.
וְגַם מַה דְּהִמְשִׁיל כָּל הַנִּסִּים לְלַיְלָה וְאֶסְתֵּר לְשַׁחַר,
And furthermore, regarding the metaphor comparing all miracles to night and Esther to dawn:
אִם הַנֵּס הוּא אוֹר,
if a miracle is considered light,
הֲרֵי כָּל הַנִּסִּים גַּם כֵּן הָיוּ מְאִירִים עוֹד יוֹתֵר,
surely all the other miracles were even more illuminating,
דִּבְפֶסַח יָצְאוּ מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵרוּת,
for on Passover they went out from slavery to total freedom,
וּבְפוּרִים "אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן",
whereas on Purim "we are still servants of Ahasuerus,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִלָּה (י״ד עַמּוּד א׳).
as they said in Megillah (14a).

items.h:
Seif 2 — Night, Day, Writing, and Living Speech
This world conceals Havayah; writing preserves revelation in a garment, while spoken words carry immediate living vitality.

p: אֲבָל הָעִנְיָן,
However, the inner matter is,
כִּי אָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ פְּסָחִים (ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳) דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִמְשַׁל לְלַיְלָה וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא לְיוֹם,
for they said at the beginning of Pesachim (2a) that this world is compared to night and the World to Come to day;
הַיְינוּ דִּבְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה "זֶה שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם" כְּתִיב (שָׁם נ׳ עַמּוּד א׳),
meaning that in this world "this is My Name forever (le'olam / le'allem - to conceal)" is written (ibid. 50a),
דְּהַכָּרַת הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ דְּשֵׁם הַהֲוָיָ"ה,
in that the perception of the absolute truth of the Ineffable Name Havayah,
שֶׁהִיא מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
which is the attribute of truth belonging to our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
נֶעְלָם מְאֹד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא,
is exceedingly concealed in this world, which is the realm of falsehood,
דְּכָל עִנְיָנָיו "עַד אַרְגִּיעָה" כְּמִדַּת לְשׁוֹן שָׁקֶר.
wherein all its transient matters endure only "for a brief moment," like the nature of a lying tongue.
וְהֵם הַמַּאֲפִילִים וּמַעֲלִימִים הַכָּרַת הָאֱמֶת,
And these temporal illusions darken and obscure the perception of truth,
דְּ"אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ" מַמָּשׁ שׁוּם מְצִיאוּת כְּלָל.
that "there is none else besides Him" — literally no other reality at all.
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵין נִיכָּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רַק דֶּרֶךְ אֱמוּנָה,
And this truth is not visibly discernible in this world except by way of faith,
כְּטַעַם "וֶאֱמוּנָתְךָ בַּלֵּילוֹת",
in the sense of "and Your faithfulness in the nights,"
וְ"לֹא כְּשֶׁאֲנִי נִכְתָּב אֲנִי נִקְרָא" —
and "not as I am written am I pronounced" —
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר מוּשָּׂג בְּפִי הַנִּבְרָאִים רַק דֶּרֶךְ שֵׁם הָאַדְנוּת,
meaning it is apprehended in the mouths of created beings only through the Name of Lordship (Adonut),
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר הַכָּרַת אַדְנוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
meaning the acknowledgment of His blessed mastership,
וְשֶׁהוּא מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה.
and that He is King of the universe Whose sovereignty rules over all.
וְאַף דִּ"בְּאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים",
And even though "in the light of the King's countenance is life,"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא דֶּרֶךְ כַּמָּה צִמְצוּמִים וּמַסָכִים וְאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָאוֹת שֶׁאֵין מְאִירוֹת
nevertheless it comes through multiple contractions, veils, and non-luminous lenses
לִרְאוֹת הָאֲמִתּוּת מַמָּשׁ,
to behold the literal essence of the reality,
וְרַק נִכְתָּב בִּכְתִיבָה,
and it is merely inscribed through writing,
שֶׁהִיא גַּם כֵּן לְבוּשׁ הַמַּגְשִׁים אוֹתִיּוֹת הַדִּבּוּר
which is likewise a garment that materializes the spiritual letters of speech
וּמַלְבִּישָׁם בְּצוּרַת אוֹתִיּוֹת גַּשְׁמִיּוֹת שֶׁל דְּיוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי קְלָף וּנְיָר,
and clothes them in the tangible form of physical letters of ink upon parchment and paper,
וְאֵין בָּהֶם עוֹד חַיּוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּדִּבּוּר,
and they no longer contain that living vitality that exists in spoken speech,
שֶׁהוּא רוּחָנִי וְיוֹצֵא מִפֶּה חַי מְדַבֵּר,
which is spiritual and issues forth directly from a living, speaking mouth,
וּבְלֹא חַיּוּת אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְדַבֵּר,
and without life-force it is impossible to speak,
וְאֵין מוּרְגָּשׁ לַשּׁוֹמֵעַ אֶלָּא בְּעֵת הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁיּוֹצֵא עִם הַחַיּוּת שֶׁבּוֹ.
and it is palpable to the listener only during the actual moment of speech that issues forth with the vitality inside it.

items.h:
Seif 3 — Seeing Hashem and the Departure of Life
Direct divine perception overwhelms bodily life because finite vitality dissolves before its infinite source.

p: וְנֶאֱמַר: "כִּי לֹא יִרְאַנִי הָאָדָם וָחָי",
And Scripture says: "For man shall not see Me and live,"
דִּבְהַרְגָּשַׁת אֲמִתּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for upon the direct perception of His blessed true essence,
מִעוּט חַיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַ מִמַּעַל
the small measure of soul-vitality, which is a part of God from Above,
מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת וּמִתְכַּלֶּלֶת בִּמְקוֹרָהּ,
departs the body and becomes dissolved and integrated into its Source,
כְּמוֹ אוֹר נֵר בַּאֲבוּקָה הַסָּמוּךְ לוֹ, כַּיָּדוּעַ.
like the small flame of a candle nullified within the blaze of a nearby torch, as is known.
וְכֵן בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד שֶׁזָּכָה לִרְאִיָּה בְּאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And so it was at the Giving of the Torah: with a single divine Utterance in which Israel merited vision through the luminous lens like Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
כִּי הָיוּ "רוֹאִים אֶת הַקּוֹלוֹת",
for they were "seeing the voices,"
דְּהָיָה אֶצְלָם הָרְאִיָּה וְהַשְּׁמִיעָה הַכֹּל אֶחָד כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵם מְיוּחָדִים בִּמְקוֹרָם,
in that sight and hearing were united as one for them, just as they are unified in their supernal Source,
וּמַה שֶּׁהָיָה נִשְׁמָע הָיָה נִרְאֶה גַּם כֵּן.
and what was heard was simultaneously seen as well.
וְכֵן הַשָּׂגָה דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא נִרְאֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רַק בִּכְתָב,
And likewise, the apprehension of the Name Havayah, which in this world is only visible in written letters,
הָיָה אָז נִשְׁמָע וּמוּשָּׂג הָאֲמִתּוּת לְגַמְרֵי,
was at that moment audibly perceived and its true essence fully grasped,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָצְאָה נִשְׁמָתָם (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳).
and through this their souls departed (Shabbat 88b).
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת "בְּאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים" עַל יְדֵי שֶׁדְּבֵקִים בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים,
Even though in absolute truth "in the light of the King's countenance is life" through cleaving to the living God,
אֲבָל אֵין זֶה חַיּוּת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בִּלְבוּשׁ גּוּפָנִי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
this is not the corporeal life of this world clad in a physical body of this world,
רַק כְּטַעַם (תַּעֲנִית ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, לֹא מֵת,
but rather in the manner of (Taanit 5b): "Our father Jacob, peace be upon him, did not die,"
אַף דִּקְבָרוּ קַבְרַיָּא;
even though the embalmers buried him;"
רַק כָּל חַיּוּתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּפִי מִדָּתוֹ בְּהַכָּרַת אֲמִתּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
rather, his entire vitality in this world, according to his measure in apprehending His blessed true essence,
לֹא הָיְתָה חַיּוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל.
was not a worldly life-force at all.

items.h:
Seif 4 — A Foretaste of Life beyond the Evil Inclination
Sinai and death by the divine kiss reveal a higher vitality freed from sorrow, sin, and bodily limitation.

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק ה׳),
And this is what they taught in Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 5):
דְּזָכָה לְחַיִּים שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע,
that he merited a life devoid of sorrow and devoid of the evil inclination,
וְזֶהוּ מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
and this is a foretaste of the World to Come.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁזָּכוּ לָזֶה גַּם כֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
And just as Israel likewise merited this at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
אַחַר שֶׁהוֹרִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא טַל שֶׁל תְּחִיָּה לְהַחֲיוֹתָם,
after the Holy One, blessed be He, brought down the dew of resurrection to revive them,
וְזָכוּ לְאוֹתוֹ חַיּוּת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אַחַר תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים,
and they merited that sublime vitality that will prevail after the resurrection of the dead,
שֶׁהוּא חֵרוּת מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע וּמִשִּׁעְבּוּד גָּלֻיּוֹת;
which is freedom from the evil inclination and from subjugation to the exiles;
עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳:
to the extent that they said in Avodah Zarah 5a:
אִלְמָלֵא אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁחָטְאוּ — אָנוּ כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא בָּאנוּ לָעוֹלָם,
were it not that our ancestors sinned, we would be as those who never needed to be born into this world,
דְּגַם כֵּן לֹא הָיוּ מֵתִים כְּלָל.
for they would never have died at all.
כִּי חַיּוּת הָאֱמֶת הוּא חַיִּים נִצְחִיִּים,
For true vitality is eternal life,
וְלֹא "עַד אַרְגִּיעָה" כְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and not a momentary existence "for a brief flash" like the life of this world.
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת,
And our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who is the root of the attribute of truth,
וַדַּאי זָכָה לְכָךְ;
certainly merited this;
וְאַף שֶׁהָיָה מְלֻבָּשׁ עוֹד בַּלְּבוּשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and even while he was still clothed in the physical garment of this world,
לֹא הָיָה מַרְגִּישׁ עִנְיַן הַגּוּף
he did not experience bodily existence
אֶלָּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָדָם מַרְגִּישׁ הַמַּלְבּוּשׁ שֶׁהוּא לָבוּשׁ.
except as an ordinary person senses the outer apparel he is wearing.
וְלֹא כְּחַיּוּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And this was not like ordinary worldly life,
שֶׁהַגּוּף הוּא מְקֻשָּׁר מַמָּשׁ עִם הַנֶּפֶשׁ בְּעֶצֶם הַחַיּוּת,
wherein the physical body is bound intimately with the soul in the very essence of living,
וּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הַקִּישּׁוּר, כָּךְ הוּא גּוֹדֶל צַעַר הַמִּיתָה בִּפְרִידָתָם;
and in proportion to the intensity of that attachment, so is the magnitude of the pain of death at their separation;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (ח׳ עַמּוּד א׳) דִּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מִיתוֹת,
as they said in the first chapter of Berakhot (8a) that there are nine hundred and three forms of death,
וְקָשָׁה שֶׁבְּכֻלָּם — אַסְכָּרָה,
and the most agonizing of them all is croup (askara),
שֶׁהוּא בַּעֲוֹן לְשׁוֹן הָרָע,
which comes on account of the sin of evil speech,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (ל״ג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳);
as they said in Shabbat (33b);
שֶׁעִיקַּר חַיּוּת הַגּוּפָנִי הוּא בַּדִּבּוּר,
for the essence of physical vitality resides in the power of speech,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁתִּרְגֵּם אוּנְקְלוֹס עַל "לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה" — "לְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא";
and as Onkelos translated on the verse "into a living soul" — "into a speaking spirit";
וְכַאֲשֶׁר מְקַלְקֵל הַדִּבּוּר וְנִמְשָׁךְ בּוֹ לָרַע שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַגּוּף,
and when one degrades speech and is drawn through it toward evil, which stems from the side of the body,
הֲרֵי הַחַיּוּת מְקֻשָּׁר בְּיוֹתֵר בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּתוֹ,
the soul's life-force becomes ever more bound up with his coarse physical nature,
עַל כֵּן פְּרִידָתָם קָשָׁה בְּיוֹתֵר.
and therefore their tearing apart in death is exceedingly difficult.
וְנִיחָא שֶׁבְּכֻלָּם — נְשִׁיקָה,
And the easiest and gentlest of them all is death by the Divine Kiss,
שֶׁהוּא הַמִּיתָה שֶׁ"עַל פִּי ה'",
which is the death that occurs literally "by the mouth of the Lord,"
דִּבְמִיתָתָם רוֹאִים (סִפְרֵי בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ פִּסְקָא ק״ג)
for at the moment of their passing they gaze upon the Divine (Sifrei Behaalotecha 103)
וּמִתְכַּלְּלִים בִּמְקוֹרָם;
and are gently integrated into their Source;
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי טָהֳרַת הַפֶּה וְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא,
and this is achieved through the purity of the mouth and the speaking spirit,
שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִידָּבֵק וּלְהִנָּשֵׁק בְּפִי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
whereby one merits to cleave and be kissed by the word of the Blessed Name.

items.h:
Seif 5 — Moshe's Death and Jacob's Deathlessness
Moshe still experienced death through a residual bodily flaw, while Jacob's cleaving left no true category of death.

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אַף מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֵת אַף שֶׁהָיָה עַל פִּי הַשֵּׁם.
And nevertheless, even Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, died, even though it was by the word of Hashem.
וּבְחֶטְאוֹ מֵת חֵטְא הַדִּבּוּר דְּשִׁמְעוּ נָא הַמֹּרִים
And he died on account of his sin: the sin of speech in "Hear now, you rebels,"
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא הֶרְגֵּשׁ מִיתָה לַגּוּף
for through this an awareness of death came to the body,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ צַד גּוּפָנִי עֲדַיִן הַמַּמְשִׁיךְ חַיּוּת נַפְשִׁי אֵלָיו וּמִצִּדּוֹ הוּא הֶרְגֵּשׁ מִיתָה.
since there was still a bodily aspect that drew soul-vitality to itself, and from its perspective comes the sensation of death.
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ שׁוּם הֶרְגֵּשׁ מִיתָה אַף כְּמִשְׁחַל בִּנְיָתָא מֵחֲלָבָא גַּם כֵּן
Jacob our father, peace be upon him, by contrast, felt no sensation of death whatsoever, not even like drawing a hair from milk,
כִּי לֹא הָיָה אֶצְלוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְחַיּוּתוֹ הָאֲמִתִּי עִם הַגּוּף כְּלַל.
because his true vitality had no connection to the physical body at all.
וּפְטִירָתוֹ הָיָה רַק כְּפוֹשֵׁט מַלְבּוּשׁ זֶה וְלוֹבֵשׁ מַלְבּוּשׁ אַחֵר שֶׁל עוֹלָם הָעֶלְיוֹן
His passing was only like stripping off this garment and putting on another garment of the Upper World,
וּמַלְבּוּשׁ זֶה נִקְבַּר אֲבָל אֵין בָּזֶה עִנְיָן וְגֶדֶר מִיתָה כְּלַל.
and this garment was buried, but there was in this no aspect or category of death at all.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא חָשׁ לַהֲשִׁיבוֹ כְּלַל שָׁם בְּתַעֲנִית ה' עַמּוּד ב' עַל שְׁאֵלַת בִּכְדִי קְבָרוּ
Therefore the Gemara was unconcerned to answer the question in Taanit 5b, "Was it for nothing that the embalmers buried him?"
רַק כֵּיוָן דְּמִקְרָא אֲנִי דּוֹרֵשׁ מַה אִכְפַּת לִי מַה שֶּׁמִּצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָיָה קְבוּרָה לַגּוּף
rather, since I expound Scripture, what do I care that from the perspective of this world there was burial for the body?
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּפִי הָאֱמֶת לֹא מֵת כְּלַל.
In absolute truth he did not die at all.

items.h:
Seif 6 — Writing as the Garment of Hidden Life
What appears as death can conceal higher life, just as writing clothes living divine truth in physical form.

p: וּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא יִתְבָּרֵר גַּם בְּכָל זַרְעוֹ כֵּן דְּלֹא מֵתוּ בֶּאֱמֶת רַק כְּפִי דִּמְיוֹן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
In the future to come this will be clarified concerning all his seed as well: that they did not truly die, but only according to the illusion of this world.
וְדָבָר זֶה רָמוּז בְּתִקּוּנֵי זוֹהַר סוֹף תִּקּוּן ס"ו (דְּפוּס מַנְטוֹבָה וְהוּא סוֹף תִּקּוּן מ') בְּסוֹד אַבְנֵי שַׁיִשׁ טָהוֹר
This matter is alluded to in Tikkunei Zohar at the end of Tikkun 66 (Mantua edition, which is the end of Tikkun 40) in the secret of the "stones of pure marble";
יְעֻיַּן שָׁם כְּפִי מַה שֶׁקִּבַּלְתִּי בְּבֵיאוּרוֹ וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
see there according to what I received in its explanation, though this is not the place for it.
וְאֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב הָיָה זֶה מְבֹרָר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן מִצִּידּוֹ שֶׁהָיָה דָּבוּק בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ מִדַּת יוֹם.
With Jacob this was already clear in this world from his side as well, for he was cleaved to the absolute truth, the attribute of Day.
וְזֶהוּ מַקִּישׁ הוּא לְזַרְעוֹ מִקְּרָא דְּזַרְעֲךָ בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁבְיָם מַה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד בְּזַרְעוֹ כְּשֶׁיִּזְכּוּ גַּם כֵּן לְאוֹתָם חַיִּים.
This is why Scripture compares him to his seed from the verse "your seed in the land of their captivity": what will be in the future with his seed when they too merit that same life.
אֲבָל מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַרְגִּישׁ בְּחַיּוּת כָּזֶה דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה אַדְּרַבָּה יוֹצֵא הַחַיּוּת.
From the side of this world, however, it is impossible to experience such vitality, for through such awareness, on the contrary, life departs.
וְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַשָּׂגָה דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא רַק בִּכְתָב שֶׁהַכְּתָב הוּא גַּם כֵּן מַלְבּוּשֵׁי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חַיּוּת.
And the experiential perception of the Name Havayah in this world exists only in writing, for writing is likewise among the garments of this world that contain no vitality.

items.h:
Seif 7 — Written Torah as Divine Speech in a Physical Garment
Scripture preserves Hashem's living utterance within letters, the contracted form through which divine speech enters this world.

p: וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁנִּיתְּנָה בִּכְתָב כִּי הוּא דִּבּוּר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּנַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה בְּדַבְּרוֹ וְאֵין מוּשָּׂג בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַכְּתָב.

This is the matter of the Written Torah, which was given in writing: it is the speech of the blessed Hashem, of which it says "my soul departed when He spoke," and it cannot be grasped in this world except through writing.
וְכֵן כָּל נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים הוּא הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר ה'
So too, all the Prophets and Writings are the word that Hashem spoke;
וּבִדְבַר ה' שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ הַיְינוּ עֲשִׂיָּה גּוּפָנִית שֶׁמִּדִּבּוּרָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְהַוֶּה גַּם כֵּן לְבוּשִׁים הַגּוּפָנִים דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן.
and "by the word of Hashem the heavens were made"—meaning a bodily creation, for from His blessed utterances the physical garments of this world are likewise formed.
דִּכְלַפֵּי מַעְלָה הַדִּבּוּר הוּא גַּם כֵּן דָּבָר נִבְדָּל מֵהַמָּקוֹר וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ הִתְהַוּוּת לְבוּשִׁים הַמַּעֲלִימִים וּמַרְאִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ דָּבָר נִפְרָד.
Relative to Above, speech is likewise an entity differentiated from its source, and through this unfolds the formation of garments that conceal and present an appearance of a separate entity.
וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם בָּהֶם גָּנוּז חַיּוּת חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּלוּלֵי כֵן לֹא הָיָה לוֹ שׁוּם מְצִיאוּת אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם.
In truth, hidden even within them is the vitality of the Life of the Worlds, blessed be He, for were it not so it would have no existence at all; it is merely in complete concealment.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַמִּכְתָּב מִכְתַּב אֱלֹהִים
This is the meaning of "the writing was the writing of Elohim":
הַיְינוּ כִּי כְּתַב בָּשָׂר וָדָם הוּא כְּכָל פְּעֻלַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חַיּוּת שֶׁל הַפּוֹעֵל כְּלַל
human writing is like every mortal action, possessing none of the vitality of the actor at all,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן פְּעֻלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כֹּחוֹ בַּנִּפְעָל לְעוֹלָם וְהוּא הַמְּקַיְּמוֹ רַק שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם.
whereas in the action of the blessed Hashem His power remains in the product forever and sustains it, only that it is concealed.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתַב שֵׁם אֱלֹהִים שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם הַצִּמְצוּם וְהוּא שֵׁם הַנִּזְכָּר בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית
This is why Scripture used the Name Elohim, the Name of contraction, which is the Name mentioned throughout the Creation narrative,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הָיָה כָּל הִתְהַוּוּת מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית בְּעוֹלַם עֲשִׂיָּה הַגּוּפָנִי.
for through that power occurred the entire coming-into-being of Creation in the physical world of action.

items.h:
Seif 8 — The Tablets, Twilight, and Sacred Script
The letters of Torah continue the divine act of creation, with sacred writing serving as an authorized vessel for His word.

p: וְכֵן כְּתַב לֻחוֹת הוּא מִכְּלַל מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית שֶׁנִּבְרָא בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק ה' דְּאָבוֹת
So too, the inscription of the Tablets belongs to the Works of Creation created at twilight, as the Sages said in the fifth chapter of Avot;
וּדְבָרִים שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת הַיְינוּ עִנְיָנִים שֶׁאֵינָם בְּרִיאָה מְיֻחֶדֶת אֶלָּא גְּמָר שֶׁל כְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה.
and things created at twilight are not a separate creation, but the completion of the totality of Creation.
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹדֵעַ עִתָּיו וּרְגָעָיו וְאֵין אֶצְלוֹ בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת זְמַן סָפֵק
For the blessed Hashem knows His times and moments, and with Him twilight is not a time of doubt;
רַק רֶגַע סוֹף הַיּוֹם וְהֶרֶף עַיִן שֶׁזֶּה נִכְנָס וְזֶה יוֹצֵא הוּא הַנִּקְרָא בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת
rather, the moment of the day's end and the twinkling of an eye when one enters and the other exits is what is called twilight,
וְהוּא רֶגַע סִיּוּם שֶׁל כְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁהָיָה בִּדְבַר ה'
and it is the concluding moment of the whole of Creation that was made by the word of Hashem.
יָצָא לַפּוֹעַל נִגְלָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּבַר ה' עַצְמוֹ בִּכְתַב הַלֻּחוֹת שֶׁהוּא עַצְמוּת דְּבַר ה' עִם הַחַיּוּת שֶׁבַּדִּבּוּר
The word of Hashem itself emerged revealed into this world in the writing of the Tablets, which is the essence of Hashem's word with the vitality of speech;
דְּזֶהוּ רוֹאִים אֶת הַקּוֹלוֹת שֶׁרָאוּ הַקּוֹל בִּכְתַב הַלֻּחוֹת הַנִּרְאֶה לָעַיִן שֶׁהוּא עַצְמוֹ קוֹל ה' מַמָּשׁ.
this is "they saw the voices"—they beheld the voice in the writing of the Tablets visible to the eye, which was literally the voice of Hashem itself.
וְרַשִׁ"י בִּפְסָחִים נ"ד עַמּוּד א' פֵּירֵשׁ עַל כְּתָב וּמִכְתָּב כָּל כְּתַב דְּעָלְמָא
Rashi in Pesachim 54a explained "script and inscription" as referring to all worldly writing;
אֲבָל רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן וְרַבֵּינוּ עוֹבַדְיָה מִבַּרְטְנוּרָא בְּאָבוֹת פֵּירְשׁוּ עַל כְּתַב לֻחוֹת
Maimonides and Rabbeinu Ovadiah of Bartenura in Avot, however, explained it as the writing of the Tablets,
וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ מְצִיאוּת הַכְּתָב בָּעוֹלָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּתַב דְּלֻחוֹת
and all is one, because the root of writing's existence in the world came through the blessed Hashem's creation of the Tablets' inscription,
וְכָל כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ קְדֻשָּׁתָם לְקוּחָה מֵהַכְּתָב דְּלֻחוֹת דְּעַל כֵּן אֵין לְשַׁנּוֹת צוּרַת הָאוֹתִיּוֹת מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁבַּלֻּחוֹת.
and all Sacred Scriptures derive their holiness from the writing of the Tablets, which is why the shapes of the letters may not be altered from those on the Tablets.
וְאַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ בִּכְתַב אֱלֹהִים לִהְיוֹת בּוֹ חַיּוּת אֱלֹהִי מַמָּשׁ כִּבְדִבַר ה'
Even though ordinary sacred writing is not "the writing of God" possessing literal divine vitality like Hashem's direct word,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּכְתַּב עַל פִּי ה' שֶׁצִּוָּה לִכְתֹּב וְנִיתַּן לִכְתֹּב הֲרֵי הַסּוֹפֵר כִּשְׁלוּחוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּבְיָכוֹל.
nevertheless, since it is written at the behest of Hashem Who commanded and authorized it to be written, the scribe acts, as it were, as His blessed emissary.

items.h:
Seif 9 — The Scribe as Divine Emissary
Writing Torah with sacred intent makes the scribe an agent through whom letters become a garment for divine speech.

p: וּכְמוֹ בְּמִצְוַת כִּתְבוּ לָכֶם יוֹצְאִין בִּכְתִיבַת סוֹפֵר בִּשְׁלִיחוּתוֹ וְהוּא שְׁלוּחָא דְּרַחֲמָנָא כִּי הַכֹּל בִּכְתָב מִיַּד ה' הִשְׂכִּיל.

Just as in the mitzvah of "Write down for yourselves" one fulfills the obligation through a scribe acting on his behalf, and the scribe is an agent of the Merciful One, for "All in writing from the hand of Hashem He gave understanding."
וּכְשֶׁכּוֹתֵב לִשְׁמָהּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מֵחַיּוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בִּדְבַר ה'
When he writes with sacred intent, it contains something of the vitality present in Hashem's word;
וְעַל כֵּן דְּבָרִים שֶׁבִּכְתָב אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בְּעַל פֶּה (גִּיטִּין ס:).
therefore, "matters that are in writing you may not recite orally" (Gittin 60b).
כִּי כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁבִּכְתָב הֵם דְּבַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרוּ בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
For all written words are the word of the blessed Hashem spoken through the Holy Spirit,
וְהַנָּבִיא אוֹ הַמְדַבֵּר בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁרוּחַ ה' דִּבֶּר בּוֹ כָּל הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ מִמֶּנּוּ הָיָה שׁוֹמֵעַ דְּבַר ה' וְחַיּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבְּתוֹכָם
and when the prophet or speaker possessed the spirit of Hashem speaking within him, anyone hearing directly from him heard Hashem's word and His blessed vitality within it;
אֲבָל אָדָם אַחֵר שֶׁיֹּאמְרֵם בְּפִיו אֵין בְּדִבּוּרוֹ אוֹתוֹ חַיּוּת כְּלַל שֶׁל דְּבַר ה'.
but another person reciting them orally has no such vitality of Hashem's word in his speech at all.
וְרַק מִתּוֹךְ הַכְּתָב יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹתוֹ חַיּוּת שֶׁהוּא גָּנוּז תּוֹךְ הַכְּתָב כִּי אוֹתָן כְּתוּבִים הֵם לְבוּשִׁים גּוּפָנִים לִדְבַר ה'.
Only from the text can one grasp that vitality concealed within the writing, for those inscribed words are bodily garments for Hashem's word.
כְּמוֹ גּוּף הָאָדָם הַמַּלְבִּישׁ לַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא רוּחָנִיּוּת וְחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיגָהּ עֲרוּמָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֲבָל מִתּוֹךְ לְבוּשׁ הַגּוּף הִיא מוּשֶׂגֶת.
Like the human body clothing the soul—which is spiritual, a portion of God, impossible to apprehend bare in this world, yet grasped through the garment of the body—
כֵּן דְּבַר ה' הוּא מוּשָּׂג עַל יְדֵי לְבוּשׁ הַכְּתָב וְצוּרַת אוֹתִיּוֹת הַמַּחְכִּימוֹת לְהַשִּׂיג עַל יְדֵי זֶה חַיּוּת דְּבַר ה' שֶׁבְּתוֹכָן.
so Hashem's word is grasped through the garment of the script and the letter-forms that enlighten one to attain through them the vitality of Hashem's word within them.

items.h:
Seif 10 — Oral Torah as Living Human Speech
Oral Torah carries the sage's own living vitality through speech, something ordinary human writing cannot fully transmit.

p: אֲבָל דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ: אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בִּכְתָב,
However, Oral Torah is the opposite: you are not permitted to recite them in writing,
כִּי דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא חָכְמַת חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for oral teachings are the wisdom of the sages of Israel,
וְעַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּר הֶחָכָם בַּפֶּה יֵשׁ בּוֹ חַיּוּתוֹ,
and through the speech of the sage with his mouth, his own vitality is present in it,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּכְתָב, אֵין בּוֹ חַיּוּת עוֹד.
which is not so with writing, wherein vitality is no longer present.
כִּי פְּעֻלַּת אָדָם וּמַעֲשֵׂה בָּשָׂר וָדָם אֵינוֹ כְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the activity of man and the handiwork of flesh and blood is not like the work of the Blessed Name,
וְאֵין יָכוֹל לְהַמְשִׁיךְ חַיּוּתוֹ בַּנִּפְעָל,
and man cannot extend his vitality into that which he produces,
וְרַק הַדִּבּוּר, שֶׁהוּא מִכֹּחַ רוּחַ חַיִּים שֶׁבּוֹ, יֵשׁ בּוֹ מֵחַיּוּתוֹ, וְלֹא בִּכְתָב.
and only speech, which issues from the power of the living spirit within him, contains of his vitality, and not writing.
וְעַל כֵּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶׁמָּסַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַתּוֹרָה לַתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
Therefore, Oral Torah—which is that which the Blessed Name transmitted the Torah to those below,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּכֹחָם לְחַדֵּשׁ חִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִשֶּׁלָּהֶם,
so that it would be in their power to innovate original insights of Torah of their own,
וְלִהְיוֹת מַמָּשׁ דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה "לִנְטֹעַ שָׁמַיִם וְלִיסֹד אָרֶץ",
and for them to become literally words of Torah "to plant heavens and lay the foundation of the earth,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א׳, ד׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּנִבְרָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ רוּחָנִיִּים,
as it is written in the Zohar (Part I, 4b): that through this, spiritual heavens and earth are created,
כְּמוֹ דְּ"בִּדְבַר ה' שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ".
just as "by the word of Hashem the heavens were made."
וּבְאוֹרַיְיתָא בָּרָא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא עָלְמָא,
And through the Torah the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world,
אֶלָּא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ נַעֲשָׂה עוֹלַם עֲשִׂיָּה גּוּפָנִי,
except that through His blessed utterance a physical World of Action was made,
שֶׁמִּצַּד תּוֹקֶף הַחַיּוּת, גַּם בְּהִתְלַבְּשׁוֹ בְּגוּפָנִית, אֵין מִטַּנֵּף וּמִתְגַּלֵּם.
which, owing to the intense power of the divine vitality, even when clothing itself within corporeality, does not become soiled or crudely materialized.
כְּטַעַם הַיְּרִידָה לְמִצְרַיִם: "אֲנִי וְלֹא מַלְאָךְ" וְכוּלֵי,
Like the principle of the descent into Egypt: "I and not an angel," and so forth,
שֶׁלְּתֹקֶף הַטֻּמְאָה לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לְשׁוּם מַלְאָךְ וְשָׂרָף לֵירֵד שָׁם,
for due to the severity of the impurity it was impossible for any angel or seraph to descend there,
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּכְבוֹדוֹ וּבְעַצְמוֹ,
only the Blessed Name in His own glory and essence,
דְּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה,
for His kingship rules over all,
גַּם בְּכָל מַדְרֵגוֹת הַתַּחְתּוֹנוֹת וְשֶׁבְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת,
and even into all the lower levels and those of the utmost lowliness,
יוּכַל לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ נִיצוֹץ חַיּוּת הַמְּחַיֶּה וּמְקַיֵּם אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר,
a spark of vitality can clothe itself to animate and sustain that thing,
כִּי הוּא חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים וּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים,
for He is the Life of the Worlds and the Source of life,
וְאֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ שׁוּם חַיּוּת וְקִיּוּם לְשׁוּם דָּבָר.
and there is no vitality or sustenance for anything besides Him.
אֲבָל חַיּוּת הָאָדָם הוּא חַיּוּת פְּרָטִי שֶׁחָלַק לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Human vitality, however, is an individual, apportioned life-force that the Blessed Name allotted to him,
וְאֵין לוֹ תְּפִיסָה וְהִתְלַבְּשׁוּת בִּכְלִי גּוּפָנִי
and it has no capacity to take hold and clothe itself in a physical vessel
אֶלָּא בְּאוֹתוֹ כְּלִי שֶׁקָּבַע וְהִגְבִּיל לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
except in that specific vessel which the Blessed Name determined and delimited for it,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִכָּנֵס לִכְלִי וּלְבוּשׁ אַחֵר לְהַחֲיוֹת כְּלָל [שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ].
and it cannot enter another vessel or garment to animate it at all [outside of the will of the Blessed Name].

items.h:
Seif 11 — When Writing Preserves the Oral Torah
The ban on writing Oral Torah was suspended so it would not be forgotten, preserving Torah through apparent suspension.

p: וְעַל כֵּן, עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אָסוּר לִכְתֹּב דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
Therefore, according to the Torah it is forbidden to write down oral teachings,
כִּי בִּכְתִיבָה מִסְתַּלֵּק חַיּוּת הָאָדָם הַמְדַבֵּר אוֹתָם דְּבָרִים,
because in writing, the vitality of the person speaking those words departs,
וְאֵין מַשִּׂיג אֶלָּא גַּשְׁמִיּוּת הַדָּבָר בְּלֹא חַיּוּת.
and one grasps only the corporeality of the matter without vitality.
וְרַק מִשּׁוּם "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה' הֵפֵרוּ תוֹרָתֶךָ" הִתִּירוּ לִכְתֹּב,
It was solely on account of "It is a time to act for Hashem, they have voided Your Torah" that they permitted writing them down,
כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּכַּח הַדְּבָרִים,
so that the teachings would not be forgotten,
דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי הַכְּתָב נוֹדַע הַדָּבָר כְּפִי הַלְּבוּשׁ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
for in any event, through writing, the concept becomes known according to its garment in this world.
וְהַמֵּבִין יָבִין מִתּוֹךְ הַלְּבוּשׁ גַּם כֵּן
And the discerning will also understand from within the garment
עַל יְדֵי חַיּוּת עַצְמוֹ הַמִּתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתוֹ הַלְּבוּשׁ הַנִּתְפָּס בְּמוֹחוֹ וְשִׂכְלוֹ.
by means of his own vitality clothing itself in that garment grasped by his mind and intellect.
וְזֶהוּ "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת" — עֲשִׂיָּה גּוּפָנִית לַה',
And this is "a time to act"—a corporeal action for Hashem,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא הֲפָרַת הַתּוֹרָה,
and even though it represents a voiding of the Torah,
הַיְינוּ מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁהוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְדִבּוּרוֹ הַמִּתְגַּלֶּה בָּעוֹלָם,
namely the law of the Written Torah, which is the will of the Blessed Name and His speech revealed in the world,
שֶׁכְּפִי רְצוֹנוֹ אֵין תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִתְקַבֵּל אֶלָּא פֶּה אֶל פֶּה וְאֵין לְהַלְבִּישׁוֹ בִּכְתָב,
that according to His will Oral Torah is to be received only mouth to mouth and is not to be clothed in writing,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, אַדְּרַבָּה, זֶהוּ קִיּוּם הַתּוֹרָה.
nevertheless, on the contrary, this is the very preservation of the Torah.
כִּי גַּם זֶה דְּ"עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת" וְגוֹמֵר מִכְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה,
For this principle, "It is a time to act..." and so forth, is likewise part of the Torah,
דִּפְעָמִים בִּטּוּלָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה זֶהוּ יְסוֹדָהּ,
that at times the suspension of the Torah is its foundation,
וַאֲמָרוּהוּ בִּמְנָחוֹת צ״ט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳ עַל שְׁבִירַת לוּחוֹת
and they said this in Menachot 99b regarding the breaking of the Tablets
וְ"הַמִּכְתָּב מִכְתַּב אֱלֹהִים".
and "the writing was the writing of Elohim."

items.h:
Seif 12 — The Sages' Authority to Give Torah a Written Garment
Because Torah was entrusted to the sages, they could authorize a written form that still conveys living concepts.

p: וּמַמָּשׁ דֻּגְמַת זֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן כְּתִיבַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And exactly parallel to this was likewise the writing down of the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ, לִכְתֹּב מִכְתַּב בָּשָׂר וָדָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חַיּוּת.
which is the opposite: writing an inscription of flesh and blood that contains no vitality.
אַךְ כֵּיוָן דְּיֵשׁ כֹּחַ זֶה גַּם כֵּן בְּיַד חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהָפֵר תּוֹרָה,
However, since the sages of Israel also possess this power to annul a precept of the Torah,
שֶׁהוּא כְּטַעַם (מוֹעֵד קָטָן ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גּוֹזֵר וְצַדִּיק מְבַטֵּל,
which follows the principle (Moed Katan 16b): the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees and the righteous one annuls,
שֶׁכָּךְ מָסַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַתּוֹרָה לְגַמְרֵי לַתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
for the Blessed Name handed over the Torah entirely to those below,
וְכֵן הַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהוּא בַּתּוֹרָה.
and likewise the governance of the world, which operates through the Torah.
עַל כֵּן גַּם דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִכְתֹּב דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הָיָה בְּיָדָם לְבַטֵּל,
Therefore this principle as well—that one may not write down oral teachings—they had the authority to override,
וּמִמֵּילָא יִשְׁתַּנֶּה הַדָּבָר גַּם בְּעִנְיַן הַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם,
and automatically the reality shifts regarding the governance of the world as well,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּכֹחַ לְהַמְשִׁיךְ חַיּוּת בְּדִבְרֵיהֶם הַנִּכְתָּבִים.
so that the power exists to extend vitality into their inscribed words.
וְאַף שֶׁאֵין הַחַיּוּת הַמִּתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּעֶצֶם הַכְּתָב דֻּגְמַת הַחַיּוּת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
And even though the vitality clothing itself in the physical writing is not identical to the vitality in the Written Torah,
שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֶה לְחַיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַמִּתְלַבֵּשׁ בַּגּוּף בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
which resembles the soul's vitality clothing itself in the body in this world,
דְּעַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּתוּבָה אַשּׁוּרִית עַל הַסֵּפֶר וּבִדְיוֹ דַּוְקָא,
wherefore it must be written in Ashurit script on parchment and strictly in ink,
וְאִם חָסַר אוֹת אֶחָד נִפְסַל הַכֹּל,
and if a single letter is missing the entire scroll is invalidated,
וְכֵן שְׁאָר פְּסוּלֵי סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה,
as well as the other disqualifications of a Torah scroll,
דֻּגְמַת אֵיזֶה קִלְקוּל שֶׁאֵֵירַע בַּגּוּף הַגּוֹרֵם סִלּוּק לְחַיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁבּוֹ.
analogous to a fatal defect occurring in the physical body that causes the departure of the soul's vitality within it.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּתִיבַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת חַיּוּת עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה,
This is not so regarding the writing of the Oral Torah, in which vitality does not invest itself in this bodily manner;
אֵין תְּנָאִים בִּכְתִיבָתוֹ וְלֹא שַׁיָּךְ בּוֹ פִּסּוּל בִּכְתִיבָה.
there are no rigid scribal conditions in its transcription, and halachic invalidation does not apply to its writing.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, יֵשׁ בּוֹ הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת חַיּוּת דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל בָּעִנְיָן הַנִּכְתָּב,
Nevertheless, it does possess an investiture of vitality in a general sense within the recorded concept,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מוּשָּׂג גַּם עֶצֶם הַחַיּוּת שֶׁבַּדִּבּוּרִים הָהֵם
so that the very vitality inherent in those spoken words can also be attained
לְשֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם הַמַּשִּׂיגָם כַּאֲשֶׁר הַדְּבָרִים מִתְעַצְּמִים בְּשִׂכְלוֹ.
by the intellect of the person apprehending them when the concepts become fully integrated into his mind.

items.h:
Seif 13 — Hearing a Sage versus Reading a Book
Words spoken from the heart carry a living impression that books cannot reproduce, while writing preserves what exile would erase.

p: וְזֶהוּ הַחִלּוּק שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁאֵין דּוֹמֶה שְׁמוּעָה מִפִּי חָכָם לִרְאִיָּה בִּסְפָרִים,
This explains the well-known distinction that hearing a teaching directly from the mouth of a sage is not comparable to seeing it in books;
כִּי דְּבָרִים הַיּוֹצְאִים מִלֵּב חָכָם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם חַיּוּת גָּמוּר הַמִּתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתָן דִּבּוּרִים
for words that issue from the heart of a sage contain complete vitality that clothes itself in those spoken words
דֶּרֶךְ הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת גָּמוּר מֵחַיּוּת הַמְדַבֵּר עַצְמוֹ.
by way of a complete investiture of the speaker’s own vitality.
וְעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ בָּהֶם כֹּחַ לִפְעוֹל בְּלֵב הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ, כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּ"דְבָרִים הַיּוֹצְאִים מִן הַלֵּב נִכְנָסִים לַלֵּב".
Therefore, they possess the power to make an impression on the heart of the listener, as is known: “words that issue from the heart enter the heart.”
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּכְתִיבָה, הַהִתְלַבְּשׁוּת אֵינוֹ מִצַּד חַיּוּת פְּרָטִי שֶׁל חָכָם הַמְחַדֵּשׁ הַדָּבָר הַהוּא,
In writing, by contrast, the investiture does not derive from the personal vitality of the sage who innovated that teaching,
דְּאוֹתוֹ חַיּוּת אֵין יָכוֹל לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּכְתָב,
for that individual vitality cannot clothe itself in written letters,
רַק מִצַּד הִתְכַּלְלוּת חַיּוּתוֹ בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים, יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁהוּא חֵלֶק מִמֶּנּוּ,
but only from the inclusion of his vitality within the Source of Life, blessed be His Name, of which he is a part,
וְגַם חָכְמַת בְּנֵי אָדָם הַכֹּל הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and all human wisdom likewise stems entirely from the blessed Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ הִתְכַּלְלוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
This reflects the inclusion of the Oral Torah within the Written Torah,
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל רָמוּז בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
for in truth everything is hinted at in the Written Torah,
וְגַם "כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ נֶאֱמַר לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי" (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה כ״ב),
and even “everything a devoted student will innovate in the future was already stated to Moses at Sinai” (Vayikra Rabbah 22:1),
וְהַכֹּל הוּא דְּבַר ה' מִצַּד שָׁרְשׁוֹ וּמְקוֹרוֹ, כִּי מִשָּׁם לוּקָּח,
and everything is the word of Hashem in terms of its root and source, for from there it was taken,
וְהַכֹּל הוּא דְּבַר תּוֹרָה גָּמוּר וְהַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר ה'.
and all of it is complete Torah and the very word that Hashem spoke.
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה שֶׁל הַחַיּוּת הַכְּלָלִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And from this perspective of the collective vitality present in the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד דְּבַר ה' שֶׁאָמַר: "עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ" וְגוֹמֵר, "לֹא תָסוּר מִן הַדָּבָר" וְגוֹמֵר, "שְׁאַל אָבִיךָ" וְגוֹמֵר,
which derives from the word of Hashem who said: “According to the Torah they teach you...,” “You shall not deviate from the matter...,” and “Ask your father...”
דְּעַל כֵּן מְבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ" עַל מִצְוֹת דְּרַבָּנָן,
which is why we recite the blessing “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us” over rabbinic commandments,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (כ״ג עַמּוּד א׳), דְּגַם זֶה מִצְוַת ה' דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל —
as the Sages explained in Shabbat 23a, that this too constitutes the commandment of Hashem in a general sense—
חַיּוּת זֶה יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת נִתְפָּס בִּכְתָב כְּכָל דְּבָרִים שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
this vitality can indeed be captured in writing like all written matters,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהִיא מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בִּכְתָב פְּרָטִי בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר פְּרָטִי שֶׁחִדְּשׁוּ סוֹפְרִים.
only that it expands into a specific written text concerning that particular insight innovated by the Scribes.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִכְנָס לְשֵׂכֶל הַמַּשִּׂיג,
And when it enters the intellect of the one studying it,
מִצַּד הִתְדַּבְּקוּתָם בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים דִּדְבַר ה' הַכְּלָלִי הַגָּנוּז בּוֹ,
by virtue of their attachment to the Source of Life through the general word of Hashem hidden within it,
יוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג כָּל פְּרָטֵי הַחַיּוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר,
he can attain all the details of the vitality present in that matter,
כְּאִלּוּ שָׁמַע פֶּה אֶל פֶּה מִבַּעַל שְׁמוּעָה הָעוֹמֵד לְנֶגְדּוֹ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב׳ דִּשְׁקָלִים י״א עַמּוּד א׳).
as though he heard it mouth-to-mouth from the master of the teaching standing before him (Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim 2:5 [11a]).
אֶלָּא שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לָזֶה הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֵׂכֶל הַמַּשִּׂיג גַּם כֵּן יוֹתֵר מִבִּשְׁמִיעָה פֶּה אֶל פֶּה.
However, this requires intellectual exertion on the part of the student far greater than what is needed when hearing mouth-to-mouth.
וְאִלְמָלֵא נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ לוּחוֹת, לֹא הָיוּ שׁוֹכְחִים דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כַּיָּדוּעַ (עֵירוּבִין נ״ד עַמּוּד א׳),
And had the Tablets not been broken, words of Torah would never have been forgotten, as is known (Eruvin 54a),
לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לִכְתֹּב תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
and there would have been no need to commit the Oral Torah to writing.
אֲבָל זֶה גַּם כֵּן מִכְּלַל יְסוֹדָהּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי בִּטּוּלָהּ,
Yet this too is part of the principle that its suspension serves its foundation,
דְּעַל יְדֵי שְׁבִירַת לוּחוֹת, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֶחֱזִירוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
for through the breaking of the Tablets, they brought the Oral Torah back to being like the Written Torah,
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
so that it could clothe itself in this world.

items.h:
Seif 14 — The Oral Torah as Israel's Inner Secret
The Written Torah's outer form can be copied, but its inner meaning belongs uniquely to Israel through Oral Torah.

p: וְזֶה דָּבָר גָּדוֹל וִיסוֹד הַתּוֹרָה,
This is a great matter and a foundational principle of the Torah:
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה הוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
for in truth, the essential core of the Torah is the Oral Torah,
כִּי מַה שֶּׁבִּכְתָב אֵין לָאָדָם תְּפִיסָה בּוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
since a person has no grasp of what is written except through the Oral Torah.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא תִּשָּׂא ל״ד):
And as the Sages taught in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 34):
שֶׁעֲתִידִין אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לוֹמַר "אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל" וְכוּלֵי,
in the future the nations of the world will say, “We are Israel,” and so forth,
"מִי שֶׁמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי בְּיָדוֹ" וְכוּלֵי;
and the Holy One will respond: “He who possesses My secret mysteries...,” and so forth.
דְּמִצַּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, שֶׁהוּא הַלְּבוּשׁ גַּשְׁמִי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
For regarding the Written Torah, which constitutes the physical garment in this world,
יוּכְלוּ גַּם אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לוֹמַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם תְּפִיסָה וַאֲחִיזָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
the nations of the world can also claim that they have a grasp and hold upon the words of Torah.
וּבֶאֱמֶת "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי",
In truth, however, “He has not done so for any nation,”
וַאֲפִילּוּ יְקַיְּמוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם
and even if they were to observe the entire Torah, it counts for nothing
אִם לֹא יִתְגַּיְּרוּ וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכֻנּוּ,
unless they convert and are called by the name of Israel,
כִּי לֹא נִיתְּנָה תוֹרָה אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנִּתְגַּלּוּ לָהֶם הַמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁבָּהּ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
for the Torah was given only to Israel, to whom its inner mysteries were revealed through the Oral Torah.

items.h:
Seif 15 — The Second Temple and the Rise of Oral Torah
With prophecy diminished, the Second Temple era became the great flowering of Torah's inner radiance through the sages.

p: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפִרְקֵי הֵיכָלוֹת (פֶּרֶק כ״ז):
And as it is written in Pirkei Heichalot (chapter 27):
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי,
that even though the Shechinah did not abide in the Second Temple,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה וְזִיוָהּ וַהֲדָרָהּ לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי,
nevertheless the essence of the Torah, its radiance, and its splendor existed only in the Second Temple;
שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ לִבְנוֹת עַד שֶׁהִבְטִיחָם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְגַלּוֹת לָהֶם רָזֵי הַתּוֹרָה,
for they refused to build it until the blessed Hashem promised to reveal to them the secrets of the Torah;
יְעֻיַּן שָׁם בִּפְנִים.
let it be examined there in the text itself.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הַתְחָלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הָיָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי מֵאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה,
This is because the beginning of the Oral Torah occurred during the Second Temple period through the Men of the Great Assembly;
שֶׁהֵם מְיַסְּדֵי הַבַּיִת, הֵם יִסְּדוּ גַּם כֵּן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
those who founded the House were the very ones who also founded the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּשְׁקָלִים (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ה׳).
as the Sages stated in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim 5:1.
וּבִימֵי מָרְדֳּכַי, דְּקִיְּמוּ מַה שֶּׁקִּבְּלוּ כְּבָר,
And in the days of Mordechai, when they reaffirmed what they had already accepted,
שֶׁחָזְרוּ לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה שֶׁלֹּא עַל יְדֵי כְּפִיַּת הַר כְּגִיגִית,
returning to receive the Torah out of love rather than through the mountain suspended over them like a vat,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳), אָז זָכוּ לְכָךְ.
as our Sages of blessed memory taught in Shabbat 88a, they then merited this.
כִּי עִיקַּר הַכְּפִיַּת הַר הָיָה עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
For the principal coercion at the mountain was directed at the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ, עַיֵּן שָׁם בִּפְנִים;
as the Sages taught in Midrash Tanchuma, Parashat Noach; see there in the text;
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא קִבְּלוּהָ מֵרְצוֹנָם, לֹא נִמְסְרָה עֲדַיִן לָהֶם לְגַמְרֵי,
and as long as they had not accepted it willingly, it was not yet fully handed over to them,
וְהָיוּ מִתְנַהֲגִים עַל פִּי נְבִיאִים, הַכֹּל בִּכְתָב מִיַּד ה'.
and they were guided through the prophets, with everything in writing directly from the hand of Hashem.

items.h:
Seif 16 — Why a Sage Can Surpass a Prophet
Prophecy sees through spiritual vision, while a sage's intellectual Ruach HaKodesh can penetrate beyond visionary form.

p: וְאַף שֶׁהַנְּבוּאָה הוּא גִּלּוּי מְפֹרָשׁ מַרְאוֹת ה' יוֹתֵר מֵהַשָּׂגַת הַחֲכָמִים,
Although prophecy is an explicit revelation of visions of Hashem far beyond the intellectual perception of the sages,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא י״ב עַמּוּד א׳ דְּ"חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא",
nevertheless the Sages taught in Bava Batra 12a that “a sage is superior to a prophet”;
וְעַיֵּן שָׁם בְּרַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן נַחְמָן דְּיָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג מַעֲמַקִּים יוֹתֵר.
and see Nachmanides there, who explains that the sage can attain greater depths.
וְכַיָּדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה, שֶׁהִגִּיד דְּבָרִים בְּעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים
And as is known from the holy Ari of blessed memory, who disclosed teachings concerning supernal worlds
שֶׁכְּפִי דַּעַת עַצְמוֹ הוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים
which by his own reckoning transcend the attainment of all the prophets,
וַאֲפִילּוּ הַשָּׂגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כַּנּוֹדָע לַהוֹגִים בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה.
and even the attainment of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, as is well known to those who study his writings.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם הִשִּׂיגוּ דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיָּה,
The distinction is that the prophets perceived through vision,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִרְאוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה יוֹתֵר כְּפִי הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת גּוּפָנִיּוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and one cannot see more in this world beyond what the physical garments of this world allow,
דְּעַל כֵּן דִּבְרֵיהֶם נִתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב בִּלְבוּשׁ גָּמוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
which is why their words could be committed to writing in a complete worldly garment.
אֲבָל הוּא הִשִּׂיג דֶּרֶךְ הַשָּׂגָה בַּשֵּׂכֶל,
The sage, however, attains through the intellect,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן נַחְמָן שָׁם,
which is the attainment of the Holy Spirit, as Nachmanides wrote there;
וְשֶׁלֹּא דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיָּה אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג הַרְבֵּה.
and without the constraints of sensory vision, one can attain vastly more.

items.h:
Seif 17 — Rabbi Akiva and What Moshe Did Not See
Moshe received future Torah prophetically, yet later sages could inwardly comprehend innovations beyond prophetic sight.

p: וְזֶה מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְנָחוֹת (כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
This explains what the Sages said in Menachot 29b,
דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, לֹא הֵבִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not understand the words of Rabbi Akiva;
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (חֻקַּת) דְּ"רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם",
and in Midrash Rabbah (Chukat) that “Rabbi Akiva’s eye saw what Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not see.”
וְאַף דְּלֹא קָם כָּמוֹהוּ, הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַשָּׂגָתוֹ דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיָּה,
Though none arose like Moses, this refers specifically to attainment through visionary sight,
וְלוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה גַּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ, וַאֲפִילּוּ מַה שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ.
for to Moses was revealed everything an advanced student would ever innovate, even what Rabbi Akiva would innovate.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַכֹּל הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת נְבוּאָה דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיָּה,
However, all of that was prophetic revelation through vision,
וְלֹא דֶּרֶךְ הַשָּׂגָה שִׂכְלִיּוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁמַּשִּׂיגִים אוֹתָם הַמְחַדְּשִׁים הַדְּבָרִים,
and not through the intellectual grasp experienced by those who innovate the concepts,
שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה לֹא נִתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב,
a mode of insight that was never permitted to be written;
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַלְבִּישׁ בִּכְתָב כְּלָל,
for such an essence cannot be clothed in writing at all,
רַק מַה שֶּׁ"לֵּב חָכָם יַשְׂכִּיל פִּיהוּ",
it can only be that “the heart of the wise teaches his mouth,”
וְעִיקַּר הַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא סוֹד נֶעְלָם בְּלֵב הַמַּשִּׂיג.
and the essential core of the perception remains a hidden secret in the heart of the one who attains it.

items.h:
Seif 18 — Written Miracles and the Border of Purim
Recorded miracles descend into physical salvation; Purim stands where written revelation begins to give way to Oral Torah.

p: וְעַל כֵּן כָּל הַנִּסִּים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב
Therefore, all miracles performed for Israel that were permitted to be written down
הֵם יְשׁוּעוֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת, שֶׁנִּיצּוֹלוּ מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵרוּת וּמִמָּוֶת לְחַיִּים,
are physical salvations, where they were delivered from slavery to freedom and from death to life;
כִּי כֻּלָּם יְשׁוּעוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for all of them are the salvations of the blessed Hashem,
שֶׁהוּא הוֹשִׁיעָם בְּרַחֲמָיו וּבְרוֹב חֲסָדָיו בְּנֵס גָּלוּי לַכֹּל שֶׁהוּא הָעוֹזֵר וּמוֹשִׁיעַ.
Who delivered them in His mercy and abundant kindness through a miracle revealed to all that He is the Helper and Savior.
וִישׁוּעוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹבֵר בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת
And the salvations of the blessed Hashem traverse all the worlds
עַד שֶׁמִּתְלַבֵּשׁ גַּם בְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה הַגּוּפָנִי, וּבָא הַצָּלָה לַגּוּפוֹת גַּם כֵּן.
until they clothe themselves even in the physical World of Action, bringing rescue to physical bodies as well.
וְעַל כֵּן הָרֹשֶׁם הַנִּשְׁאָר קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים לְדוֹרוֹת עוֹלָם נִיתַּן לִכְתֹּב גַּם כֵּן
Hence the enduring impression established for all generations could likewise be committed to writing
וּלְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת הַכְּתָב,
and clothed within the letters of the text;
וְכֵן נִקְבַּע מֵהֶם יָמִים טוֹבִים, שֶׁהוּא בְּעוֹנֶג הַגּוּף וְשִׂמְחָתוֹ וּשְׁבִיתָתוֹ מִמְּלָאכָה,
and likewise festivals were established from them, celebrated through bodily pleasure, joy, and cessation of labor,
כִּי נִפְעַל הַיְשׁוּעָה גַּם לַגּוּף.
because salvation was effected for the physical body as well.
וְזֶהוּ הַכֹּל מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּפָנִי,
This all belongs to the aspect of this physical world,
צְרִיכִים הַנִּסִּים גַּם כֵּן לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּלְבוּשֵׁי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
in that the miracles too must clothe themselves in the garments of this world;
וְעַל כֵּן נִמְשְׁלוּ הַכֹּל לְלַיְלָה עַד אֶסְתֵּר,
therefore all of them were compared to night until Esther,
שֶׁהִיא סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים הַנִּיתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב,
who marks the end of all miracles permitted to be written,
וְהִיא כְּמוֹ הַתְחָלָה לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and serves as an opening to the Oral Torah,
כִּי הוּא הַמִּצְוָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים שֶׁנִּתְחַדְּשָׁה לְמִצְוָה קְבוּעָה לְדוֹרוֹת עַל יְדֵי סוֹפְרִים וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה.
for it is the first rabbinic commandment established for all generations by the Scribes and the Men of the Great Assembly.
וְעַל כֵּן אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּלֹא נִיתְּנָה לִכְתֹּב (מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳),
Therefore, one opinion holds that the Megillah was not permitted to be written (Megillah 7a),
וְשֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת מִכְּלַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
arguing that it truly belongs to the domain of the Oral Torah;
וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּנִיתְּנָה לִכְתֹּב, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הִיא הַסּוֹף מִמַּדְרֵגַת הַכְּתָב,
and according to the one who holds it was permitted to be written, it is nevertheless the very end of the level of written scripture,
וּלְעוֹלָם סוֹף מַדְרֵגָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה הוּא הַתְחָלָה וְכֶתֶר לַמַּדְרֵגָה שֶׁאַחֲרֶיהָ.
and the end of a higher level is always the beginning and crown of the level that follows.

items.h:
Seif 19 — Purim as Providence Clothed in Nature
Purim hides divine sovereignty within ordinary causality, revealing Hashem's rule through a salvation that appears natural.

p: וְהַיְינוּ דְּנֵס דְּפוּרִים לֹא הָיָה עוֹד נֵס נִגְלֶה עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ,
This means that the miracle of Purim was no longer an overtly manifest miracle directly wrought by the blessed Hashem Himself,
וּלְמַרְאֵה עַיִן הָיָה קְצָת דֶּרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע, כִּי לְאַהֲבַת אֶסְתֵּר עָשָׂה אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ.
and to outward appearances it occurred somewhat through natural causality, for Ahasuerus acted out of love for Esther.
וְזֶה טַעַם "וַתִּלְבַּשׁ אֶסְתֵּר מַלְכוּת",
This is the deeper meaning of “and Esther clothed herself in royalty,”
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם י״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): שֶׁלְּבָשַׁתָּהּ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
concerning which our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Megillah 14b): that the Holy Spirit clothed her;
וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, נַעֲשֵׂית הִיא לְבוּשׁ לְאוֹתָהּ מִדָּה שֶׁהִלְבִּישָׁה הִיא אֶת הַמַּלְכוּת.
namely, the divine attribute of His blessed Sovereignty (Malkhut)—she became a garment for that very attribute, as she clothed Royalty itself.
וְכָל נִסִּים הַנִּגְלִים כִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וְהַדּוֹמֶה,
And all the openly revealed miracles, such as the Exodus from Egypt and the like,
אַף שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
even though they were carried out through Moses and Aaron and similar intermediaries,
הָיָה גָּלוּי לַכֹּל כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַפּוֹעֵל,
it was evident to all that the blessed Hashem was the true Agent,
לְפִי שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ בְּשֵׁם הַהֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא הַגִּלּוּי שֶׁהוּא הַמְהַוֶּה הַכֹּל.
because they were enacted through the Name Havayah, which is the revelation that He brings everything into existence.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר פַּרְעֹה: "מִי ה'" וְגוֹמֵר — רָצָה לוֹמַר שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה,
Therefore Pharaoh said: “Who is Hashem...” and so forth—meaning the Name Havayah,
דְּזֶה "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי" וְאֵין לָהֶם הַשָּׂגָה בְּשֵׁם זֶה כְּלָל.
for concerning this, “He has not dealt so with any nation,” and they possess no perception of this Name whatsoever.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִצַּד שֵׁם הָאַדְנוּת, מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּבַכֹּל מָשָׁלָה,
This is not so from the aspect of the Name Adonut, the attribute of His blessed Kingship that rules over all,
וְגַם הַגּוֹיִם קָרוּ לֵיהּ "אֱלָהָא דֶּאֱלָהַיָּא", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סוֹף מְנָחוֹת (ק״י עַמּוּד א׳),
and even the gentiles refer to Him as the “God of gods,” as the Sages noted at the end of Menachot (110a),
אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּסַר הַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם לְכוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְהַנְהָגַת הַטֶּבַע.
merely imagining that He relinquished the daily governance of the cosmos to celestial forces and the mechanisms of nature.
וְנֵס דְּפוּרִים הָיָה מְלֻבָּשׁ בְּדֶרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע,
Thus the miracle of Purim was cloaked within the natural order;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, בֶּאֱמֶת הָיְתָה הַכָּרָה מְפֹרֶשֶׁת בָּזֶה בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל עַמּוֹ.
nevertheless, in truth there emerged an explicit recognition of this throughout the entire world, that the blessed Hashem actively oversees His people.

items.h:
Seif 20 — Esther's Demand to Be Written
Esther insists that Purim's hidden providence be recognized as explicit divine salvation while its mitzvot celebrate bodily rescue.

p: וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁאָמְרָה אֶסְתֵּר: "קִבְעוּנִי לְדוֹרוֹת",
And this is the reason that Esther said: “Establish me for all generations,”
וְהֵשִׁיבוּ: "קִנְאָה אַתְּ מְעוֹרֶרֶת", "כִּתְבוּנִי" וְכוּלֵי (שָׁם ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳);
and the Sages responded: “You are arousing jealousy against us,” and regarding “Write me down...” and so forth (Megillah 7a);
שֶׁהַכְּתִיבָה מוֹרָה עַל נֵס מְפֹרָשׁ וְנִיכָּר גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לִישׁוּעַת ה',
for committing it to writing signifies a miracle explicit and discernible even within this world as the salvation of Hashem,
וְהֵם חָשְׁבוּ דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם סוֹבְרִים דְּהָיְתָה סִבָּה טִבְעִית.
whereas the Sages assumed that the nations of the world would view it merely as a natural occurrence.
וְהִיא הֱשִׁיבָתַם: "כְּבָר כְּתוּבָה" וְכוּלֵי —
And she replied to them: “It is already recorded...” and so forth—
רָצָה לוֹמַר דְּגַם הֵם כָּתְבוּ זֶה לְנֵס וִישׁוּעַת ה',
meaning that the nations themselves had likewise recorded it as a miracle and a divine deliverance.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִלָּה י״א עַמּוּד א׳: "אֵימָתַי רָאוּ כָּל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ" וְכוּלֵי;
And as the Sages said in Megillah 11a: “When did all the ends of the earth see...” and so forth;
דִּבְנֵס גָּלוּי הֲרֵי גָּלוּי לַכֹּל, אֲבָל זֶה שֶׁהָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לַמִּתְעַקְּשִׁים לִתְלוֹת בְּדֶרֶךְ טִבְעִי,
for in an open miracle the matter is immediately visible to everyone, whereas here it was possible for obstinate individuals to ascribe it to natural causes,
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם כְּפִי הַסִּבּוֹת וְהַמְסֻבָּבִים הַנִּסְמָכִים הֵבִינוּ הַכֹּל דְּהוּא פֹּעַל ה' וִישׁוּעַת אֱלֹהֵינוּ,
yet because of the interconnected sequence of causes and effects, everyone comprehended that this was the work of Hashem and the salvation of our God;
זֶה נִקְרָא רְאִיַּת אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ —
this is termed the perception of the “ends of the earth”—
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁהֵבִינוּ שֶׁגַּם בִּפְעֻלּוֹת הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהֵם פְּעֻלּוֹת הַטִּבְעִיִּים יֵשׁ דֶּרֶךְ נִסִּי וִישׁוּעַת ה'.
meaning they recognized that even within earthly, mundane actions—which operate naturally—there exists a miraculous course and the direct salvation of Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ קְצֵה הַקּוֹמָה דִּישׁוּעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְנִסָּיו הַנִּגְלִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
This represents the outer perimeter of the structure of the blessed Hashem’s salvation and His revealed miracles in this world,
שֶׁמִּדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הוּא מִדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה בְּכָל קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה כַּנּוֹדָע,
for the attribute of Malkhut is the final attribute in every complete spiritual configuration, as is known,
וְהִיא לְהַרְאוֹת מַלְכוּתוֹ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים וּבְהַנְהָגַת הָאָרֶץ הַזּוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and its purpose is to demonstrate His sovereignty among the lower realms and within the terrestrial governance of this physical world.
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם הִיא הָיְתָה יְשׁוּעָה גּוּפָנִית מִמִּיתָה לְחַיִּים,
Therefore, this deliverance too was a corporeal salvation from death to life,
וְלָכֵן קְבָעוּם יְמֵי מִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה לַהֲנָאַת הַגּוּף גַּם כֵּן.
and for that reason they established them as days of feasting and gladness for the physical pleasure of the body as well.

items.h:
Seif 21 — Why Purim Is Not a Full Yom Tov
Purim's deepest victory is spiritual - renewed Torah and mitzvah - while political servitude remains, so labor was not suspended.

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, יוֹם טוֹב לֹא קַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ לִהְיוֹת שְׁבִיתָה גְּמוּרָה לַגּוּף
And nevertheless, they did not take upon themselves a full festival (yom tov) involving complete cessation of labor for the body,
מִשּׁוּם דְּ"אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן",
because “we are still the servants of Ahasuerus,”
וְלֹא הָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּה גְּמוּרָה לַגּוּף מִשִּׁעְבּוּד גַּם כֵּן;
and there was not a complete physical redemption from servitude;
דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, הָעִיקָּר בַּיְשׁוּעָה דְּאָז הָיָה דְּ"לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה" וְגוֹמֵר,
since in any event, the essential core of the salvation then was that “the Jews had light...” and so forth,
דְּפֵירְשׁוּ בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּמְגִלָּה (ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳): זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְיוֹם טוֹב וּמִילָה וּתְפִלִּין, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
which the Sages expounded at the end of the first chapter of Megillah (16b): this refers to Torah, festival, circumcision, and tefillin; see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְסַנְחֵרִיב וּנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר כֻּלָּם לֹא בָּאוּ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד אֱמוּנָתָם דַּוְקָא,
This means that the exile of Egypt, Sennacherib, and Nebuchadnezzar did not come upon Israel specifically on account of their religious faith,
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יַעַזְבוּ אֱמוּנָתָם גַּם כֵּן הָיוּ מִשְׁתַּעְבְּדִים בָּהֶם וּמַגְלִים אוֹתָם.
for even had they abandoned their faith, those conquerors would still have subjugated them and exiled them.
וְכֵן כָּל הַצָּרוֹת דְּעַד בַּיִת שֵׁנִי שֶׁהָיוּ מֵהָאֻמּוֹת לֹא מָצִינוּ גְּזֵרַת שְׁמָד,
And similarly, in all the afflictions suffered from the nations prior to the Second Temple, we find no decrees of religious apostasy (shemad),
דְּלָא אִכְפַּת לְהוּ בֶּאֱמוּנָה,
for they did not care about religious dogma,
רַק בָּאוּ לְכָבְשָׁם וְלִלְחוֹם בָּם כְּמוֹ בְּאֻמָּה אַחֶרֶת,
they merely came to conquer them and wage war against them as against any other nation,
וְהוּא רַק צַעַר הַגּוּפָנִי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵם כָּל יִעוּדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בִּשְׂכַר וָעֹנֶשׁ גּוּפָנִי.
and this was solely physical distress, just as all the promises of the Written Torah are phrased in terms of physical reward and punishment.

items.h:
Seif 22 — Why the Written Torah Speaks in Physical Reward
Written Torah is the physical garment of divine truth; its spiritual meanings are uncovered through the Oral Torah.

p: וְכָל הַקַּדְמוֹנִים נִתְקַשּׁוּ בָּזֶה עַל שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שָׂכָר וָעֹנֶשׁ הָרוּחָנִי,
And all the early commentators struggled with this question: why spiritual reward and punishment is not explicitly detailed in the Written Torah;
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין זֶה קֻשְׁיָא כְּלָל,
yet in truth this is no difficulty at all,
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, הַכְּתָב הוּא לְבוּשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
for in the Written Torah, the written script is the physical garment of the Torah in this world,
וְכָךְ הִיא הַתּוֹרָה בְּכָל עוֹלָם מִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּלְבוּשׁ הַשַּׁיָּךְ לְאוֹתוֹ עוֹלָם,
and so it is that in every world the Torah clothes itself in the garment appropriate to that world:
וּבָעוֹלָם הָרוּחָנִי שָׁם אוֹתָן יִעוּדִים עַצְמָם הֵם בְּרוּחָנִיּוּת, וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֵם בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת.
in the spiritual realm those very same promises exist spiritually, while in this world they appear materially.
וְדָבָר זֶה שֶׁל שָׂכָר וָעֹנֶשׁ הָרוּחָנִי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ פֵּירוּשׁ עַל שָׂכָר וָעֹנֶשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי שֶׁבִּכְתָב לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And this concept of spiritual reward and punishment is disclosed only by way of exposition upon the physical reward and punishment of the written text by the sages of Israel in the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהֵם מַשִּׂיגִים מִסְטוֹרִיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וּכְפִי מַה שֶּׁהִיא בְּכָל עוֹלָמוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנִים.
for they apprehend the inner mysteries hidden within the Written Torah and how it exists across all supernal realms.
אֲבָל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב עַצְמָהּ, שֶׁהִיא לְבוּשָׁהּ הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
However, in the Written Torah itself, which is its manifest garment in this world,
אֵין לִכְתֹּב כְּלָל אֶלָּא הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
it is not appropriate to write anything other than what is manifest in this physical world.

items.h:
Seif 23 — Torah's Hidden Governance of the World
Hashem governs all realms through Torah, but both Torah's meaning and providence remain deeply concealed from ordinary perception.

p: וּמִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
From the standpoint of the Written Torah, meaning from the perspective of the blessed Hashem,
הָיָה רָאוּי כֵּן בֶּאֱמֶת לִהְיוֹת בָּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה תֵּיכֶף הַשָּׂכָר וָעֹנֶשׁ כְּיִעוּדֵי הַתּוֹרָה;
it would indeed have been fitting that reward and punishment be realized immediately in this world according to the Torah's promises;
כִּי כָּל דְּבַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא פּוֹעֵל בְּשָׁוֶה בָּעוֹלָמוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנִים כְּמוֹ בְּעוֹלַם עֲשִׂיָּה הַגּוּפָנִי, כִּי אֶצְלוֹ הַכֹּל שָׁוֶה,
for every utterance of the blessed Hashem operates equally in the supernal realms as in the physical World of Action, since with Him all is unified,
וְהַנְהָגַת כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה.
and the governance of all realms proceeds solely according to the Torah.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת "נָעוּ מַעְגְּלֹתֶיהָ" שֶׁל תּוֹרָה,
However, in truth the paths of the Torah are deeply intricate and unfathomable;
וְאַף עַל פִּי דִּכְתִיבָא וּמַנְחָא, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לֵידַע כְּלוּם מִמֶּנָּה אִם לֹא עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and even though it is written and laid before us, it is impossible to know anything of it except through the Oral Torah,
וַ"אֲרֻכָּה מֵאֶרֶץ מִדָּהּ", דְּהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אֵין לָהּ קֵץ,
and “its measure is longer than the earth,” for the Oral Torah has no end,
וּבְכָל יוֹם אֶפְשָׁר לְתַלְמִיד וָתִיק לְחַדֵּשׁ חֲדָשׁוֹת,
and on each day it is possible for a devoted scholar to innovate fresh insights,
וּכְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ לְטַהֵר הַשֶּׁרֶץ,
such as that student who knew how to declare the creeping creature ritually pure,
וְאֵין זֶה פִּלְפּוּל שֶׁל הֶבֶל כְּקֻשְׁיַת הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (עֵירוּבִין י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳);
and this is not empty sophistry, as the objection of Tosafot might suggest (Eruvin 13b);
דַּהֲרֵי בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב מִזְמוֹר קמ״ו): "ה' מַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים" — דֶּעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַתִּיר אִסּוּרִים.

for our Sages of blessed memory truly stated (Shocher Tov, Psalm 146): “Hashem frees the bound (matir asurim)”—meaning that in the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will permit that which was forbidden.
וְחַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה תִּשְׁתַּנֶּה כִּי הִיא נִצְחִית;
And God forbid that the Torah itself should change, for it is eternal;
רַק כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ג): "חִדּוּשׁ תּוֹרָה מֵאִתִּי תֵצֵא",
it is only as the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 13:3): “A new dimension of Torah shall proceed from Me,”
שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה אֵיזֶה חִדּוּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה לְהַתִּיר דְּבָרִים שֶׁהָיָה אָסוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
meaning that a novel insight within the Torah will be revealed to permit things that were forbidden in this world,
וְאָז כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הַחִדּוּשׁ יַכִּירוּ הַכֹּל וְיֵדְעוּ שֶׁגַּם זֶה עַצְמוֹ מִכְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה וְאֵינוֹ חִדּוּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה.
and when that revelation occurs, all will perceive and realize that this too was always part of the Torah and is not an arbitrary innovation contrary to it.
וַהֲרֵי כַּמָּה דְּבָרִים חִדְּשׁוּ סוֹפְרִים לַעֲקוֹר דְּבַר תּוֹרָה,
Indeed, the Scribes instituted several measures that suspend a Torah commandment,
כְּשׁוֹפָר וְלוּלָב שֶׁאֵין דּוֹחֶה שַׁבָּת,
such as the shofar and lulav not overriding Shabbat,
וּכְהֶתֵּר כְּתִיבַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְכַדּוֹמֶה, וְזֶה חִדּוּשׁ מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים.
and the permission to record the Oral Torah in writing and the like, which are enactments stemming from the Scribes.
וְיֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן חִדּוּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה עַצְמָהּ,
And there is likewise profound innovation within the words of the Torah itself,
וְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק הָיָה מַשִּׂיג אֵיזֶה הַשָּׂגָה אֵיךְ לְטַהֵר שֶׁרֶץ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד,
and that veteran disciple had attained an apprehension of how the creeping creature will be declared pure in the future,
